background.heading: Entity identification
background.text: UK entity is Abbott Diabetes Care Limited (Companies House 02548046, Witney), formerly MediSense (U.K.) Holding Ltd, renamed 2005 following Abbott's 2004 acquisition of TheraSense/MediSense. Not found on NHS Supply Chain (searched Libre, FreeStyle Libre, Abbott Diabetes — zero results) — confirms FreeStyle Libre is dispensed via NHS prescription (Drug Tariff), not the hospital consumables catalogue. Compatible with third-party closed-loop systems (mylife CamAPS FX/YpsoPump) per Abbott's own technical documentation.

suppliers._specialitiesEvidence: 20/07/2026: added Blood and transfusion for Alinity s-series (donor blood/plasma screening -- HBsAg, anti-HCV, anti-HBc, HTLV I/II, Chagas) -- already bundled into the 'Alinity ci / h / s / m' product line but had no matching speciality tag; this family genuinely sits apart from general pathology, likely procured directly by NHS Blood and Transplant rather than the general NHS Supply Chain catalogue. Added BinaxNOW/Determine/Actim/SureStep -- the former Alere rapid-diagnostics range (Abbott acquired Alere Oct 2017), confirmed live on NHS Supply Chain under a distinct legal entity 'ABBOTT RAPID DIAGNOSTICS LTD' (separate from 'ABBOTT LABORATORIES LIMITED (BERKS)', which covers i-STAT/ARCHITECT/Alinity) -- kept as one combined 'Abbott Diagnostics' record since both are diagnostics-not-diabetes, even though NHS Supply Chain itself treats them as two legal suppliers. CONFIRMED clean separation from Abbott Diabetes Care: FreeStyle Libre is supplied via the NHS Drug Tariff (Part IXR)/community prescribing, an entirely different UK procurement route from the hospital Supply Chain catalogue used by this record -- no overlap or double-counting risk between the two supplier records. ARCHITECT is being gradually migrated to Alinity ci (both still live on NHS Supply Chain today) -- described as a managed transition, not a discontinuation, don't flag ARCHITECT as withdrawn.

background.heading: Product attribution correction
background.text: Removed 'SureStep' — this appears to be a LifeScan brand (originally Johnson & Johnson, now Platinum Equity-owned), not an Abbott product; no evidence found that Abbott ever marketed it. Current NHS point-of-care glucose testing under Abbott runs via FreeStyle Precision Pro/i-STAT instead. Diagnostics products span two UK entities: Abbott Laboratories Limited (00329102, Maidenhead, trades as 'Abbott Diagnostics' — Alinity/Architect/i-STAT) and Abbott Rapid Diagnostics Ltd (01716581, also Maidenhead — Afinion/ID NOW/Determine/Actim distribution). Both confirmed distinct from Abbott Medical U.K. Ltd (cardiac/EP) and Abbott Diabetes Care Ltd (FreeStyle Libre), already recorded separately in this dataset.

alerts.text: Physidia (home dialysis machine) is manufactured by a French company, Physidia — B. Braun Avitum is its exclusive UK distributor, not the manufacturer; worth noting the distinction. UK entity B. Braun Medical Limited (Companies House 02296559, Sheffield) confirmed family-controlled at UK level; ultimate parent B. Braun Melsungen AG (Germany) remains privately held and family-controlled (CEO Anna Maria Braun, 6th generation), no public listing. B. Braun SE fully acquired True Digital Surgery (Sept 2025, digital 3D robotic surgical microscopy), feeding directly into the already-listed Aesculap Aeos platform. US FDA recalls in 2025-2026 (Lactated Ringer's/Sodium Chloride particulate matter, Microbore Extension Set mislabelling) are US-market actions — no equivalent UK/MHRA recall was found, so these should not be presented as a UK-market issue without separate confirmation.

deepDive.tagline: Family-controlled since 1839, still unlisted · CEO Anna Maria Braun, sixth generation · UK entity B. Braun Medical Limited, Sheffield, incorporated 1988 as Aesculap Limited
deepDive.lede: The thing worth knowing before this interview: B. Braun is the biggest supplier on this Hub's framework data and it is privately held by one family, which changes how it behaves. Group sales reached €9.4bn in 2025, growth of 5.1% at constant currency, right inside the 5 to 7 percent corridor the company sets itself, and it put more than €800m back into plant and technology in the same year, including a €145m automated infusion consumables factory at Melsungen. There are no quarterly analysts to satisfy, which is why you hear "long-term" from them and mean it. The UK board is also in the middle of a turnover: Michael Parden, the Sheffield-born UK Managing Director appointed in 2021, resigned as a director on 21 April 2026, Christiane Jandt was appointed the same day, and Simon Topliss was appointed on 3 August 2026, eleven days ago. Ask what the UK leadership is being asked to do differently.

prose: B. Braun publishes a clean five-year sales series, which most of this market does not: €7,859.8m (2021), €8,499.8m (2022), €8,755.0m (2023), €9,136.9m (2024), €9,396.4m (2025). That is steady rather than spectacular, and the company frames it against a self-set corridor of 5 to 7 percent currency-adjusted growth, which it hit in 2025 at 5.1 percent. The 2.8 percent figure quoted in some coverage is the same year measured in group currency, before the currency adjustment; both are B. Braun's own numbers and they are not in conflict.

The 2025 sales split by division was Hospital Care €5,091m, Aesculap €2,374m and Avitum €1,901m, so infusion, nutrition and pain therapy is more than half the business, surgical is a quarter and dialysis and chronic care the rest. By region, Western Europe was €2,021m against North America's €2,397m and Germany's €1,441m. There is no UK-only sales line in the group report, and B. Braun Medical Limited files full accounts at Companies House as a PDF with no tagged profit and loss account, so no UK turnover figure is stated here rather than estimated.

Profitability moved more than sales did. EBITDA margin went from 11.9 to 13.0 percent and gross margin from 39.1 to 40.5 percent, which the company attributes to portfolio management, cost control and plant efficiency. The 2026 guidance is 5 to 7 percent currency-adjusted sales growth, EBITDA margin above 13 percent and return on sales above 5 percent.

ownership: B. Braun has never been sold and has never listed. It was founded in Melsungen, Germany in 1839 and remains controlled by the Braun family; Anna Maria Braun, the sixth generation, has been group CEO since 2019. The group holding is B. Braun SE. That matters commercially: there is no quarterly earnings cycle, no activist shareholder and no separation story of the kind running at several of its listed competitors, and the company's own language, a 5 to 7 percent corridor held over years rather than a growth target for next quarter, follows from that.

The UK operating entity is B. Braun Medical Limited, company number 02296559, incorporated 14 September 1988 and confirmed active at Companies House. It was originally WF 156 Limited, then Aesculap-Skidmore Holdings Limited from February 1989, Aesculap Limited from January 1991, and took the B. Braun Medical name in May 1998, which is why the Aesculap surgical brand and the B. Braun infusion brand sit inside the same UK company. Registered office is Brookdale Road, Thorncliffe Park Estate, Chapeltown, Sheffield S35 2PW. A second UK company, B Braun Sterilog Limited (01472814, incorporated 1980), also exists on the register; this repo records that match as probable rather than confirmed, because no B. Braun-published source read here names it.

press.text: Simon Paul Topliss appointed a director of B. Braun Medical Limited. The fourth change to the UK board inside 28 months, following Craig Cannings (May 2024), Christiane Jandt and Michael Parden's resignation (both 21 April 2026). If you are interviewing into the UK business, the board that hires you is not the board that set this year's plan.

Group sales €9,396m, up 5.1% at constant currency and 2.8% in group currency, with all three divisions and all six business regions growing. EBITDA margin 13.0%, return on sales before tax 4.9%. Guidance for 2026 is 5 to 7 percent currency-adjusted growth, EBITDA margin above 13 percent, return on sales above 5 percent.

B. Braun fully acquired US microsurgery specialist True Digital Surgery, extending the portfolio for robotically assisted 3D microscopy in neurosurgery, spine and ENT. Relevant if the role is anywhere near Aesculap Aeos or digital surgery.

The €145m automated ACTIVE plant for single-use infusion therapy consumables opened at Melsungen, using driverless transport, robotics and intelligent warehousing. Supply resilience is a live NHS procurement question and this is the concrete answer to it.

Foundation laid at Tuttlingen for the Technology Factory, a long-term rebuild of surgical instrument pre-production designed for carbon-neutral operation using geothermal, process waste heat and photovoltaics. Useful if the trust you are selling into has a net-zero supplier requirement.
OMNI plus launched, bringing acute dialysis and apheresis together on one platform for acute kidney failure. Avitum's headline launch of the year.

Health care centre portfolio expanded by acquisition in Romania and Czechia, increasing group dialysis capacity. B. Braun both sells dialysis equipment and runs dialysis clinics, which is unusual and worth understanding before an Avitum interview.

hiring: No rolling count of UK vacancies could be read from a B. Braun-published source in this run, so none is given here rather than estimated. What is checkable on Glassdoor, read 14/08/2026: one live UK listing, a Medical Device Product Specialist (Sales) role covering Central England, and the UK entity is sized at 1,001 to 5,000 employees with a single office location on that profile. Sheffield is both the registered office and, on the company's own Glassdoor photographs, the head office site, so the UK business is a single-site commercial and manufacturing operation rather than a distributed one.

glassdoor.scale: /5 on Glassdoor UK, B. Braun Medical (UK) specifically, not the group (90 ratings)
glassdoor.summary: Unusually, there is a UK-only profile here rather than just a global one, so this is the right number to use. 4.0 is above the 3.4 manufacturing-industry average and above the UK-entity ratings of several direct competitors. 73% would recommend to a friend. Category scores: culture and values 3.8, work/life balance 3.8, diversity and inclusion 3.7, compensation and benefits 3.6, career opportunities 3.5, senior management 3.4. The soft measures beat the hard ones, which fits the family-owned, long-tenure picture, and business outlook is the weak spot at 57% positive. On interviews, 80% of candidates rate the experience positive and average difficulty is 2.6 out of 5.

deepDive.interview: Know which division the role sits in and say the word: Hospital Care (infusion, nutrition, pain), Aesculap (surgical) or Avitum (dialysis, wound, stoma, continence). They are run separately from the executive board down and a candidate who talks about "B. Braun's portfolio" as one thing sounds like they read the website once. Lead on family ownership as a commercial argument, not a nice fact: no listing, no quarterly cycle, a self-set 5 to 7 percent corridor held for years, and more than €800m of capital investment in 2025 including a €145m automated plant. That is a supply-continuity story, and continuity of supply is what NHS procurement has actually been buying since 2022. Be ready on the UK board changes, three director appointments and one resignation since May 2024, with the most recent on 3 August 2026. On the Avitum side, understand that B. Braun runs dialysis clinics as well as selling dialysis machines, so it is a competitor to some of its own customers in that segment. And do not describe Physidia as a B. Braun product: B. Braun Avitum is the UK distributor, not the manufacturer.

deepDive.tagline: Thetford-based UK arm of Baxter International, selling IV fluids and infusion systems, parenteral nutrition, inhaled anaesthetics, injectable pharmaceuticals and surgical haemostats into the NHS - and, since 2024, no longer selling renal.
deepDive.lede: The single most important thing to know before you walk into Baxter is that the UK company you are meeting is materially smaller than it was two years ago, and it is smaller on purpose. The 2024 accounts split the year into continuing and discontinued operations: total turnover fell from £723.7m in 2023 to £662.5m in 2024, but continuing turnover ROSE from £569.4m to £618.3m. The gap is the Kidney Care business, which contributed £154.3m of turnover in 2023 and only £44.3m in 2024, and on which the company booked a £19.7m exceptional gain on transfer. Headcount fell with it, from 1,644 to 1,507 on the average monthly count. Anyone who walks in talking about Baxter's renal portfolio is describing a business that has gone.

prose: Read this company's two years side by side or you will draw the wrong conclusion. Total turnover was £723,684,000 for the year to 31 December 2023 and £662,513,000 for 2024 - down £61.2m, about 8.5%. But the accounts present the year split between continuing and discontinued operations, and on continuing operations turnover went the other way: £569,375,000 in 2023 to £618,253,000 in 2024, up £48.9m or 8.6%. The discontinued line is Kidney Care, which fell from £154,309,000 to £44,260,000.

Profit follows the same shape. Operating profit before exceptional items was £46,078,000 in 2023 and £39,545,000 in 2024; on continuing operations alone it was £38,982,000 then £36,242,000. Reported operating profit for 2024 is £59,294,000 because of a £19,749,000 exceptional gain on transfer of the Kidney Care business. Profit before taxation was £58,222,000 (2023: £49,225,000) and profit for the financial year £46,261,000 (2023: £37,592,000).

The financing lines are worth a glance because they moved sharply. Interest receivable rose from £6,983,000 to £9,908,000, of which £8,753,000 was interest on loans to group undertakings; interest payable rose from £3,836,000 to £10,980,000, of which £12,190,000 was interest on loans FROM group undertakings. Net interest went from £3,147,000 income in 2023 to £1,071,000 expense in 2024. The accounts record intercompany receivable rates of 3.58% and 2.256% in the year (2023: 5.604% and 4.038%).

Two post-balance-sheet events are recorded and both matter commercially. On 31 January 2025 Baxter International Inc. completed the sale of Vantive to Carlyle. On 12 June 2025 the company distributed an intercompany loan receivable of £165,189,000 to its shareholder as a dividend. Nothing here comes from anywhere but the company's own filed accounts, and no group turnover is quoted, because Baxter International Inc. is a US registrant whose figures are not read in this record.

ownership: BAXTER HEALTHCARE LIMITED, company number 00461365, registered office Caxton Way, Thetford, Norfolk, IP24 3SE, is an active private limited company incorporated on 18 November 1948, SIC 21100, manufacture of basic pharmaceutical products. It was named TRAVENOL LABORATORIES LIMITED from incorporation until 1 February 1988.

Note 28 of the accounts for the year ended 31 December 2024 states the chain in the company's own words: Baxter Healthcare Limited is 100% owned by Baxter Healthcare Holding Limited, a company incorporated in Malta, which in turn is ultimately owned and controlled by Baxter International Inc., One Baxter Parkway, Deerfield, Illinois 60015, USA. Baxter International Inc. is named as both the smallest and the largest group preparing group financial statements.

The company describes itself in note 1 as providing sterile intravenous solutions, infusion systems and devices, parenteral nutrition therapies, inhaled anaesthetics, generic injectable pharmaceuticals and surgical haemostat and sealant products, and records that it operates a branch in Ireland at Block 2, Deansgrange Industrial Estate, Blackrock, Co. Dublin. That description no longer includes renal, and the accounts explain why: Kidney Care is presented as a discontinued operation, and the group completed the sale of Vantive to Carlyle on 31 January 2025.

On that test there are five, all captured from those briefs on 31/08/2026 - Extension Sets and Lines (1 August 2023 to 31 July 2027, 23 suppliers), Infusion Pumps and Administration Sets and Associated Products (3 October 2022 to 30 September 2026, 27 suppliers), Total Orthopaedic Solutions 3 (1 February 2024 to 30 January 2028, 106 suppliers), Urology and Bowel Management (21 February 2024 to 20 February 2027, 57 suppliers) and Wound Closure (19 January 2026 to 18 January 2030, 39 suppliers).

One of those five expires within weeks of this record being written. Infusion Pumps and Administration Sets and Associated Products runs to 30 September 2026. deepDive.interview: Go in knowing the portfolio has changed shape, because that is what separates a candidate who has read the filing from one who has read the website. Kidney Care is a discontinued operation in the 2024 accounts, falling from £154.3m of turnover to £44.3m, and the group completed the sale of Vantive to Carlyle on 31 January 2025. Talking about Baxter's renal business as though it were still there would date you. The right framing is the opposite one: on continuing operations turnover grew from £569.4m to £618.3m, up 8.6%, so this is a business that got smaller and better at the same time. Ask what the continuing portfolio is being asked to do now that renal has gone, and you are having the conversation the leadership team is actually having. The second question is about coverage and it is a fair one, not a hostile one. Sales and marketing headcount fell from 175 to 127 across 2024 - a 27% reduction - while continuing turnover rose 8.6%. Asking how territories were redrawn to carry that, and what it did to trust-level relationships, shows you understand that a national framework position and actual adoption in a trust are two different things. Have one date ready: NHS Supply Chain's Infusion Pumps and Administration Sets and Associated Products framework runs out on 30 September 2026. For a company that leads on infusion, knowing when its core framework expires is the sort of specific that gets remembered.

news.text: 9 Feb 2026: BD completed the spin-off of its Biosciences and Diagnostic Solutions business and its combination with Waters Corporation. The business was valued at $18.8bn on Waters' 6 February closing price and BD received $4bn in cash; BD shareholders ended up holding 39.2% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis. Flow cytometry, single-cell multiomics, microbiology, molecular diagnostics and point-of-care testing now trade as Waters Biosciences and Waters Advanced Diagnostics. Specimen management, including Vacutainer, was retained and sits in BD's Medical Essentials segment.

6 Aug 2026: Q3 FY2026 revenue $5.0bn, up 5.4% as reported and 4.4% currency-neutral; adjusted diluted EPS $3.23; full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised to $12.62 to $12.72. The first full quarter reported as the four-segment company, with all four segments growing.

31 Jul 2026: BD issued a US nationwide recall of specific lots of the BD Intraosseous Vascular Access System Needle Sets after reports of difficulty removing the obturator; the FDA classified it Class I. Affected lots were distributed 30/09/2024 to 12/06/2026. The BD Intraosseous Powered Driver is not affected. No corresponding UK field safety notice appears in this Hub's gov.uk and NHS Supply Chain alert feed as at 15/08/2026, so UK stock impact is Not verified — check the MHRA alerts page before raising it with a trust.

NHS Supply Chain framework status per product still to confirm — many lines are sold DIRECT / off-framework (Rowa, EnCor, Pyxis/Alaris capital). Diabetes needles excluded (Embecta spin-off 2022). deepDive.lede: The thing worth knowing before this interview: BD is not the company most reps still describe. On 9 February 2026 it completed the spin-off of its Biosciences and Diagnostic Solutions business into Waters Corporation, in a Reverse Morris Trust that valued the business at $18.8bn and handed BD $4bn in cash. Flow cytometry, microbiology, molecular and point-of-care diagnostics went with it and now trade as Waters Biosciences and Waters Advanced Diagnostics. What is left, which BD calls New BD, is four segments — Medical Essentials, Connected Care, BioPharma Systems and Interventional — and the company describes itself as one of the world's largest pure-play medtech businesses. It is trading well on that narrower base: revenue of $4,983m in the quarter to 30 June 2026, up 5.4%, with full-year guidance raised on 6 August 2026. Walk in talking about BD's diagnostics portfolio and you will be a year out of date.

prose: No UK-only turnover can be read for this company. Becton, Dickinson U.K. Limited files full accounts at Companies House, but as a PDF with no tagged figures, so identifying the turnover line by position would be a guess rather than a reading, and nothing is taken from it. Its last accounts were made up to 30 September 2025; the next are due by 30 June 2027, and its most recent confirmation statement is dated 14 August 2026. Everything below is therefore group-wide, as reported by BD in its own filings.

Group revenue was $20,178m in FY2024 and $21,840m in FY2025, both years ended 30 September and both as reported before the separation. That basis stops there. After the Waters deal BD restated FY2025 to $18,544m on a continuing-operations basis, and reports the nine months to 30 June 2026 at $14,183m against $13,539m, up 4.8%. Full-year FY2026 guidance, raised on 6 August 2026, is low single-digit revenue growth and adjusted diluted EPS of $12.62 to $12.72.

The number worth asking about is the cost of getting there. The nine months to 30 June 2026 carry $605m of restructuring charges, including $450m of non-cash impairments booked when BD committed to exit activities and projects that no longer fit its Excellence Unleashed strategy. A company simplifying that hard is one where it is fair to ask what the UK commercial structure looks like on the other side.

ownership: BD (Becton, Dickinson and Company) is a US public company listed on the New York Stock Exchange as BDX, headquartered at 1 Becton Drive, Franklin Lakes, New Jersey. There is no parent above it. Tom Polen is chairman, chief executive and president, and signed both the February 2026 separation release and the August 2026 results release in that capacity.

The group has been deliberately reshaped rather than grown whole: BD's own account of the last several years is three substantial non-core divestments and more than twenty tuck-in acquisitions, ending with the Biosciences and Diagnostic Solutions separation on 9 February 2026, which it calls the final milestone of its BD 2025 strategy. The structure was a Reverse Morris Trust: the business was spun into a separate entity that merged with a Waters subsidiary, BD shareholders received about 0.135 Waters shares per BD share and ended up with 39.2% of the combined company, and BD took $4bn in cash, earmarking $2bn for an accelerated share repurchase and $2bn for debt repayment.

The UK operating entity is Becton, Dickinson U.K. Limited, company number 00852702, incorporated 25 June 1965 and active, registered office 1030 Eskdale Road, Winnersh Triangle, Wokingham, Berkshire RG41 5TS, SIC 32500, manufacture of medical and dental instruments and supplies. BD also runs a manufacturing site at Plymouth, which appears in its own careers listings.

press.text: FY2025 results: revenue $21.8bn, up 8.2% as reported and 2.9% organic; adjusted diluted EPS $14.40, up 9.6%. BD states the Waters combination is on track to complete around the end of the first quarter of calendar 2026.

The spin-off of Biosciences and Diagnostic Solutions completes and the business combines with Waters Corporation. BD receives $4bn cash, its shareholders take 39.2% of Waters, and the business is valued at $18.8bn on the previous day's Waters closing price. BD calls itself a pure-play medtech company from this point.

Waters names its new divisions the same day: Waters Biosciences is the former BD Biosciences (flow cytometry, single-cell multiomics) and Waters Advanced Diagnostics is the former BD Diagnostic Solutions plus the Waters clinical business (microbiology, molecular, multiplex, automation, point of care). Anything in those categories is no longer a BD conversation.

MHRA Class 2 medicines recall EL(26)A/34 for ChloraPrep 1mL applicators, a potential sterility breach across all lots with expiry to 05/2029. The fourth ChloraPrep recall since May 2025 and the most live UK-facing issue on this account. Full detail and links are in this supplier's alerts.
The Venflon IV cannula with wings, 14G to 22G, completes its NHS Supply Chain delisting, having been progressively withdrawn since January 2025. Any trust still using it has had to convert.

Q3 FY2026 results: revenue $4,983m, up 5.4%, described by BD as its first full quarter as New BD. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised to $12.62 to $12.72. Highlights named a Vizient Innovative Technology contract for the BD CentroVena One insertion system, the launch of the Elyra thulium fibre laser system in kidney stone care, and a collaboration with Brazilian pharmaceutical company EMS on the Vystra injection pen for semaglutide.

hiring: BD runs its own careers site at jobs.bd.com, which carries UK listings including manufacturing, engineering, field service and sales roles at the Plymouth site. No vacancy count, salary band or UK headcount was verified in this session, so none is stated here.
marketPosition: BD describes itself as one of the world's largest pure-play medical technology companies, with more than 60,000 employees. That is the company's own claim, not an audited market share, and no verified market-share figure was found in this session, so none is given. The strongest UK-specific evidence of scale is procurement footprint: named supplier on 18 separate NHS Supply Chain frameworks, spanning IV cannulation and vascular access, infusion pumps and administration sets, needle-free connectors, extension sets, blood collection, specimen management, surgical mesh, urology and endoscopy consumables, renal replacement, skin cleansing and pathology services, all confirmed against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs.

⚠️ Read this supplier's product list with the separation in mind. The Hub's captured range for BD still includes flow cytometry (FACSLyric, FACSAria, FACSymphony, LSRFortessa), BACTEC, BD MAX, Kiestra, Phoenix and Veritor, all of which transferred to Waters on 09/02/2026. Whether individual UK supply contracts and NHS Supply Chain framework places for those lines have novated to a Waters entity is Not verified: it would be settled by the framework's own supplier list at the next refresh, or by NHS Supply Chain's catalogue. Until that is checked, do not tell a customer BD supplies them.
deepDive.interview: This is a company that has just made itself smaller on purpose, so the interesting questions are about focus rather than growth. Know which of the four segments the role sits in — Medical Essentials, Connected Care, BioPharma Systems or Interventional — because they are separately managed and the diagnostics conversation has left the building. On UK ground, the two live issues are the ChloraPrep recall sequence, four since May 2025, and the Venflon delisting that completed on 31 July 2026: both are switching conversations happening in trusts right now, and being able to talk about continuity of licensed supply is worth more than product knowledge. The $605m of restructuring in the first nine months of FY2026 is a fair, non-hostile thing to raise as a question about what Excellence Unleashed means for the UK team.

alerts.text: IMPORTANT SAFETY FLAG: the ACCOLADE pacemaker/CRT-P family (Accolade, Proponent, Essentio, Altura 2, Visionist, Valitude) is subject to an FDA Class I recall/correction affecting over 1 million devices — a high battery-impedance issue causing an unexpected 'Safety Mode'; as of 18 March 2026 Boston Scientific reported 4 deaths and 2,557 serious injuries. The fix is a software update (SMR6, released March 2026), not device explant — worth surfacing to any rep positioning this pacemaker family. Separately, the Carotid Wallstent Monorail Endoprosthesis was recalled in 2025 for a manufacturing defect (narrow inner lumen risking stroke). UK entity: Boston Scientific Limited (Companies House 02729626, London) — a differently-numbered 'Boston Scientific (UK) Limited' (04949633) is dissolved since Oct 2023, don't use it. Boston Scientific has an active pending $14.5bn acquisition of Penumbra, Inc. (mechanical thrombectomy) announced 2026 but not yet closed — don't add Penumbra products until completion is confirmed. Other recent acquisitions (Cortex cardiac mapping, Bolt Medical, Nalu Medical, SoundCath, Intera Oncology) are agreed/closing through 2025-2026 but not yet reflected as flagship UK-commercial products.

deepDive.tagline: US-parented cardiology, endoscopy and neuromodulation major, on 7 confirmed NHS Supply Chain frameworks -- wholly owned by Boston Scientific Corporation (Delaware) through a UK subsidiary with a single active UK-registered director
deepDive.lede: Boston Scientific Limited is the UK trading entity of a $5bn-a-quarter US medtech group, and its own Companies House record is a reminder that a subsidiary this size can still run on a very small UK board: one active director, Emily Marie Woodworth, appointed 16 August 2024 alongside a corporate nominee secretary, and no other UK-resident officer on the register. Its parent, Boston Scientific Corporation of Delaware, has held 75% or more of the shares and the right to appoint or remove directors since notification on 6 April 2016. Seven NHS Supply Chain frameworks are confirmed against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs, spanning cardiology, neuromodulation, endoscopy, theatre equipment, radiotherapy, surgical mesh and men's and women's health implants. The group itself is mid-acquisition: a $14.5bn deal to buy Penumbra, Inc., announced 15 January 2026, was still awaiting regulatory clearance as of 29 July 2026 and is not reflected in any UK-commercial product list here until it closes.

stats.n: named supplier, confirmed against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs, captured into this supplier's frameworks array 17/08/2026: Airway Management Products, Endoscopy/Endourology/Oncology Ablation Consumables, Neuromodulation Devices, Operating Theatres Equipment, Radiotherapy Treatment Systems, Surgical Implants for Men's and Women's Health, and Surgical Mesh. A further named entry in this supplier's own frameworks array ("Interventional Cardiology / IR / Neuro / CRM / EP") is a general reference rather than a single confirmed brief and is not counted in the 7.

£307,982,000, against £285,301,000 in the year to 31 December 2023, an increase of 7.9%. Read from the Statement of Comprehensive Income and notes 3, 4 and 5 of Boston Scientific Limited's full accounts for the year ended 31 December 2024, filed at Companies House on 17/11/2025 and read on 20/08/2026. Cost of sales was £241,495,000 and gross profit £66,487,000, a gross margin of 21.6% against 21.3%. The filing is a scanned PDF with no iXBRL tagging and no text layer, which is why this Hub's automated accounts extractor holds no turnover for this company; the figure here was read from the line the company itself labelled Turnover, not taken by position.

average monthly number of employees, from note 5 of the Statement of Comprehensive Income and notes 3, 4 and 5 of Boston Scientific Limited's full accounts for the year ended 31 December 2024, filed at Companies House on 17/11/2025 and read on 20/08/2026: 360 selling and distribution and 105 administration, against 443 in 2023 split 308 and 135. Staff costs were £50,542,000 (wages and salaries £41,715,000, social security £5,992,000, pensions £2,835,000). The selling and distribution line grew by 52 people while administration fell by 30.

Emily Marie Woodworth, appointed director and secretary on 16 August 2024, correspondence address in Marlborough, Massachusetts. Two dated resignations fall on the same day: Jonathan Richard Monson and Vance Ronald Brown both resigned as directors on 16 August 2024. No succession is asserted, because succession is not a register fact and the register does not record who took over what. Abogado Nominees Limited (UK company 1688036) sits alongside her as nominee secretary. No UK-resident officer is on the current register. Note 4 of the FY2024 accounts adds that no director received any remuneration during the year (2023: nil), the directors' services to this company being minimal compared with their service to the rest of the group and recorded in other group companies.

£8,890,000 against £6,706,000, from the Statement of Comprehensive Income in the same filing. Operating profit was £8,702,000 against £8,837,000 before impairment; the prior year's stated operating profit of £6,854,000 is after a £1,983,000 write-off of investments in subsidiaries that did not recur. Group-level, Boston Scientific reported net sales of $5.2bn for Q1 2026 (+11.6%), with the company's own release citing continued UK/European roll-out of the FARAPULSE pulsed-field ablation system for atrial fibrillation -- already on this supplier's record. The pending $14.5bn acquisition of Penumbra, Inc. (mechanical thrombectomy), agreed 15 January 2026, was still awaiting the remaining regulatory clearances as of 29 July 2026 and Boston Scientific's own guidance continued to point to a close in the second half of 2026; nothing from Penumbra's range should be added to this supplier's UK product list until that closes and is separately confirmed.

deepDive.interview: Two things are worth knowing before this one. First, the UK company you would be joining is a thin legal shell around a large commercial operation: one active Companies House director, based in Massachusetts, appointed the same day her two predecessors resigned in August 2024, and a UK nominee secretary alongside her -- nobody UK-resident on the statutory register at all. That is normal for a US-parented subsidiary of this size and is not itself a red flag, but it means governance questions get answered in Marlborough, not Hemel Hempstead, and it is worth asking who actually signs off UK commercial decisions day to day. Second, ask where the business is mid-change: the Penumbra acquisition, agreed in January 2026 at $14.5bn, was still not closed as of the company's own late-July 2026 guidance, so anyone joining now is joining before that integration starts, not after it. On the framework side, seven confirmed NHS Supply Chain lines spanning cardiology, neuromodulation, endoscopy and theatre equipment is a genuinely broad NHS footprint for one supplier, and FARAPULSE's continuing UK roll-out (flagged in this record's existing alert) is the live growth story to ask about in an EP or structural heart interview specifically.

deepDive.tagline: The UK entity of Cardinal Health, Inc. - a 34-person specialist distributor of diagnostic and interventional cardiology and endovascular products, on £22.7m of turnover, registered care-of TMF Group in the City rather than at an operating site.
deepDive.lede: Do not let the parent's name set your expectations. Whatever Cardinal Health, Inc. is worldwide - and no figure for it is quoted here, because none was read in this session - the UK company on the register, Cardinal Health U.K. 432 Limited, turned over £22,667,112 in the year to 30 June 2025 and employed 34 people on average - 20 in sales, 13 in new product development, one in administration. Its own strategic report describes it as a healthcare service provider specialising in the distribution of diagnostic and interventional cardiology and endovascular solutions, and attributes the year's 2.4% revenue increase mainly to higher demand for some products, including surgical gloves. That is a narrow, specialist business, and it is registered care-of TMF Group at One Angel Court in the City - not at a warehouse.

prose: Turnover, read from the face of the statement of comprehensive income in each filed set: £20,908,870 for the year to 30 June 2023, £22,143,138 for 2024 and £22,667,112 for 2025. That is 5.9% then 2.4% - and the 2.4% is the company's own figure, given in the strategic report and attributed mainly to increased demand for some products, including surgical gloves.

The profit line has flattened. Operating profit was £732,940 for 2023, £1,095,359 for 2024 and £969,097 for 2025. Gross profit was £5,484,237, then £6,626,352, then £6,626,593 - essentially identical in the last two years despite £524,000 more revenue, so the whole of the 2025 revenue increase came through at close to nil incremental gross margin. Administrative expenses rose from £5,530,993 to £5,657,496, up 2.3%, which the directors attribute to increased travel-related costs.

Profit before taxation was £743,710, then £1,233,533, then £1,184,582. The 2025 figure holds up better than the operating result because interest receivable rose from £143,914 to £223,117. Profit for the financial year was £620,241, £926,812 and £858,615.

Two balance sheet facts are worth carrying into a conversation. Cash fell from £5,734,860 to £4,916,713 across the year, and the company was in net current liabilities of £159,378 at 30 June 2025 - much improved on the £1,329,600 a year earlier, but still negative. The directors state that preparing the accounts on a going concern basis is appropriate because of ongoing profitability and the continued financial support of the ultimate parent company. Note also that the equity history includes a £5,478,166 dividend paid in the year to 30 June 2024. No group turnover is quoted here: Cardinal Health, Inc. is a US registrant and its figures are not read in this record.

ownership: Cardinal Health U.K. 432 Limited, company number 01278801, registered office C/O TMF Group, 13th Floor, One Angel Court, London EC2R 7HJ, is an active private limited company incorporated on 24 September 1976, SIC 46180, agents specialised in the sale of other particular products. The registered office is a corporate services address, not an operating site.

The company has a long name history that matters when you are matching records: PENNINE OPTICAL PLC from incorporation, THE INTERCARE GROUP PLC from 15 November 1989, THE INTERCARE GROUP LIMITED from 2 March 2004, and its present name from 14 March 2005. Anyone searching Companies House for the Intercare Group will land here.

Note 21 of the accounts for the year ended 30 June 2025 states the chain in the company's own words: the immediate parent undertaking and controlling party is Cardinal Health Netherlands 502 B.V., a company incorporated under the laws of the Netherlands, and the company is a subsidiary undertaking of Cardinal Health, Inc. The directors also record, in the going concern statement, that they rely on the continued financial support of the ultimate parent company.

The filing shows a company that added two people across the year to 30 June 2025 - 32 to 34 on the average monthly count, with sales up from 19 to 20 and new product development from 12 to 13. marketPosition: The measurable part of this company's NHS position is its framework footprint, and the rule used here is narrow: a framework counts only where NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch brief names this supplier. On that test there are seven, all captured on 31/08/2026 - Clinical and Sharps Waste Management (1 November 2023 to 23 October 2027, 14 suppliers), Electrodes, Ultrasound Gels, Defibrillation and Related Consumables (1 February 2024 to 31 January 2028, 37), Enteral Feeding, Bile Bags and Associated Products (5 September 2025 to 13 July 2027, 19), Surgical Gloves (27 November 2023 to 25 April 2027, 12), Syringes, Needles and Associated Products (1 July 2026 to 30 June 2029, 53), Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions (4 August 2026 to 3 August 2028, 40) and Vascular Therapy and Associated Products (28 February 2024 to 27 February 2028, 23).

There is a real tension in that list worth understanding before an interview. The company's own strategic report describes its principal activity as the distribution of diagnostic and interventional cardiology and endovascular solutions - a specialist, clinician-facing sale. But the framework footprint is dominated by commodity consumables: gloves, syringes and needles, sharps waste, electrodes. And the directors' own explanation of the 2025 revenue increase names surgical gloves. The narrowest field it sits in is Surgical Gloves, with only 12 named suppliers, and that framework expires on 25 April 2027.

Two of the seven started within the last two months of this record being written - Syringes, Needles and Associated Products on 1 July 2026 and Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions on 4 August 2026 - which means live implementation work across trusts right now, being carried by a 34-person company with 20 people in sales.

This supplier's own product range has not been crawled into the Hub's product layer, so no product count is given and none is inferred. No market share is stated and none is calculable from anything read in this session; the only competitive figures here are NHS Supply Chain's own supplier counts on each framework.

deepDive.interview: Get the scale right in your own head first, because most candidates do not. Whatever the parent group is worldwide, Cardinal Health U.K. 432 Limited is a £22.7m, 34-person specialist business whose registered office is care of TMF Group in the City. Walking in and talking about the parent's scale would tell them you have not read anything about the entity actually hiring you. The most interesting thing in the filing is the shape of that 34: 20 in sales, 13 in new product development, one in administration. Thirty-eight per cent of a distributor's payroll sitting in NPD is not a normal ratio, and asking what that team does - whether it is technical product introduction, regulatory work, or building the cardiology and endovascular portfolio the strategic report leads on - is a question that shows you looked at the structure and not just the logo. The second question is about margin and it is the commercially serious one. Gross profit was £6,626,352 in 2024 and £6,626,593 in 2025 - effectively flat - on £524,000 more revenue, so the whole of the year's growth came through at close to nil incremental gross margin. The directors attribute the increase mainly to demand for some products including surgical gloves, and gloves are the commodity end of the range. Asking how the specialist cardiology and endovascular business is protected from being diluted by commodity volume is the question a commercial director would want asked. Have one date ready: the Surgical Gloves framework, on which NHS Supply Chain names only 12 suppliers, expires on 25 April 2027.

deepDive.tagline: Peterborough-based UK arm of the Danish continence, ostomy, wound and urology manufacturer Coloplast, turning over £406.9m with 727 people - most of them selling and distributing to patients at home rather than to trusts.
deepDive.lede: Two numbers frame this one. Coloplast Limited turned over £406,866,000 in the year to 30 September 2025 with 727 people, of whom 669 are in selling and distribution - which is an unusually sales-heavy shape for a company this size, and it is the shape of a business that sells through Charter, its own home delivery service, rather than only through a hospital catalogue. And the profit is real trading profit, not financing: operating profit was £33,710,000 on that revenue, up from £29,454,000, with interest making almost no difference to the result. Revenue has grown three years running, £371.6m to £390.4m to £406.9m, and the directors' own words in the 2025 strategic report attribute it to Charter maintaining its strong performance.

prose: Revenue, read from the face of the income statement in each filed set: £371,575,000 for the year to 30 September 2023, £390,449,000 for 2024 and £406,866,000 for 2025. That is 5.1% then 4.2%. The directors' own review of the business in the 2025 strategic report puts it at 4% and says the year's growth came as Charter - the company's home delivery, support and advice service - maintained its strong performance.

Margin has held while revenue grew. Gross profit was £108,609,000, then £110,580,000, then £117,412,000; as a percentage of revenue that is 29.2%, 28.3% and 28.9%. Distribution costs, which is where a home-delivery business carries most of its cost, ran at £72,700,000, £77,305,000 and £79,874,000 - rising more slowly than revenue in the latest year.

Operating profit did not move in a straight line: £31,874,000 for 2023, £29,454,000 for 2024, £33,710,000 for 2025, the 2025 figure struck after £552,000 of special items. Profit before income tax was £33,985,000, £31,808,000 and £34,534,000. Profit for the financial year was £26,250,000, £23,495,000 and £25,553,000, the 2024 dip driven by the lower operating result rather than by anything below the operating line.

The balance sheet is a trading balance sheet, not a financing one, and that distinguishes this company from many UK subsidiaries of overseas groups. Interest receivable was £1,410,000 in 2025 and interest payable £586,000 - immaterial against a £33.7m operating profit. Goodwill of £12,868,000 sits on the balance sheet, relating mainly to the acquisitions of Charter Healthcare Limited and Coloplast Medical Limited, and is not amortised but tested for impairment; the value in use of intangible assets was assessed at £71,284,000 at 30 September 2025 against £57,386,000 a year earlier. No group turnover is quoted here: Coloplast A/S is a Danish company and files no UK-readable turnover.

ownership: COLOPLAST LIMITED, company number 01094405, registered office Nene Hall, Lynchwood Park, Peterborough Business Park, Peterborough, Cambridgeshire, PE2 6FX, is an active private limited company incorporated on 5 February 1973, SIC 46900, non-specialised wholesale trade. It was named COLOPLAST UK MEDICAL SUPPLIES LIMITED from incorporation until 31 December 1978.

Note 2 of the accounts for the year ended 30 September 2025 states the position in the company's own words: the company is itself a subsidiary company, wholly owned by Coloplast A/S, and is exempt from preparing group financial statements by virtue of section 400 of the Companies Act 2006. The financial statements therefore present the company as an individual undertaking and not as a group.

The company describes its own business in the strategic report as marketing products and services for people with private and very personal medical conditions, working closely with users on their intimate healthcare requirements. The commercially significant part of that is Charter, the company's own home delivery, support and advice service, which the directors name as the driver of the 2025 result. Goodwill on the balance sheet relates mainly to the acquisitions of Charter Healthcare Limited and Coloplast Medical Limited.

marketPosition: The measurable part of Coloplast's NHS position is its framework footprint, and the rule used here is narrow: a framework counts only where NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch brief names this supplier. On that test there are five, all captured on 31/08/2026 - Advanced Wound Care (1 September 2025 to 31 August 2027, 56 suppliers), Endoscopy, Endourology and Oncology Ablation Consumables and Associated Products (1 October 2025 to 30 September 2027, 58 suppliers), Operating Theatres Equipment and Related Accessories and Services (12 April 2024 to 11 April 2028, 43 suppliers), Surgical Implants for Men's and Women's Health (1 April 2026 to 31 March 2028, 9 suppliers) and Urology and Bowel Management (21 February 2024 to 20 February 2027, 57 suppliers).

The one to lead with is Surgical Implants for Men's and Women's Health. It started on 1 April 2026 and NHS Supply Chain names only nine suppliers on it. On every other framework here Coloplast is one of 43 to 58; on that one it is one of nine. Whether that translates into volume is not something this record can say, but the field is materially narrower and it is the newest of the five.

The framework route is only half of how this company reaches the NHS, and missing the other half is the classic mistake. The frameworks array also carries a Drug Tariff Part IX (IXA/IXB/IXC) row - the primary-care reimbursement route for appliances, dispensed in the community rather than bought by a trust. For a continence and ostomy business selling through its own home delivery service, that route is where a large share of the volume sits, and it is not on any NHS Supply Chain brief. Two further rows are not counted as verified frameworks: an NHS Supply Chain Urology and Bowel Management row explicitly marked unverified in the record, which duplicates the verified row above, and an NHS SBS SBS10142 reference carried from the Hub's retired supplier directory.

This supplier's own product range has not been crawled into the Hub's product layer, so no product count is given and none is inferred. No market share is stated and none is calculable from anything read in this session; the only competitive figures here are NHS Supply Chain's own supplier counts on each framework.

deepDive.interview: The insight that will separate you here is that Coloplast Limited is not primarily a hospital supplier, and its accounts say so plainly. Of 727 average employees, 669 sit in selling and distribution, and the directors' own review of the 2025 year credits growth to Charter, the company's home delivery, support and advice service, maintaining its strong performance. Distribution costs were £79,874,000 - more than seventeen times administrative expenses. That is the cost base of a company that ships to patients' homes, not one that delivers pallets to a trust store. If you talk about this business as a theatre or catalogue sale, you have misread it. So ask about the patient, not the buyer: how Charter converts a hospital-initiated prescription into a long-term community relationship, and where the NHS Supply Chain frameworks fit around that rather than instead of it. The second thing to have ready is Drug Tariff Part IX. Continence and ostomy appliances are dispensed and reimbursed in primary care through Parts IXA, IXB and IXC, not bought through a trust catalogue, and a candidate who knows the difference between a framework award and a Tariff listing is talking the language of the actual route to market. A third, smaller point that shows you have done the reading: of the five NHS Supply Chain frameworks this company is named on, Surgical Implants for Men's and Women's Health, which started on 1 April 2026, has only nine suppliers on it. Everything else has between 43 and 58. Knowing which of your employer's positions is the narrow one is exactly the sort of specific that gets remembered.

deepDive.tagline: Swindon-registered UK arm of ConMed Corporation of Utica, New York - surgical energy, minimally invasive surgery, endoscopy and orthopaedic consumables, on £34.3m of UK turnover with 45 people.
deepDive.lede: The number that tells you what kind of business this is: 23 of 45 average employees are in sales. Conmed UK turned over £34,314,694 in the year to 31 December 2024, almost exactly flat on 2023's £34,133,902 after a 19.5% jump the year before, but it converted that into a slightly better operating profit of £3,242,356 on a gross margin that improved from 39.6% to 42.9% because cost of sales came down. This is a clinician-facing surgical business, not a catalogue one, and the frameworks bear that out - electrosurgical consumables, minimally invasive surgery, rigid endoscopy, theatres. Two of the three current directors were appointed on the same day, 22 December 2025, and two others resigned nine days later.

prose: Turnover, read from the face of the profit and loss account in each filed set: £28,554,958 for the year to 31 December 2022, £34,133,902 for 2023 and £34,314,694 for 2024. That is a 19.5% jump into 2023 and then a flat year - up 0.5%. Whatever drove 2023, it did not repeat, and that is the first thing to understand about this company's recent trading.

The interesting movement is in margin, not revenue. Cost of sales FELL from £20,631,258 to £19,599,771 on flat turnover, so gross profit rose from £13,502,644 to £14,714,923 and gross margin went from 39.6% to 42.9%. Across three years the margin has climbed steadily: 36.9% in 2022, 39.6% in 2023, 42.9% in 2024. A distributor holding revenue flat while adding six points of gross margin in two years is either changing mix or repricing, and this record does not say which, because the accounts do not.

That margin gain did not fully reach the bottom line. Distribution costs fell from £4,983,368 to £4,581,572, but administrative expenses rose from £5,385,826 to £6,890,995 - up £1,505,169, or 28%. Operating profit therefore moved only from £3,133,450 to £3,242,356. Profit before tax was £3,257,761 against £3,139,085.

Below that line the year looks much worse than it was. The tax charge more than doubled, from £764,552 to £1,839,688, cutting profit for the financial year from £2,374,533 to £1,418,073 - a 40% fall on a business whose trading result improved. Read the drop as tax, not trading. One further figure from note 7 is striking in a 45-person company: the highest paid director received remuneration of £2,889,565 in 2024 (2023: £2,401,196), of which the great majority is amounts receivable under long-term incentive schemes. No group turnover is quoted here: ConMed Corporation is a US registrant and its figures are not read in this record.

Note 1 of the 2024 accounts confirms both the number and the address in the company's own words.

The name history matters for record matching: the company was SPACEGLASS LIMITED at incorporation, LINVATEC U.K. LIMITED from 1 June 1998, and took its present name on 24 October 2013. Linvatec was ConMed's arthroscopy and powered-instruments brand, so a search for Linvatec UK lands here.

Note 20 of the accounts for the year ended 31 December 2024 states the chain in the company's own words: the immediate parent company is Conmed Europe BV, incorporated and registered in Belgium, and the ultimate parent undertaking and controlling party is ConMed Corporation, incorporated and registered in Delaware, USA, at 11311 Concept Boulevard, Largo, Florida. ConMed Corporation is named as the parent of both the smallest and the largest group preparing consolidated statements that include this company.

marketPosition: The measurable part of Conmed's NHS position is its framework footprint, and this record is unusual in that every framework row in it is verified against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch brief - there are no legacy or unverified rows carried forward. On that test there are seven, all captured 31/08/2026: Electrodes, Ultrasound Gels, Defibrillation and Related Consumables (1 February 2024 to 31 January 2028, 37 suppliers), Electrosurgical Consumables and Related Accessories (20 October 2025 to 19 October 2028, 33), Endoscopy, Endourology and Oncology Ablation Consumables and Associated Products (1 October 2025 to 30 September 2027, 58), Minimally Invasive Surgery, Related Equipment and Accessories (10 August 2026 to 9 August 2028, 60), Operating Theatres Equipment and Related Accessories and Services (12 April 2024 to 11 April 2028, 43), Rigid Endoscopy and Associated Options and Related Services (1 April 2022 to 31 March 2028, 18) and Total Orthopaedic Solutions 3 (1 February 2024 to 30 January 2028, 106).

Those seven are coherent in a way that many supplier footprints are not: electrosurgery, minimally invasive surgery, endoscopy, theatres and orthopaedics are one clinical territory, worked by one theatre-facing sales team. The narrowest field is Rigid Endoscopy, with 18 named suppliers; the broadest is Total Orthopaedic Solutions 3, with 106. Three of the seven started within the last twelve months, including Minimally Invasive Surgery on 10 August 2026, which means live implementation work across trusts right now.

The Hub's crawl of conmed.com's XML sitemap, verified 27/08/2026, captured 167 products across divisions including AirSeal and insufflation, allograft cartilage and tissue, and orthopaedics. Those names are derived from URL segments rather than read from a product record, so they show the shape and breadth of the range and should not be quoted as a catalogue. The company's own registration record also confirms the Linvatec heritage: this entity traded as LINVATEC U.K. LIMITED until 24 October 2013.

deepDive.interview: The story in these accounts is margin, and if you spot it you are ahead of most candidates. Turnover was flat between 2023 and 2024 - £34,133,902 to £34,314,694, up 0.5% - but cost of sales fell, so gross margin went from 39.6% to 42.9%, and across three years it has climbed from 36.9%. A distributor adding six points of gross margin on flat revenue has changed something about mix or price, and asking which is the single best commercial question you can ask here. Be ready for the follow-up too, because the gain did not reach the bottom line: administrative expenses rose 28%, from £5,385,826 to £6,890,995, and operating profit moved only from £3,133,450 to £3,242,356. Do not misread the reported profit fall. Profit for the financial year dropped 40%, from £2,374,533 to £1,418,073, but that is the tax charge more than doubling to £1,839,688, not trading going backwards. Saying so out loud shows you can read a P&L below the operating line. The second thing to know is that the board changed at the end of 2025 - two directors appointed on 22 December 2025, two resigned on 31 December 2025 - so two thirds of the current UK board is new. New boards change plans, and asking what the UK priorities are under it is both fair and well informed. Finally, know your framework calendar: Minimally Invasive Surgery started on 10 August 2026 and Electrosurgical Consumables on 20 October 2025, so both are in live implementation, while Rigid Endoscopy - the narrowest field at 18 suppliers - runs to 31 March 2028.

Editorial deepDive built from Companies House (Crest Medical Limited 03876927 and its parent Crest Medical Holdings Limited 06484761: company overview, persons with significant control, officers, charges and filing history), the audited accounts of both companies for the year ended 31 March 2025 read from the tagged (iXBRL) documents filed on 22/12/2025, NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs, BSI's own standards development record, Crest Medical's own website and its Cezanne careers board, all read on 18/08/2026.
deepDive.tagline: Warrington first aid, PPE and wound care supplier, named on 17 NHS Supply Chain frameworks and six of them started in 2026 · owner-controlled through Crest Medical Holdings Limited, formerly First Aid Holdings
deepDive.lede: The thing worth knowing before this interview: Crest Medical carries a great many NHS Supply Chain frameworks against a thin trading margin. Seventeen frameworks puts it level with Stryker and Mölnlycke and inside the top thirteen of the 1,216 suppliers this Hub holds, counted one way only, by how many of NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs name the company. Its own audited accounts for the year to 31 March 2025 record turnover of £24,303,917, down slightly on the £24,683,108 of the year before, and a profit before tax of £829. Not £829,000. Eight hundred and twenty-nine pounds. One rung up, the group that owns it turned over £27,984,811 and lost £824,149 before tax, which is a real improvement on the £2,381,568 it lost the year before, and it is paying £565,973 a year in interest while it builds a new warehouse and invests in the manufacturing arm it bought in 2023. Set that against the framework record and you have the interesting question in the room: six of its seventeen NHS Supply Chain frameworks started during 2026, so this is a business winning NHS category ground faster than it has so far converted into margin — and the group loss narrowed by about two thirds year on year while gross margin improved, which is the direction a commercial hire would be joining to keep going. Ask what the plan is to turn framework wins into margin.

named supplier, confirmed against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs; three re-read directly on 18/08/2026. Ranking rule, so you can judge it: count the briefs that name the company, one per framework, across the 1,216 suppliers in this Hub's seed. On that count 17 is joint eleventh with Stryker and Mölnlycke; only B. Braun (30), GBUK and Fannin (25), BD (24), GE HealthCare (23), Medtronic (22), Vygon, Praxis and Medline (21) and Banner (18) are named on more. It is a count of frameworks, not of revenue, lots or market share, and nothing here is inferred from product ranges.

Wound Closure (19 January), Skin Cleansing, Disinfection and Hygiene (16 February), Single Use Theatre Protective Wear (26 May), General Wound Care (24 June), Syringes, Needles and Associated Products (1 July) and Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions (4 August 2026)

prose: Crest Medical Limited's turnover has sat within a band of about £600,000 for four years: £24,088,369 in the year to 31 March 2022, £24,361,928 in FY2023, £24,683,108 in FY2024 and £24,303,917 in FY2025. The first three of those were read from the tagged (iXBRL) accounts by this Hub's Companies House pipeline. The FY2025 figure is not tagged in the filing, so it is quoted here from the wording of the company's own strategic report, which states it alongside the prior year. Flat is the honest description, and the flatness is what makes the framework record below worth asking about.

The profit line is where the story is. FY2025 profit before tax was £829, following a loss of £229,187 in FY2024. At group level Crest Medical Holdings Limited turned over £27,984,811 (£27,240,891 of it in the United Kingdom and £743,920 overseas) against £26,538,137 the year before, and lost £824,149 before tax against £2,381,568. So the group is growing where the trading subsidiary is not, and the loss has narrowed by about two thirds. Gross margin is the reason: gross profit rose to £9,356,525 on those sales, 33.4% against 29.8% the previous year. Below that line, distribution costs of £5,078,181 and administrative expenses of £4,397,526 still take more than the gross profit, and interest payable of £565,973 does the rest.

The directors describe a deliberate investment phase: a long-term investment in a new warehousing facility, continued investment in Crest Healthcare to strengthen manufacturing capability, and an increased focus on the hospital and retail markets. An exceptional charge of £139,532 for relocation costs sits in the FY2025 group accounts, and the registered office moved from Blue Dot House at Chesford Grange to Unit 5 Farrell Industrial Estate on 30 May 2025. No dividend was paid. The group balance sheet carries one outstanding charge, a fixed and floating debenture in favour of Clydesdale Bank PLC created on 29 March 2010; the other seven charges on the trading company's record are satisfied.

ownership: Crest Medical Limited, company number 03876927, was incorporated on 15 November 1999 and is active. It has traded under earlier names, becoming CREST MEDICAL LIMITED on 19 December 2006, and its registered SIC code is 46460, wholesale of pharmaceutical goods. Its registered office moved on 30 May 2025 from Blue Dot House, 3 Chesford Grange, Woolston, Warrington WA1 4RQ to Unit 5 Farrell Industrial Estate, Howley Lane, Warrington WA1 2PB.

Its sole person with significant control is Crest Medical Holdings Limited, company number 06484761, notified on 6 April 2016 and holding 75% or more of the shares. That parent was incorporated on 25 January 2008 as FIRST AID HOLDINGS LIMITED and took its present name on 22 August 2018. It is registered as a non-trading company (SIC 74990) at the same Warrington address, and its own sole person with significant control is Mr Alastair Gerald Lees Maxwell, notified on 1 January 2017, with the nature of control recorded as significant influence or control. This is an owner-controlled British group, not a subsidiary of an overseas manufacturer, which is unusual among suppliers with this many NHS Supply Chain frameworks and is worth knowing: decisions are taken in Warrington.

The group's own strategic report for the year to 31 March 2025 names the wholly owned subsidiaries as Crest Medical Limited, Crest Logistics Limited, Crest Healthcare Limited, Wallace Cameron Training Limited, Scopeguard Limited and Braidlock Limited, alongside other non-trading companies, and describes the group as operating across first aid, pharmaceuticals, PPE and medical consumables. Crest Healthcare Limited (15116309) was incorporated on 5 September 2023, days before the trade press reported Crest's purchase of the assets of Macdonald & Taylor Healthcare, a Cheshire manufacturer established in 1976 that brought the Primeguard brand and UK manufacturing into the group. Crest Logistics Limited (06773990) dates from 16 December 2008. The group's auditor is Wheawill & Sudworth Limited of Huddersfield, its bankers Virgin Money and its solicitors Brabners LLP.

press.text: Trade press reports Crest Medical's acquisition of the assets of Macdonald & Taylor Healthcare, a Cheshire manufacturer established in 1976, bringing the Primeguard brand and UK manufacturing capability into the group. Crest Healthcare Limited was incorporated on 5 September 2023.

Registered office of both Crest Medical Limited and Crest Medical Holdings Limited moves from Blue Dot House, Chesford Grange, to Unit 5 Farrell Industrial Estate, Howley Lane, Warrington. The FY2025 group accounts carry an exceptional charge of £139,532 for relocation costs.

Audited accounts for the year to 31 March 2025 filed for both companies. Crest Medical Limited: turnover £24,303,917, profit before tax £829. Crest Medical Holdings Limited: group turnover £27,984,811, loss before tax £824,149, no dividend.

Crest Medical's own newsroom states that BSI published BS 8599-1:2019+A1:2026, the workplace first aid kit standard, on this date. BSI's own standards development record confirms the reference and gives the full title as "Workplace first aid kits – Part 1: Contents of first aid kits and provision of Automated External Defibrillators (AEDs) in the workplace – Specification", under committee CH/100. The publication date itself is Crest's statement, read on their site 18/08/2026.

NHS Supply Chain's General Wound Care framework starts, running to 23 June 2028, with Crest Medical Ltd among 28 named suppliers (reference 2025/S 000-028909). Re-verified against the brief on 18/08/2026.

NHS Supply Chain's Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions framework starts, running to 3 August 2028, with Crest Medical Ltd among 40 named suppliers (reference 2025/S 000-032216). It combines the former Patient Assessment Devices, Blood Pressure Cuffs and Support Products, and Thermometer Device and Support Products frameworks. Re-verified against the brief on 18/08/2026.

NHS Supply Chain posts a contract launch update on the General Wound Care framework: a number of new product NPCs were not orderable at the 24 June launch, with plasters, cotton wool and first aid kit lines being released through August. This is a framework-level notice and NHS Supply Chain does not attribute the affected lines to a named supplier on the brief, so no claim is made here that they are Crest's.

The Infusion Pumps and Administration Sets and Associated Products framework expires. NHS Supply Chain's own brief records it as a Contract Extension that "starts on 3 October 2022, runs for 48 months and ends on 30 September 2026", including a 24 month extension, with Crest Medical Ltd among 27 named suppliers. Verified on the brief on 18/08/2026; six weeks away at the date of this record.

hiring: Crest Medical's own careers board, hosted on Cezanne, carried exactly one live vacancy on 18/08/2026: a Senior Warehouse Operative in Warrington, in Supply Chain. No salary is published. The careers pages describe roles "from apprenticeships to direct roles in our warehouse and manufacturing teams, through sales and customer service, to senior leadership", and list benefits including a birthday day off, the option to buy annual leave and discounted gym membership. Read that as a company recruiting for operations right now rather than proof it is not recruiting commercially: with 82 people in the trading company and 115 in the group, field vacancies here are occasional and are also placed through recruiters this check did not cover.
marketPosition: The verifiable measure of this company's NHS position is its framework footprint: named supplier on 17 separate NHS Supply Chain frameworks, each confirmed against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch brief. They span wound care at both ends (Advanced Wound Care and General Wound Care), Wound Closure, Skin Cleansing, Disinfection and Hygiene, Single Use Theatre Protective Wear, Syringes and Needles, Blood Collection Devices, Extension Sets and Lines, Infusion Pumps and Administration Sets, Enteral Feeding and Bile Bags, Patient Temperature Management, Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions, External Defibrillation Devices, Orthotics, Podiatry and Immobilisation, Physiotherapy and Occupational Therapy, Maternity, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Sexual Health, and Cleaning Equipment and Supplies. Six of the 17 started during 2026 and one, Infusion Pumps and Administration Sets, expires on 30 September 2026.

That breadth is the thing to understand about Crest. It is not a category specialist. It is a wholesaler and own-brand manufacturer whose route into the NHS is being on a great many framework lots with modest volumes on each, and its own site describes it as a wholesale manufacturer of first aid, occupational health products, PPE and consumer health products, and a private label supplier to retail in the UK, Europe and the USA. Its brands are Blue Dot, Wallace Cameron, McKinnon Medical, BioSafe, Irripod, Stericlens and Primeguard, with Microplast, Easyice, Burnkool, Cromessol, Revive-Aid, Advapore, Advacare and Once alongside them. Primeguard is manufactured in the UK by Crest Healthcare.

No market share is given here, and one widely repeated claim is deliberately not repeated: a third-party company directory describes Crest Medical as the largest provider of personal protective equipment to the NHS. No source for that was found in NHS Supply Chain's own material, in the company's filings or on the company's own website, so it is treated as unverified and is not published as a fact. Three Crest products are confirmed in the NHS Supply Chain catalogue by NPC: Stericlens 0.9% sodium chloride aerosol spray in 240ml (ELZ008) and 100ml (ELZ007), and Irripod 20ml sodium chloride irrigation pods in packs of 25 (MRB742). The Hub's own crawl of crestmedical.co.uk on 12/08/2026 read 872 products from the site's XML sitemap; those names come from URL slugs rather than a product record, so treat that as the shape of the catalogue rather than an exact list.

deepDive.interview: Read the accounts before you go in, because they set up the two questions worth asking. The first is margin. Turnover has been flat around £24m for four years and FY2025 profit before tax was £829, while group gross margin improved from 29.8% to 33.4%. Asking what the next point of margin comes from, own-brand mix or the new warehouse, is a serious commercial question and shows you have read the filing rather than the website. The second is conversion. Six NHS Supply Chain frameworks started in 2026, which means live implementation work across trusts right now, and the Infusion Pumps and Administration Sets framework expires on 30 September 2026, so there is a renewal in the diary within weeks of most start dates. Ask how the team is resourced across both. Two pieces of context help you sound like an insider: the standard for workplace first aid kits was amended this year and BSI's own title for BS 8599-1:2019+A1:2026 now runs to the provision of AEDs in the workplace, which touches two Crest categories at once; and this is an owner-controlled business, so the person with significant control sits on the board you are joining rather than in another country. Finally, know which entity you are being hired into. Crest Medical Limited, Crest Healthcare Limited and Crest Logistics Limited are separate companies at the same address doing different jobs.

alerts.text: CRITICAL OWNERSHIP CORRECTION: Current Health is NO LONGER owned by Best Buy. Best Buy acquired it for ~$400m in late 2021, took a $475m non-cash goodwill impairment charge (Q4 2024), launched a $109m restructuring and wound down hospital-at-home partnerships (May 2025), then SOLD Current Health back to co-founder/former CEO Chris McGhee on 24/06/2025 -- it now operates as an independent private company refocused on US home-hospital/high-acuity care. UK/NHS availability is UNCONFIRMED post-divestiture: the current site is entirely US-hospital-focused, the /uk/ marketing page now 404s, the clinical command-centre nursing staff are described as US-licensed only, and no UKCA mark was found (only FDA 510(k) and EU CE Class IIa). Only historical NHS references found: Dartford and Gravesham NHS Trust pilot (Jan 2019), Whittington Health Virtual Ward trial (Feb 2023) -- no evidence of a live 2025/2026 NHS deployment. Do not present this as a currently NHS-available product without direct confirmation from the company.

background.heading: Speciality re-tagging
background.text: Re-tagged primary speciality to Anaesthesia and critical care (kept Renal and dialysis as a secondary tag) -- CE-marked indications are cytokine/bilirubin/myoglobin adsorption in critical illness and intraoperative anticoagulant removal during cardiac surgery, not renal replacement itself (it's commonly run in-line with a CRRT circuit, which is a delivery mechanism, not the clinical indication). NICE has published three Medtech Innovation Briefings -- MIB87 (sepsis), MIB217 (COVID-19 respiratory failure), MIB249 (cardiac surgery bleeding reduction) -- all note the evidence base is low-quality/small-sample/mostly observational; current sepsis evidence does not show improved mortality. Any efficacy claims should be qualified as emerging, not established.

background.heading: NHS deployments and funding
background.text: Do NOT list DrugSorb-ATR (ticagrelor removal — FDA De Novo denied April 2025, unclear CE status) or HemoDefend-RBC/-BGA (blood-transfusion safety filters) as available products -- both are investigational/pipeline-stage only, not approved anywhere for the DrugSorb-ATR/HemoDefend line.

background.heading: Entity identification
background.text: The domain danielshealth.co.uk is a PARKED/inactive domain, not Daniels Health's genuine UK site -- the real UK operating entity trades as 'Sharpsmart' at sharpsmart.co.uk (Companies House: SHARPSMART LIMITED, 04261387). Exhaustively checked NHS Supply Chain: 'Sharpsmart', 'Clinismart' and 'Bladesmart' ALL return zero results -- these appear to run as managed-lease service contracts direct with trusts (Daniels owns/reprocesses the containers, trusts pay a service fee) rather than catalogue-orderable disposables, which is the most likely explanation for the absence, though this is inference not confirmed fact. FLAG: 'Sharpsguard' (already listed in this record) could not be confirmed as a genuine Daniels Health/Sharpsmart product in this research pass -- it did not appear anywhere on sharpsmart.co.uk. Worth checking directly, as this name is commonly associated with a different manufacturer -- do not present it as confirmed Daniels/Sharpsmart branding without verification.

background.heading: Entity identification
background.text: IMPORTANT: there is a SEPARATE, unrelated company also trading in sharps/clinical waste containers under a very similar name -- 'Daniels Healthcare' at daniels.co.uk, part of Mauser Packaging Solutions since 2016 (Mauser UK Ltd). Its products (e.g. 'Daniels Transport 7') ARE confirmed live on NHS Supply Chain under supplier 'MAUSER UK LTD' -- do not conflate the two companies; Mauser's Daniels Healthcare does not offer Sharpsmart's reusable-container model.
