deepDive.origin: supplier-deep-capture scheduled run, 26/08/2026. Built from Companies House (company overview, filing history and officers pages for DELTA SURGICAL LIMITED, 04154893; company overview and persons-with-significant-control pages for CRE8 MEDICAL LIMITED, 06306663, the immediate/ultimate parent), Delta Surgical's own filed accounts for the year ended 30 September 2025 read at source (tagged iXBRL), and Delta Surgical's own website (About Us and product pages), all read in this session. The framework rows are this Hub's own capture of 24/08/2026 from NHS Supply Chain's contract launch briefs and are not restated here.
deepDive.tagline: A Staffordshire neurosurgery, ENT and endovascular distributor on eight NHS Supply Chain frameworks, turnover up 2.8% to £11.9m in the year to 30 September 2025, and majority-owned by an employee ownership trust since 26 September 2024.
deepDive.lede: Delta Surgical Limited is a small, still-family-run distributor that changed hands on paper without changing hands in practice. On 26 September 2024 the persons-with-significant-control register of its parent, CRE8 Medical Limited (06306663), recorded three individual holders — Katie Louise Armfield, Karina Humble and Robin Charles Humble, each previously holding more than 25% but not more than 50% — as ceased the same day, and recorded Cre8 Medical Trustee Limited (15509678) as notified with more than 50% but less than 75% of the shares and voting rights and the right to appoint or remove directors. Jonathan Charles Humble's own entry, more than 25% but not more than 50%, is unaffected and still active. That is the register's own description of a move to majority employee ownership, and it is confirmed independently in the FY2025 accounts: note 25 states the company had outstanding contractual commitments to its parent of £6,830,712 (2024: £7,876,348) "in relation to future contributions payable to the employee ownership trust which holds a majority shareholding in the parent company", and note 28 names CRE8 Medical Limited as the immediate and ultimate parent, with Cre8 Medical Trustee Limited as the ultimate controlling party. Turnover rose 2.8% to £11,946,722 in the year to 30 September 2025, with gross margin held at 46% in both years; the FY2025 strategic report attributes the fall in profit before tax to costs "previously incurred by the parent company, now being incurred in Delta Surgical Limited", which reads consistently with an EOT-linked group reallocating cost between the trading company and its parent.

stats.n: £11,946,722, from the line the company itself labels Turnover on the face of its profit and loss account, note 3 ("Turnover and other revenue"), in the full accounts for the year ended 30 September 2025, filed at Companies House 30 June 2026, approved by the board and authorised for issue 25 June 2026, signed by Mr R C Humble, Director. Prior year £11,619,731, a rise of 2.8%. No turnover tag exists in the filing's iXBRL tag set (only core:ProfitLoss and core:AverageNumberEmployeesDuringPeriod are tagged), so this figure is read from the labelled line on the face of the accounts rather than extracted automatically, per this Hub's PDF/xhtml-reading method.

£2,153,340 against £2,303,500 in FY2024, from core:ProfitLossOnOrdinaryActivitiesBeforeTax in the tagged filing. Profit for the year (after tax) was £1,561,346 against £1,725,662 (core:ProfitLoss). The strategic report attributes the fall to costs "previously incurred by the parent company, now being incurred in Delta Surgical Limited", while stating gross margin was maintained at 46% in both years.

Prior year UK turnover was £11,01x,xxx-range (partially cut off in the extract read); the note confirms the business is overwhelmingly UK-facing, consistent with its role as an NHS Supply Chain framework distributor rather than an exporter.

Read as printed rather than as tagged: core:AverageNumberEmployeesDuringPeriod carries scale="-2" against values of 31 and 25, which would divide to 0.31 and 0.25 if the scale were applied. Per this Hub's standing rule (a scaled headcount that is not a whole number was not scaled, it was mangled), the figures are used as printed: 31 for FY2025, 25 for FY2024. prose: The strategic report's own account of the year is short and consistent with the numbers: turnover up 2.8% "driven by the promotion of existing lines of products", gross margin flat at 46%, and a fall in profit before tax explained by cost reallocation from the parent rather than by trading weakness. No revenue growth strategy, product launch or contract win is named in the extract read.

ownership: DELTA SURGICAL LIMITED, company number 04154893, registered office Unit 10, Evolution, Hooters Hall Road, Lymedale Business Park, Newcastle, Staffordshire, England, ST5 9QF, is a private limited company incorporated on 6 February 2001 and Active. SIC code on the register: 47990, other retail sale not in stores, stalls or markets — a generic wholesale/distribution code that does not describe the specific product range and should not be used to categorise the company.

Active officers, read from the register 26/08/2026: Mrs Katie Louise Armfield (appointed 11 April 2017), Mr Jonathan Charles Humble (appointed 11 April 2017), Mrs Karina Humble (appointed 10 October 2002) and Mr Robin Charles Humble (appointed 1 October 2012). Two historic appointments are resigned: Mr Christopher Hugh Carberry (appointed 6 March 2001) and Mr Graham Roger Langley (appointed 30 September 2002), alongside a formation-agent secretarial appointment resigned the same year the company was formed.

The parent, CRE8 MEDICAL LIMITED, company 06306663, is registered at the same Lymedale Business Park address, incorporated 9 July 2007, SIC 70100 (activities of head offices), and is named in Delta Surgical's own FY2025 accounts (note 28) as its immediate and ultimate parent undertaking. CRE8 Medical Limited's own PSC register records the 26 September 2024 change described in the lede above: majority control (more than 50%, less than 75% of shares and voting rights) passed to Cre8 Medical Trustee Limited (15509678), a company limited by guarantee at the same address, while Jonathan Charles Humble's own minority holding (more than 25%, not more than 50%) continued unaffected. The register records this as a dated PSC entry, not as a described transaction: no price or consideration is on file, and this record asserts only what the register itself states.

The FY2025 accounts describe the trust's economic role, not just its shareholding: note 25 records £6,830,712 of the company's guaranteed outstanding contractual commitments to its parent (2024: £7,876,348) relating to future contributions payable to the employee ownership trust that holds the parent's majority shareholding. That figure has fallen year on year, which is consistent with the trust's acquisition debt (typically raised to buy out the selling shareholders) being paid down, though this session did not read an earlier filing to confirm when the EOT was established relative to the 26 September 2024 PSC change.

marketPosition: The framework footprint, captured for this Hub on 24/08/2026 from NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs, names Delta Surgical Ltd (or Delta Surgical Limited) on eight frameworks: Electrosurgical Consumables and Related Accessories (33 suppliers), Patient Monitoring Equipment, Bedside Equipment Alarm Monitoring Systems, Related Products and Services (35), Patient Temperature Management (18, Lots Three and Five), Pressure Area Care and Patient Handling (53), Procedure Packs (29), Syringes, Needles and Associated Products (53), Total Orthopaedic Solutions 3 (106) and Wound Closure (39). Two of the eight — Pressure Area Care and Patient Handling and Wound Closure — started in 2026. Full dates, references and supplier counts are on this record's own framework panel rather than restated here.

The framework categories (temperature management, pressure area care, wound closure, procedure packs) sit oddly against the product range the company's own website actually shows, which is neurosurgery, ENT and spinal surgical instruments, endovascular thrombectomy and aneurysm devices, and intensive-care/haemostatic consumables — cranial stabilisation and brain retraction (DORO, Vycor), ICP and multi-modality neuromonitoring (Raumedic), CSF management (Neuromedex, IRRAS), surgical drill systems (Bien Air), ultrasonic aspirators (Söring), aneurysm clips (Peter Lazic), endovascular aspiration thrombectomy and vasospasm treatment (Vesalio NeVa), advanced haemostats (Collastat, StypCel, Surgispon, Boz) and Zoll intensive therapy unit products. Neither list should be read as complete for the other: a framework award evidences that the company supplies into that category, it does not evidence which specific product lines fill it, and the website's own product menu is not cross-checked here against NHS Supply Chain's catalogue.

The company's own About Us page describes itself as "a privately run UK company, founded in 2001" with its HQ and distribution hub in Staffordshire, acting as a UK distributor to overseas medical device manufacturers, and separately manufacturing/sourcing its own range of equipment covers and patient drapes. It makes no mention of CRE8 Medical, the employee ownership trust, or any parent company — the group structure is visible only in the Companies House filings, not on the company's own site.

deepDive.interview: The one thing worth knowing before this meeting isn't on Delta's own website: since 26 September 2024 the majority owner of its parent company, CRE8 Medical Limited, has been an employee ownership trust, not the Humble family outright. Jonathan Charles Humble still holds a direct minority stake and, with Robin Charles Humble, Karina Humble and Katie Louise Armfield, still sits on the trading company's board — so day-to-day, this is still a small, founder-family-run distributor, and its own site still describes itself that way with no mention of the trust. But the FY2025 accounts show the trust structure has a real cash cost: £6.8m of contractual commitments to fund future EOT contributions, down from £7.9m the year before, which is the debt from buying the family out being paid down. Turnover is modest and steady — £11.6m to £11.9m, up 2.8% — with margin held flat at 46%, and the fall in profit before tax is explained by the parent moving some of its own costs down into the trading company, which is a bookkeeping shift inside the group rather than a trading problem. On product fit: their own site is squarely neurosurgery, ENT and endovascular — DORO cranial stabilisation, Vesalio NeVa thrombectomy, Zoll ITU kit — which sits awkwardly against the eight NHS Supply Chain frameworks they're named on (pressure area care, wound closure, procedure packs, syringes and needles). Don't assume either list is the whole story: ask which of their eight frameworks actually carries product they distribute, because the framework award itself only proves category eligibility, not which lines are live.

deepDive.lede: This is Draeger Medical UK Limited (company number 04310199, Hemel Hempstead), the sales, service and distribution arm of the German Dräger Group's medical equipment in the UK. It is not the same company as Draeger Safety UK Ltd (00777464, Blyth, Northumberland), which is the group's separate industrial gas-detection and PPE business — the two are easy to confuse because Blyth is the larger, more visible UK site, but nothing in this record is about Blyth. Draeger Medical UK turned over £58.9 million in the year to 31 December 2024, down 4.1% on 2023's £61.3 million after an unusually strong prior year; it employed 191 people on average, mostly in selling, distribution and servicing (164 of the 191), and posted an operating margin of 4.0% (2023: 7.5%). It does not do its own research and development — that sits elsewhere in the Dräger Group — and its cash is pooled with its German parent. It is on several live NHS Supply Chain frameworks covering anaesthesia machines, ventilators, airway management, patient monitoring, theatres, patient temperature management, respiratory and neonatal/phototherapy equipment. An MHRA safety notice is currently open on its Atlan anaesthesia workstations over a ventilator motor fault.

prose: Turnover swung sharply through the pandemic years: £41.6m (2018) to £48.8m (2019), then a spike to £82.4m in 2020 before falling back to £61.9m (2021), £53.7m (2022), £61.3m (2023) and £58.9m (2024). The company's own 2024 strategic report describes the latest move (down 4.1% on 2023) as "reflecting the timing of project delivery", against 14.3% growth the year before — in other words, large capital-equipment orders land in lumps, and a single big NHS trust order sliding between financial years can move the whole line.

Profitability has narrowed more than turnover has fallen. Gross margin was 21.3% in 2024 against 23.3% in 2023, and operating profit to turnover fell from 7.5% to 4.0%, which the strategic report attributes to product mix and a 7% rise in distribution and administration costs from inflation and investment. Return on capital employed dropped from 48.9% to 31.5% over the same year.

The company pays no bank interest of note and holds no debt beyond lease liabilities; it participates in a cash-pooling arrangement with its German parent, so its own balance sheet cash is nominal (£100,000 in the years checked) and its liquidity depends on the Drägerwerk Group, which the FY2024 accounts say has given assurances that funding will continue to be available.

An interim dividend of £3.96m was paid in 2024 (£0.92 per £1 ordinary share), up from £3.02m in 2023; no final dividend was recommended in either year. Dividends have consistently exceeded the profit retained in most of the years checked, i.e. the UK company is run to remit cash to the German parent rather than to build up reserves.

ownership: Draeger Medical UK Limited, company number 04310199, was incorporated in England and Wales on 24 October 2001. Its registered office is The Willows, Mark Road, Hemel Hempstead, Hertfordshire, HP2 7BW — this address is printed on the face of every set of accounts checked (FY2019 through FY2024) and matches the live Companies House register exactly, which is one of the four routes used to confirm this is the correct entity. It has no previous registered names.

A second, separate UK-registered Dräger company exists and is NOT this supplier: Draeger Safety UK Ltd, company number 00777464, registered office Ullswater Close, Blyth Riverside Business Park, Blyth, Northumberland, NE24 4RG, incorporated 16 October 1963 (previously Draeger Safety Group Limited, and Draeger Limited from 1986 to 2002). Its SIC codes (28990 — manufacture of other special-purpose machinery; plus 46690 and 74909) and Blyth address show it is the industrial gas-detection, PPE and drug/alcohol-testing business, not hospital equipment. The two entities are easy to conflate because Blyth is the larger, more publicly visible UK Dräger site; this record draws only on 04310199's own filings.

Identity for 04310199 was established four ways, not from the Hub's stored "probable" match: (1) the registered office on the live Companies House register (The Willows, Mark Road, Hemel Hempstead, HP2 7BW) matches the address printed on the face of every set of accounts read; (2) the accounts themselves state "Registered number 04310199" (or "4310199") on their cover page in every year checked, 2019–2024; (3) the directors named in the accounts (Mr M Irving and Mr M Bedford, later Malcolm Irving and Matthew Thomas Bedford) match the active directors on the live officers register, both appointed 22 October 2020; (4) the persons-with-significant-control register names Drägerwerk AG & Co. KGaA directly (ownership of shares, 75% or more, notified 6 April 2016), matching note 22 of the accounts.

Note 22 ("Ultimate parent undertaking") of the FY2024 accounts states: "The immediate and ultimate parent undertaking and controlling party is Drägerwerk AG & Co KGaA, incorporated in Germany... Drägerwerk AG & Co KGaA is the parent undertaking of the smallest and largest group of undertakings to consolidate these financial statements at 31 December 2024. The consolidated financial statements of Drägerwerk AG & Co KGaA are available from Drägerwerk AG & Co KGaA, Moislinger Allee 53/55, 23541 Lubeck, Germany." This has been the stated position in every year of accounts checked (2019–2024).

The directors' report (FY2024) states the company's research and development is managed by other entities within the Group, and that the company "operates as a sales, marketing and distribution agent for the Dräger Group". The FY2024 accounts also disclose that goodwill on the balance sheet (carried at cost, assessed annually for impairment, recoverable amount in excess of £124,000 at the last test) arose from "the UK element of the Group's acquisition of the patient monitoring business of Siemens under a global Joint Venture in 2003" — the one piece of the company's history that involves an acquisition rather than simply distributing Dräger-branded product.

Auditor: the accounts were audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP (Newcastle upon Tyne) at least through the FY2023 accounts, signed by Toni Alderson (Senior Statutory Auditor) on 23 May 2024. The FY2024 accounts were instead audited by KPMG LLP (also Newcastle upon Tyne), signed by Tara Stonehouse (Senior Statutory Auditor) on 23 May 2025 — i.e. the audit changed hands from PwC to KPMG between the FY2023 and FY2024 signing dates. No reason for the change is stated in either set of accounts.

One caution for anyone pulling further documents from this filing series: the FY2023 accounts' own contents page carries a drafting slip — the line for the auditors' report reads "Independent auditors' report to the members of Draeger Safety UK Limited", naming the sister company. This appears to be a copy-paste error by whoever prepared the document (both companies likely share preparers within the Group); the report's own heading two pages later, and every figure and signature in the document, correctly say Draeger Medical UK Limited, and the revenue and profit figures on that filing reconcile exactly with the comparative columns in the surrounding years' filings. It is noted here only as a live illustration of how easily the two entities get mixed up, not as a doubt over which company's figures these are.

marketPosition: Draeger Medical UK Limited does not manufacture or design the products it sells. Its own directors' report says plainly that it "operates as a sales, marketing and distribution agent for the Dräger Group" and that R&D is carried out by other Group entities; its principal activity is "the supply of medical equipment and related activities including the servicing of medical equipment and the supply of consumables and spare parts." Anyone meeting this company is meeting the UK commercial and service organisation for anaesthesia workstations (Atlan, Perseus), ICU ventilators (Evita, Babylog for neonatal), patient monitoring (Infinity) and neonatal/infant care equipment (Isolette, Babyleo, Babyroo, BiliLux) manufactured by the wider Dräger Group, largely in Germany.

"Not listed here" is not evidence the company is absent from a given category; it was simply not checked on this run.

The one open safety issue on the company's own core capital equipment is the MHRA notice on Atlan anaesthesia workstations (see press, above) — a ventilator motor defect being corrected in the field, not a recall of the platform, and with no confirmed patient harm reported by the manufacturer as of the notice's own reference date.

deepDive.interview: Ask what the UK entity actually controls versus what sits with the German parent: pricing and stock allocation for capital equipment like Atlan and Evita are set by a manufacturing group that had €3.48bn in worldwide net sales in FY2025, so a UK rep's room for manoeuvre on a big theatre order is worth probing directly. Ask about the Atlan ventilator motor issue (MHRA DSI/2026/005) — how the UK service organisation is prioritising the motor-assembly replacement programme across NHS trusts, and what "permanent supervision" in the interim actually means for a busy theatre list. Given turnover fell 4.1% in 2024 on the company's own account of "timing of project delivery", ask how order timing and installation scheduling actually work for large capital deals, since that lumpiness is central to how revenue is recognised and reported. Given the company runs on a cash-pooling arrangement with its parent and pays out dividends larger than several years' retained profit, ask what genuine investment authority the UK operation has for stock, service vehicles or headcount versus what needs sign-off from Lübeck. Finally, given the accounts changed auditor from PwC to KPMG between the FY2023 and FY2024 signings with no stated reason, this is a fair, neutral thing to ask about if audit or governance comes up — auditor rotation is routine and this alone proves nothing, but it is a genuine, sourced fact worth having in your back pocket rather than a rumour.

prose: Group turnover, read from the face of the consolidated profit and loss account in each filed set: £111,338,000 for the year to 31 December 2023, £108,545,000 for 2024 and £105,957,000 for 2025. That is three consecutive years of decline, down 2.5% then 2.4%, and 4.8% over two years.

The result has deteriorated faster than the revenue. Operating profit of £196,000 in 2023 became an operating loss of £1,541,000 in 2024 and £3,757,000 in 2025. Gross profit actually held up - £36,219,000, £34,629,000, £35,477,000 - and gross margin improved from 32.5% to 31.9% to 33.5%, so the problem is not the front line. Below gross profit, distribution costs rose from £15,815,000 to £16,921,000 and administrative and other operating expenses from £13,259,000 to £15,331,000, up £2,072,000 in a single year on falling turnover. Other gains swung from a £628,000 credit in 2024 to a £956,000 charge in 2025.

Interest is a material drag and it is intercompany. Interest payable and similar charges were £1,872,000, £2,462,000 and £2,535,000; note 23 records £21,802,000 owed to Medical Depot Inc., a parent company, at 31 December 2025, at 9.9% per annum, with an interest charge of £1,865,000 for the year and a repayment date of 20 December 2031. Loss before taxation was £1,676,000 in 2023, £4,003,000 in 2024 and £6,292,000 in 2025; loss for the year £2,227,000, £4,038,000 and £6,020,000. The parent company alone lost £5,110,000 in 2025 (2024: £3,239,000).

The financing position changed completely after the year end and the directors set it out at length. The Kingswood acquisition on 3 November 2025 ended the existing Medical Depot facilities with JP Morgan Chase Bank and Delaware Trust Company, along with the formal guarantees over a number of UK entities. New guarantees in favour of Fortress Credit Corp were lodged at Companies House on 13 February 2026, secured over certain UK assets, and are not due for repayment for five years from the acquisition. Separately, the Commercial Loan from Lloyds Bank plc was repaid early in January 2026, the revolving credit facility ceased, and Lloyds' securities were withdrawn. The directors forecast underlying EBITDA and cash generation through to 30 June 2027. No group turnover for the wider Kingswood-owned group is quoted here: nothing readable in this session gives one.

ownership: The registered entity is 04301005, registered office Sidhil Business Park, Holmfield Industrial Estate, Holmfield, Halifax, West Yorkshire HX2 9TN, an active private limited company incorporated on 8 October 2001, SIC 46900 and 86900. Its name on the register today is DRIVE MEDICAL LIMITED. It was DRIVE MEDICAL LIMITED from 21 January 2008, DRIVE DEVILBISS HEALTHCARE LIMITED from 1 August 2016, and reverted to DRIVE MEDICAL LIMITED on 17 July 2026. The 2025 accounts, which cover a period ending before that change, are filed under the DeVilbiss name. Its own website, read 04/09/2026, brands entirely as Drive Medical and states "Drive Medical Ltd is a company registered in England and Wales. Company Number: 4301005", which is 04301005 zero-padded.

Ownership changed on 3 November 2025. The directors state in the strategic report, the going concern note and note 25 that the ultimate parent company, CD&R Reign Topco Inc, and all of its worldwide subsidiary entities were sold to Kingswood Capital Management. In the strategic report's Investors section they describe the ultimate parent as Kingswood Capital Management LLC, registered in the United States, and set out how the group reports to it: annual financial targets and in-year reforecasts signed off by both, regular meetings on monthly and quarterly performance, and prior approval required for any significant investment or structural change. The accounts refer to the acquirer as both Kingswood Capital Management LP and Kingswood Capital Management LLC in different places; this record repeats both rather than choosing, because the filing does not resolve it.

Medical Depot Inc. remains a parent company for related-party purposes, owed £21,802,000 at 31 December 2025 at 9.9% per annum. The UK group also has subsidiaries of its own: the directors record that Drive Devilbiss Healthcare Limited incurred directors' remuneration on behalf of Drive Devilbiss Sidhil Limited and Specialised Orthotic Services Limited in the year and did not recharge them. The Sidhil name in the registered office address is the Halifax bed and pressure-care manufacturer the group acquired; it is the reason this supplier's aliases include Sidhil.

This is a community and care-home equipment position, not a theatre one, and the crawled range confirms it: 985 products from the drivemedical.co.uk XML sitemap, verified 01/09/2026, across bathing and toileting, beds and accessories, moving and handling, furniture and more - toilet frames, footstools, community care home beds, hoists. The crawl domain itself is drivemedical.co.uk, which independently corroborates the rebrand.

Two of the five frameworks started within the last six months of this record being written - Pressure Area Care and Patient Handling on 9 March 2026 and Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions on 4 August 2026 - which means live implementation across trusts and community equipment services right now, being carried by a sales function that shrank from 68 people to 61 across 2025.

Two rows in the frameworks array are not counted in the five and should not be quoted as current: an undated Aids for Daily Living and Walking Aids row and an undated Pressure Area Care and Patient Handling row, both marked 'verify lot at source', which duplicate the verified rows above. No market share is stated and none is calculable from anything read this session; the only competitive figures here are NHS Supply Chain's own supplier counts.

deepDive.interview: Get the name right before anything else. Companies House recorded the change from Drive DeVilbiss Healthcare Limited to Drive Medical Limited on 17 July 2026, the website now brands entirely as Drive Medical, and there is not a DeVilbiss reference on the homepage. Saying DeVilbiss in the room would date you by more than a year, and it is an easy thing to get right. The reason behind it is the substance of the conversation: on 3 November 2025 the ultimate parent, CD&R Reign Topco Inc, and all its worldwide subsidiaries were sold to Kingswood Capital Management, and a rebrand back to the older name three months into new ownership is a decision somebody made deliberately. Ask what the new owner wants the UK business to be, and you are asking the question the board is answering. Be honest about the numbers, because they are not good and pretending otherwise will not read as loyalty. Group turnover has fallen three years running, £111.3m to £108.5m to £106.0m, and the operating result has gone from a £196,000 profit in 2023 to a £3,757,000 loss in 2025. But gross margin actually improved, from 32.5% to 33.5%, so the front line is holding; the damage is in distribution costs and administrative expenses, which together rose more than £3m across two years on falling revenue, and in £2,535,000 of interest, most of it on a £21.8m intercompany loan at 9.9%. That last point is the one that will mark you out: the interest is intercompany, and the post-year-end refinancing under Fortress Credit Corp changes the picture. Finally, know the workload: two of the five NHS Supply Chain frameworks - Pressure Area Care and Patient Handling from 9 March 2026, and Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions from 4 August 2026 - are in live implementation, and the sales headcount fell from 68 to 61 in the same period.

Two sets of filed statutory accounts of Drive Devilbiss Healthcare Limited, both downloaded from Companies House and read page by page in this session: the year ended 31 December 2025, source for the 2025 and 2024 consolidated profit and loss account, the strategic report (principal activities, the Kingswood sale, the exceptional items table, the Investors section on parent reporting), the directors' report (SECR figures and going concern), note 4 (exceptional items and operating loss detail), note 5 (employee numbers by category, staff costs, directors' emoluments, key management compensation, the subsidiary remuneration point), note 23 (the Medical Depot Inc. loan, rate, interest charge and repayment date) and note 25 (post balance sheet events: the Fortress Credit Corp guarantees lodged 13 February 2026, the Lloyds Commercial Loan repayment in January 2026 and the RCF cessation); and the year ended 31 December 2024, source for the 2023 comparatives. The company's own website at drivedevilbiss.co.uk, read 04/09/2026, is the source for the Drive Medical branding and the registration statement in its footer. background.heading: Divestment and spin-off
background.text: MAJOR CORPORATE SPLIT: in March 2021 Eckert & Ziegler divested its entire HDR afterloader/applicator business into a separate company, BEBIG Medical GmbH, which as of 31/03/2024 is 100% independently owned (majority stake TCL Healthcare Equipment, Shanghai) -- Eckert & Ziegler has NO ownership stake left in it. Eckert & Ziegler BEBIG Limited (the UK entity, Companies House 05270457) was dissolved 05/03/2024. Eckert & Ziegler retains ONLY the prostate-seed (IsoSeed/IsoCord/IsoStrand) and ophthalmic (Ru-106) product lines -- SagiNova, GyneSource, Tulip and the Co-60/Ir-192 sources are now BEBIG Medical GmbH's, distributed in the UK via Oncology Systems Ltd (osl.uk.com). The old MultiSource afterloader is superseded by SagiNova -- do not list as current.

suppliers.ownership: Eckert and Ziegler retains the seed and ophthalmic brachytherapy business on medical.ezag.com. The HDR afterloading and X-ray therapy business was spun off into BEBIG Medical GmbH and sold to TCL Healthcare Equipment (Shanghai) Co., Ltd; BEBIG Medical GmbH now trades independently on bebigmedical.com. deepDive.tagline: Ecolab Limited (company no. 00649192), the NHS's hand-hygiene, cleaning and decontamination supplier trading as "Ecolab Ltd", turned over £238.5 million in the year to 30 November 2025, up from £233.5 million the year before (Companies House, full accounts filed 24 July 2026).

deepDive.lede: Ecolab Limited is the UK trading company behind the hand hygiene, surface disinfection and decontamination products the NHS actually orders: Actichlor Plus, Videne, Skinman and the Bioquell decontamination equipment range. It turned over £238.5 million in the year to 30 November 2025 (2024: £233.5 million), with profit down to £22.4 million from £25.6 million as costs grew faster than sales. That figure covers the whole UK entity, not an NHS-only slice - Ecolab Limited also sells hospitality and foodservice hygiene products, and the accounts do not split turnover by customer or product. The physical manufacturing sits in a sibling company, Ecolab Manufacturing UK Limited, since an internal trade transfer in September 2021. The ultimate owner is Ecolab Inc. of St Paul, Minnesota (NYSE: ECL), a $16.1 billion-turnover world leader in water, hygiene and infection prevention. Its pharma/cleanroom brand Klercide sits in a different global reporting segment entirely and is not sold into NHS wards - do not present it as a ward product.

prose: Turnover has grown from about £198-200 million a year in 2020-2022 to £238.5 million in FY2025, but the growth is not organic trading momentum alone: the step up from £198.1 million (FY2022) to £227.5 million (FY2023) follows Ecolab Limited's acquisition of Bioquell Limited and Bioquell UK Limited on 6 June 2022, with their decontamination-equipment trade and assets moved onto Ecolab Limited's own books the same day. Bioquell's hydrogen-peroxide-vapour decontamination technology is precisely the product line that now appears against "Ecolab Limited" on NHS Supply Chain's Decontamination Capital Equipment framework, so this is a directly NHS-relevant acquisition, not a diversification away from the health sector.

Profit has not kept pace with turnover. FY2025 profit before tax fell to £19.0 million from £30.2 million in FY2024, and profit for the year fell to £22.4 million from £25.6 million, even though turnover rose. Cost of sales rose from £172.8 million to £175.5 million and administrative expenses rose sharply from £43.1 million to £49.1 million, while "income from shares in group undertakings" (a non-trading intercompany item) fell from £9.2 million to £1.4 million and swung most of the pre-tax profit movement on its own. A rep should read this as margin pressure in the underlying trading business, partly offset in past years by non-trading group income that has now largely gone away.

Average headcount has been broadly flat at 920-970 since the September 2021 restructuring moved manufacturing staff to Ecolab Manufacturing UK Limited (headcount was over 1,000 in 2020-2021, when manufacturing was still inside this company). Net assets have risen steadily, from £115.8 million (FY2023) to £124.6 million (FY2025), helped by a growing pension surplus (£30.5 million at FY2025, up from £29.9 million) sitting on the balance sheet.

Directors paid dividends of £16.4 million in FY2025 (2024: £26.7 million) and recommended none for the year - a normal pattern for a wholly owned subsidiary remitting cash to its US parent rather than a sign of distress; the strategic report itself calls FY2025 performance "in line with expectations".

ownership: Ecolab Limited, company number 00649192, is a private company limited by shares, incorporated in England and Wales on 10 February 1960. It was originally SOILAX LIMITED (10 Feb 1960 - 16 Mar 1987), then ECOLAB LIMITED (16 Mar 1987 - 11 Jul 1991), then HENKEL-ECOLAB LIMITED (11 Jul 1991 - 30 Nov 2001), reverting to ECOLAB LIMITED on 30 November 2001 - all four routes to identity confirmed independently this session: these previous names as recorded on the live Companies House register; the registered office on the register (Winnington Avenue, Northwich, Cheshire, CW8 4DX) matching the address printed on the face of every set of accounts read; the company number 00649192 printed on both the cover and the balance sheet of the accounts, matching the register; and the active directors named in the FY2025 accounts (D Hough, P Lund) matching the active officers currently shown on the register.

SIC code on the register is 20411, manufacture of soap and detergents. Note 1 of the FY2025 accounts states the company's principal activity as "the manufacture and sale of hygiene products and provision of related hygiene services", and note 5 states all turnover "arose from one class of business" with no further split - so the £238.5 million headline covers Ecolab's whole UK hygiene trading book (hospitality, foodservice and industrial customers as well as NHS and other healthcare), not an NHS-only or healthcare-only figure. No product-line or customer-segment breakdown is disclosed in the UK filing.

Immediate parent undertaking: Nalco Acquisition One, a company incorporated in the United Kingdom (note 30, FY2025 accounts). Ultimate parent undertaking and controlling party: Ecolab Inc, incorporated in the United States of America (Delaware, 1924), whose registered address for its consolidated accounts is given as Ecolab Center, 370 Wabasha Street North, St Paul, Minnesota 55102, USA. Ecolab Inc is listed on the New York Stock Exchange as ECL and is the smallest and largest group to consolidate Ecolab Limited's results. Under FRS 102, Ecolab Limited is exempt from disclosing transactions with fellow Ecolab Inc group companies, and the accounts state there were no transactions with related parties outside the Ecolab Inc group in the year.

Auditor: PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, Chartered Accountants and Statutory Auditors, Manchester. The FY2025 report is signed by Edward Moss, Senior Statutory Auditor, dated 9 July 2026, giving an unqualified opinion (true and fair view; no exceptions reported under the Companies Act 2006). The financial statements were approved by the board on 8 July 2026 and signed on its behalf by D Hough, Director.

Companies House lists several other active UK companies whose name begins "Ecolab", checked individually this session to rule out confusion with the healthcare-supplying entity: ECOLAB MANUFACTURING UK LIMITED (03555308, active, same Winnington Avenue registered office, SIC 82990 other business support) - this is where the physical manufacturing trade and assets sit since the September 2021 intercompany transfer described above; it is not the entity that contracts with the NHS. ECOLAB (U.K.) HOLDINGS LIMITED (04524464, active, same registered office, SIC 70100 activities of head offices) - a UK holding company, not a trading entity. ECOLAB SERVICES (01946513, active, registered at Chancery House, Sutton, Surrey - a different address - SIC recorded as "non-trading company"). ECOLAB GB 1 LIMITED (15287488, active, incorporated 15 November 2023, registered in Llantrisant, Wales, SIC "non-trading company") - a newly formed, apparently dormant vehicle. ONE ECOLAB PENSION PLAN TRUSTEE LIMITED (05982934, active, same registered office, SIC 99999 dormant company) - the pension scheme's corporate trustee only. ECOLAB SOLUTIONS LP (SL021505, active Scottish limited partnership, registered at a corporate-services address in Edinburgh) - no trading or SIC information found; not the supplying entity. MICROTEK MEDICAL EUROPE LIMITED (02671655, DISSOLVED, formerly at the same Winnington Avenue address) - the historic UK home of Ecolab's surgical drapes and barrier-products ("surgical solutions") business; Ecolab Inc's FY2025 Form 10-K confirms the group sold its global surgical solutions business on 1 August 2024, consistent with this UK entity now being dissolved and confirming that line is no longer part of Ecolab's current NHS offer. ECOLAB POWLES HUNT LIMITED (05718253, dissolved, a different registered office in Swindon) - no accounts were read for this dissolved company and no link to the current healthcare business could be established; treated as unconnected. ECOLABNL CHEMICAL LTD (16416723, active, incorporated 29 April 2025, registered at a Cambridge serviced-office address with no other connection found to any Ecolab Inc UK entity) - treated as a coincidental name match and excluded; searches for "Anios" and "Microtek" turned up no other UK-registered Ecolab-linked entity beyond Microtek Medical Europe Limited above.

Confidence on identity: HIGH. Only 00649192 trades under the exact name ("Ecolab Ltd" / "Ecolab Limited") printed on every NHS Supply Chain contract launch brief for this supplier; only 00649192 carries the soap/detergent-manufacture SIC code and describes itself as a manufacturer and seller of hygiene products and services; and only 00649192's own strategic reports document the 2022 Bioquell acquisition that put decontamination equipment - the exact category on the NHS Decontamination Capital Equipment framework - onto its books. No other UK Ecolab-family entity is active, trading and healthcare-facing at the same time. Turnover, profit and headcount figures in this record apply to 00649192 only.

press.text: Ecolab Limited acquired Bioquell Limited and Bioquell UK Limited and, the same day, took their trade and assets onto its own balance sheet - the source of the decontamination-equipment business now named against "Ecolab Limited" on NHS Supply Chain's Decontamination Capital Equipment framework. Reported in Ecolab Limited's own Companies House-filed Strategic report for the year ended 30 November 2022, page 1.

Ecolab Limited's manufacturing trade and assets were transferred by intercompany asset purchase agreement to a subsidiary, Ecolab Manufacturing UK Limited - the trading model Ecolab Limited still operates under. Reported in Ecolab Limited's Strategic report for the year ended 30 November 2021, page 1.

Ecolab Inc sold its global surgical solutions business (surgical drapes and barrier products). Disclosed in Ecolab Inc's Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2025 as a comparability adjustment to organic-sales measures. This is consistent with the dissolution of the UK company that historically carried this trade, Microtek Medical Europe Limited (02671655, registered at the same Winnington Avenue address as Ecolab Limited, now dissolved).

Ecolab Inc restructured its reportable segments: the former Global Healthcare and Life Sciences segment was split, with the healthcare/hospital infection-prevention business moving into the Institutional operating segment (part of the new Global Institutional & Specialty reportable segment) and Global Life Sciences (pharma/personal-care cleanroom work, including Klercide) becoming its own standalone reportable segment. Disclosed in Ecolab Inc's Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2025.

Ecolab Inc acquired Ovivo's electronics business for $1.6 billion cash, a provider of ultrapure water technology for semiconductor manufacturing, reported within the Light & Heavy operating segment (Global Water) - not healthcare-related, but the largest disclosed group acquisition in the period covered by this record. Disclosed in Ecolab Inc's Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2025.

No vacancy counts are published in this record as a result, rather than an estimate drawn from third-party job-listing aggregators, which are not used as a source under this system's rules.
marketPosition: Ecolab Limited is a manufacturer, distributor and service provider of hygiene, cleaning and infection-prevention products and equipment - not a device manufacturer in the implant/instrument sense, and not a single-product company. Its own accounts describe one class of business: "the manufacture and sale of hygiene products and provision of related hygiene services", sold across hospitality, foodservice and industrial customers as well as the NHS - the UK filing does not separate healthcare/NHS revenue from the rest.

The NHS-relevant part of the range, per the Hub's existing framework capture (see frameworks), spans: hand hygiene and associated products and services; skin cleansing, disinfection and hygiene (Videne, Skinman, Manodes GP); instrument decontamination and accessories; environmental decontamination; decontamination capital equipment (the Bioquell hydrogen-peroxide-vapour range, acquired June 2022); cleaning equipment, supplies and associated products; and a named-supplier position (Lot Three) on Patient Temperature Management. Products named in the Hub's existing record include Actichlor Plus (NaDCC chlorine tablets with detergent) and Ecolab Soluscope (endoscope/probe decontamination consumables). This is a whole-hospital hygiene and infection-prevention footprint, not a single-department deal.

Klercide is a genuine Ecolab brand but sits in Ecolab Inc's Global Life Sciences segment (pharmaceutical and personal-care cleanroom contamination control), which as of 1 January 2025 is formally a separate reportable segment from the hospital-facing Institutional business. It should not be presented to an NHS ward audience as a ward-hygiene product - the Hub's existing correction note (zero NHS Supply Chain hits for Klercide) stands and is reinforced by this year's segment split.

Physical manufacturing for the UK business does not sit inside Ecolab Limited - it was moved to sibling company Ecolab Manufacturing UK Limited in September 2021. A rep or candidate should not assume Ecolab Limited itself runs the factory; it is the trading, sales and (since 2022) decontamination-equipment company, while Ecolab Manufacturing UK Limited is the production entity, and Ecolab (U.K.) Holdings Limited sits above both as the UK holding company.

Group strategy, per Ecolab Inc's FY2025 10-K, aims by 2030 to help protect 2 billion people from infections and to provide enough drinking water for 1 billion people, alongside continued M&A (most recently the $1.6 billion Ovivo Electronics acquisition in the unrelated Global Water segment, completed 16 December 2025) - the group is acquisitive and still restructuring how it reports its healthcare business, so a candidate should expect segment names and reporting lines to keep moving.

Honest gaps: no UK-specific or NHS-specific revenue, margin or headcount figure is disclosed anywhere in the sources read - the £238.5 million UK turnover is the whole trading company, and the $6.10 billion Global Institutional & Specialty segment figure mixes healthcare with an unrelated foodservice/QSR business. No commercial or sales leadership names could be verified. No market-share claim is made or available in this system.

deepDive.interview: Ask about the split trading model: manufacturing moved out of Ecolab Limited into Ecolab Manufacturing UK Limited in September 2021 - find out who a rep should actually call for a supply or production query, since the entity that signs an NHS contract is not the one that makes the product. Ask how well the Bioquell decontamination-equipment business (acquired June 2022) is now integrated three years on, since it drove most of the jump in turnover from £198 million to £227 million between FY2022 and FY2023 - is it still growing on its own, or was that a one-off step change. Ask directly about margin: turnover rose in FY2025 but profit before tax fell from £30.2 million to £19.0 million, with cost of sales and administrative expenses both rising faster than sales - what is driving that, and is it expected to continue. Ask how the group's 1 January 2025 segment split plays out on the ground in the UK: healthcare/hospital infection prevention now sits inside the Institutional business rather than a standalone healthcare segment, while Klercide and cleanroom work sit in the separate Global Life Sciences segment - does that change who a rep reports to, or how healthcare accounts are resourced, within Ecolab Limited. Finally, for a candidate: ask which UK Ecolab entity they would actually be employed by, given the group runs at least three active UK companies (Ecolab Limited, Ecolab Manufacturing UK Limited, Ecolab (U.K.) Holdings Limited) plus a newly formed, apparently dormant Ecolab GB 1 Limited - and note that Companies House shows two director changes on the same day, 5 September 2025 (Paul Rawding out, Per Lund in), which is worth asking about directly since Companies House itself records no reason for the timing.

alerts.text: MAJOR CORPORATE CHANGE: Exactech, Inc. filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy in October 2024, driven by ~2,600 patient lawsuits over a packaging/oxidation defect (vacuum bags missing an oxygen barrier layer, causing polyethylene insert oxidation across 140,000+ knee, ~130,000 hip and ~1,500 ankle systems, plus the Equinoxe shoulder system) -- recall ran August 2021 through April 2024. Court confirmed a restructuring plan 15/09/2025; assets sold to a new investor group (Strategic Value Partners, Stellex Capital Management, Greywolf Capital Management). The business relaunched as ADVITA ORTHO, LLC on 03/11/2025, which now owns and distributes the Equinoxe/Vantage/Alteon/Truliant/Novation/Newton/GPS product lines. TPG Capital (the brief's assumed current owner) no longer owns the business -- a litigation trust was set up to pursue claims against TPG. UK legal entity Companies House record shows 'ADVITA ORTHO UK LIMITED' with 'previous name: EXACTECH (UK) LIMITED'. NHS Supply Chain now refers to the supplier as 'Advita Ortho (Exactech) Ltd.' Recall litigation/restructuring fallout is still live as of the most recent sources -- do not present the recall as resolved-and-behind-them without this context.

deepDive.tagline: Companies House 02663514, active since 1991 · registered office Vital Westminster Industrial Estate, Measham, Swadlincote · controlling party changed on 8 September 2025 to Healthco Investment Limited, the vehicle named in Investindustrial's purchase of DCC Healthcare
deepDive.lede: The thing worth knowing before this interview: Fannin is named on more NHS Supply Chain frameworks than any other supplier in this Hub's framework data — 25, against GE HealthCare's 20 and Medtronic's 19 — and it changed hands less than a year ago. On 8 September 2025 the Companies House PSC register recorded B.M.Browne (UK Holdings) Limited ceasing to control the company and Healthco Investment Limited being notified in its place; two days later DCC plc announced it had completed the sale of its healthcare division, and Healthco Investment Limited is the vehicle named in Investindustrial's own announcement of that deal. The board has turned over completely since: six officers resigned between August 2025 and March 2026, five were appointed between September 2025 and May 2026, and the year end moved from 31 March to 31 December. This is a first-year private-equity carve-out with an unusually wide NHS framework footprint, and that combination is the real subject of any conversation about targets, territory or which ranges get pushed.

ownership: Fannin (UK) Limited is a long-standing UK company under a brand-new owner. It was incorporated on 18 November 1991 as Showissue Limited, traded as B.M. Browne (UK) Limited from February 1992, and took the Fannin name on 28 June 2007. Until last year it sat inside DCC plc's healthcare division — the Vital medical devices platform — with B.M.Browne (UK Holdings) Limited (02872126) recorded as the party with significant control since June 2016.

In November 2024 DCC plc announced, after a strategic review, that it intended to dispose of DCC Healthcare and concentrate on its larger energy business. On 22 April 2025 Investindustrial announced it had signed an agreement to buy the division, naming Healthco Investment Limited as the acquiring entity, at a total enterprise value of £1,050 million on a cash-free, debt-free basis, including £130 million of two-year deferred consideration. Investindustrial's own release describes DCC Healthcare as two platforms — HBI, a supplements and beauty contract manufacturer, and Vital, a supplier of medical devices to acute and primary care — with more than 3,000 employees, 11 manufacturing sites, revenue of £859.4 million and adjusted operating profit of £88.1 million in the year to 31 March 2024, about 13% of DCC group adjusted operating profit. DCC announced completion on 10 September 2025, alongside an £800 million return of capital to its own shareholders.

The register carries the same event from Fannin's side, and this is the part that can be checked rather than taken on trust: on 8 September 2025 the PSC entry for B.M.Browne (UK Holdings) Limited ceased and Healthco Investment Limited (16384404, a holding company incorporated on 14 April 2025) was notified as having significant influence or control. The identical PSC event, on the identical date, appears on Williams Medical Supplies Limited (04240054) and SP Services (UK) Limited (03424705). Both of those are themselves named on NHS Supply Chain frameworks in this repo's data — Williams on 3, SP Services on 2 — so 28 distinct framework positions in this data now sit under one owner. Fannin and SP Services are co-listed on two of them (Electrodes, Ultrasound Gels, Defibrillation and Related Consumables; General Wound Care), and Fannin and Williams share none. Worth knowing before you read an 'also on this framework' list as a list of independent rivals.

Investindustrial's portfolio page presents the business simply as Vital: around 1,500 employees, headquartered in Ireland, operating in France, the UK and Germany and selling into more than 100 countries, through units it names as Vital Healthcare and Vital Healthcare Ireland. That page does not name Fannin, and it dates the investment to August 2025 rather than September; the register date and DCC's own completion announcement are used here in preference. Whether the Fannin trading name survives the group's rebranding is not something any source read here settles, and it is a fair question to ask in an interview rather than a fact to assume.

marketPosition: Fannin is named on 25 NHS Supply Chain frameworks in this repo's data, the highest count of any supplier in it. The counting rule: a supplier is counted on a framework only where NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch brief for that framework names it, supplier names are normalised to a single key so that 'Fannin Ltd', 'Fannin UK Ltd' and 'Fannin UK Limited' count once per framework, and the count is taken over the 122 briefs parsed into this repo on 12 August 2026. Fifteen further briefs did not parse and are logged as unparsed, so this is a ranking over what has been read, not over every framework NHS Supply Chain runs.

What that number is not: it is not turnover, volume, or share. A framework position is permission to be bought from, not evidence of anything having been bought. No market share percentage is published for this company anywhere in this system, because nobody has that data. What the count does support is a narrower and more useful claim — Fannin's route to the NHS is breadth of distribution across many consumable categories rather than depth in one, which is a different sales job from a single-technology manufacturer's, and is worth reflecting in how you pitch yourself.

On size, Fannin (UK) Limited files full accounts, but the filing at Companies House is a PDF with no tagged figures, so no turnover is read from it and none is estimated here. The £859.4 million quoted above is DCC Healthcare's whole divisional revenue for the year to 31 March 2024 under the previous owner, covering both HBI and Vital across every country, and it must not be read as Fannin's.

glassdoor.summary: 42% would recommend the company to a friend and 46% rate the business outlook positively. Sub-ratings: compensation and benefits 2.3, work-life balance 3.2, culture and values 3.2, career opportunities 2.2. Read honestly, this is a small sample on a group employer page that is Ireland-weighted rather than specific to the UK entity or the Measham site, and the reviews predate the change of ownership; treat it as a weak signal, not a verdict on the UK business. The lowest-scored items are pay and progression, which is the pair worth probing if you are asked whether you have any questions.

deepDive.interview: Lead with the ownership change, because it is recent, checkable and nobody expects a candidate to know it: the company came out of DCC plc into Investindustrial's hands in September 2025, and every current board member was appointed after that date. Fair questions follow naturally — what the first year under the new owner has changed about targets and range focus, whether the Fannin brand stays as the group consolidates on the Vital name, and whether the two sister companies now under the same owner (Williams Medical Supplies, SP Services) change how territories or accounts are split. On the commercial side, know that this is a broad-line distributor: 25 NHS Supply Chain frameworks spanning airway, vascular access, electrosurgery, endoscopy, wound care, theatre wear, orthopaedics and waste, rather than one flagship technology. That means a portfolio-selling conversation with procurement and category managers, not a single-product clinical evangelism pitch, and your examples should be picked to match. Do not walk in describing them as an independent family business; that stopped being true last September.

background.text: Confirmed genuinely single hardware product. Received FDA approval Dec 2025 (first at-home brain-stimulation device approved for depression in the US), US launch targeted Q2 2026, prescription-only in the US -- this is a US regulatory milestone, not UK/NHS-relevant directly. UK/EU: CE-marked Class IIa (specific certificate numbers not independently verified), sold direct-to-consumer, no prescription required privately. Not on general NHS prescription -- a 2026 NHS Innovation Accelerator fellow with pilot activity across 5 named NHS trusts (Leicestershire Partnership, Northamptonshire Healthcare, Norfolk and Suffolk, Rotherham Doncaster and South Humber, West London) plus NHS Practitioner Health -- local pilots/QI projects, not national commissioning. NICE HTG382 (tDCS for depression, general) recommends use only 'with special arrangements for clinical governance, consent and audit or research' -- do not overstate as NICE-approved. ~$13m raised Oct 2025, plus One Mind Accelerator investment Feb 2026 tied to US expansion.

alerts.text: IMPORTANT CONTEXT — the Freedom SCS/PNS product line was originally developed by Stimwave Technologies Incorporated (US), which filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy in June 2022. Stimwave's former CEO, Laura Perryman, was criminally convicted of healthcare fraud and conspiracy (also separately SEC-charged with $41m investor fraud) — the case centred on an internal device component that in some implanted units was reportedly a non-functional piece of plastic rather than the real electronic receiver; roughly 8,000 patients were implanted with these devices between 2017 and 2020. Curonix LLC purchased Stimwave's assets out of bankruptcy in Nov 2022 and now manufactures/sells the Freedom SCS/PNS systems under the Curonix name. Whether Freedom Neuro BV is the current Curonix-era UK distributor or a leftover Stimwave-era relationship is unconfirmed. Confirmed NHS Supply Chain Neuromodulation Devices framework-approved (2024-2028) but no live catalogue SKUs found under this name. Given this is a clinician-facing CPD/training tool, this history should not be omitted if the product is referenced.

suppliers.ownership: Curonix LLC, a Delaware company, which bought certain Stimwave assets out of Chapter 11. The Freedom name survives only as the product family, the Freedom System. Effective 31/10/2022. Source: The official Stimwave estate notice at https://stimwavefreedom.com/ , read in full: 'Stimwave Technologies Incorporated and Stimwave LLC (collectively, "Stimwave") filed a voluntary petition for bankruptcy protection under Chapter 11 of the United States Bankruptcy Code in the District of Delaware on June 15, 2022. Certain Stimwave assets were purchased by Curonix LLC following the bankruptcy sale on October 31, 2022.' The page directs patients and clinicians to Curonix.com. Curonix's own site, https://curonix.com/ (which redirects to https://curonix.com/intl/ from the UK), was also read across its home, about, news, terms and privacy pages.

Editorial deepDive built from Companies House (FUJIFILM HEALTHCARE UK LIMITED 03218117: company overview and previous names, persons with significant control, officers, charges and filing history), the audited accounts of that company for the year ended 31 March 2025 filed on 05/12/2025, the audited accounts of AQUILANT ENDOSCOPY LIMITED 03402556 for the year ended 30 December 2025 filed on 03/07/2026, NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs, and the Companies House company search for every registered company whose name begins Fujifilm, all read on 20/08/2026. Both sets of accounts are scanned PDF filings with no iXBRL tagging and no machine-readable text layer; every figure below was read off the page of the filed document named beside it, from the line the company itself labelled, and none was inferred from position.
deepDive.tagline: Bedford diagnostic imaging and endoscopy business, the former Hitachi Medical Systems UK, named on nine NHS Supply Chain frameworks in its own right and one of only five suppliers on the national Flexible Endoscopes framework · turnover £45.8m in its first full year after Fujifilm UK's diagnostics division transferred in, and it bought Aquilant's endoscopy business on 1 December 2025
deepDive.lede: Three things about this company are not obvious from its name, and all three change how you would sell for it or interview at it. The first is that it is the old Hitachi business: FUJIFILM HEALTHCARE UK LIMITED, company number 03218117, was HITACHI MEDICAL SYSTEMS UK LIMITED from 2002 until 1 July 2021, and before that Hitachi Ultrasound and Ecoscan Ultrasound, so the ultrasound and MRI heritage on the NHS frameworks predates the Fujifilm badge by two decades. The second is that it only recently became the trading entity it now is. Fujifilm UK Limited's medical diagnostic division transferred into it on 1 October 2023, and the year to 31 March 2025 was, in the directors' own words, the first full year after that transfer. Turnover was £45,830,000 against £28,810,000, and the honest reading of that 59.1% is that the prior year holds roughly six months of the transferred business, not that the market grew by three fifths. The third is the shape of the headcount. Of 155 average employees, 64 are in sales and sales support and 86 in after-sales and technical, against 4 in administration and distribution. This is a capital-equipment business where the service contract is the annuity: £16,840,000 of the £45.8m, 36.7%, is rendering of services rather than sale of goods. Then on 1 December 2025 it bought the endoscopy trade of Aquilant, a competitor already carried in this Hub, and told its auditors it expects that plus the NHS 10-Year Health Plan to add 10% to sales in the year to 31 March 2026. That is the business you would be joining: mid-forties millions of UK-only revenue, growing by acquisition into a framework it already sits on with only four other suppliers.

stats.n: £45,830,000, against £28,810,000 in the year to 31 March 2024. Read from the Income Statement on page 15 of the full accounts of Fujifilm Healthcare UK Limited (03218117) filed at Companies House on 05/12/2025. All of it is United Kingdom revenue: note 3 gives the geographical analysis as £45,830,000 United Kingdom and nothing elsewhere. Treat the 59.1% increase with care, because the prior year is not a like-for-like base: see the growth section.

prose: There is no ten-year turnover series for this company and there should not be, because the entity's revenue base changed twice inside four years. Fujifilm Holdings Corporation was notified as the person with significant control on 31 March 2021, the day Hitachi's holding ceased, and the company was renamed from Hitachi Medical Systems UK Limited on 1 July 2021. Then, on 1 October 2023, the medical diagnostic division of Fujifilm UK Limited transferred into it. The two comparable figures on the face of the FY2025 accounts are turnover of £28,810,000 for the year to 31 March 2024 and £45,830,000 for the year to 31 March 2025, and the strategic report describes FY2025 as the first full year following that transfer. So the year to March 2024 carries only about six months of the transferred business. The 59.1% increase the directors print in their own key performance indicators table is arithmetically correct and is not a like-for-like growth rate. A bar chart of those two years would say something the accounts do not, so none is drawn.

Everything else on the FY2025 face of the accounts moved the same way. Gross profit was £18,535,000 on £45,830,000 of sales, a gross margin of 40.4% against 36.3% the year before. Below that, distribution costs were only £367,000 and administrative expenses £16,031,000, which is what a business with 86 field service and technical staff and 64 in sales looks like when it books almost all of its people cost as administrative. Operating profit was £2,137,000, interest receivable £447,000 against interest payable of £245,000, profit before tax £2,339,000 and profit after tax £1,748,000. Shareholders' funds rose 55.9% to £4,876,000 and cash balances to £9,455,000 from £4,789,000.

Two structural facts sit behind those numbers and are worth knowing before you read the margin as a commercial achievement. The going concern note describes the company as a Limited-Risk Distributor with access to the group's cash pooling arrangement, which is a transfer-pricing structure: a limited-risk distributor is remunerated to earn a modest, stable return, so the operating margin here of 4.7% is substantially set by group policy rather than by UK negotiation. The same note adds that the company is not permitted under group policy to use derivative or hedging techniques, transacts over 95% of purchases and sales in Sterling, holds no fixed debt and does not insure against debtor failure. The directors' forecast for the year to 31 March 2026 assumes growth in sales of 10%, attributed to the acquisition of Aquilant Endoscopy Limited and to strategic alignment with the NHS Fit for the Future 10-Year Health Plan, and assumes a £3m intercompany loan is repaid within the period.

ownership: FUJIFILM HEALTHCARE UK LIMITED, company number 03218117, was incorporated on 28 June 1996 and is active, at Fujifilm House, Whitbread Way, Bedford MK42 0ZE, with SIC code 47749, retail sale of medical and orthopaedic goods. Its previous names are the whole story of the business: ECOSCAN ULTRASOUND LIMITED from incorporation to 17 January 2000, HITACHI ULTRASOUND LIMITED to 4 April 2002, and HITACHI MEDICAL SYSTEMS UK LIMITED from then until 1 July 2021. Its sole active person with significant control is Fujifilm Holdings Corporation of Tokyo, registration number 010401065370, notified on 31 March 2021 with ownership of 75% or more of shares and voting rights and the right to appoint or remove directors. Kabushiki Kaisha Hitachi Seisakusho, that is Hitachi Ltd, is recorded as a ceased person with significant control on the same date, 31 March 2021. Note 20 of the accounts names Fujifilm Holdings Corporation as the ultimate parent company and the parent of both the smallest and the largest group for which consolidated statements are drawn up.

The company is not the only Fujifilm entity selling into the NHS, and the distinction matters when you are reading a framework award or addressing a contract. Companies House holds FUJIFILM UK LIMITED (01264514, incorporated 1976) and FUJIFILM SONOSITE LTD (04104159, incorporated 2000) at the same Bedford address, alongside this company. The strategic report records that the medical diagnostic division of Fujifilm UK Limited transferred to Fujifilm Healthcare UK Limited with completion on 1 October 2023 and all systems and activities fully integrated during the year to 31 March 2025. Note 21 records the consequence for pensions: as part of that transfer the company became a participating employer of the Fujifilm UK Pension and Life Assurance Scheme, which includes a closed defined benefit section that this company does not contribute to but has guaranteed the obligations of should another participating employer default. That scheme is accounted for in Fujifilm UK Limited's own statements and its funding position at 31 March 2025 was assets £67,579,000, liabilities £60,945,000 and a net surplus of £6,634,000.

On 30 September 2025 the company announced an asset acquisition relating to the endoscopy business of Aquilant Endoscopy Limited. Its own note 22 states the acquisition cost as £13.9m, to take place on 1 December 2025, funded by an intercompany share capital issue, and the register corroborates the funding step: an SH01 filed on 21 November 2025 records a statement of capital of GBP 13,500,000 following an allotment of shares on that date, with the enabling resolution filed on 25 November 2025. The transaction completed. Aquilant Endoscopy Limited (03402556, formerly Endoscopy UK Limited and then Imotech Medical Limited, of Basingstoke) states in its own strategic report for the year ended 30 December 2025, filed on 3 July 2026, that on 1 December 2025 a substantial portion of its trade was sold to a third party for consideration of £12,208,000, that the remaining trade and assets were immediately hived across to another group company, Aquilant Limited, and that from that date the company has ceased to trade and is expected to become dormant. The two consideration figures, £13.9m stated by the buyer as acquisition cost and £12,208,000 stated by the seller as consideration for the trade sold, are not the same number and are not reconciled here; they are quoted as each company filed them.

Four charges have been registered against the company and one is outstanding: a fixed charge in favour of Bank Mendes Gans N.V., created 5 August 2021 and delivered 6 August 2021. Bank Mendes Gans is the cash pooling and netting bank the going concern note refers to. The three satisfied charges are historic Barclays and landlord security from 1996 and 1998, two of them marked satisfied only on 18 October 2024.

press.text: The company's name changes from HITACHI MEDICAL SYSTEMS UK LIMITED to FUJIFILM HEALTHCARE UK LIMITED on the register. Fujifilm Holdings Corporation had been notified as person with significant control on 31 March 2021, the date Hitachi Ltd's holding is recorded as ceased.

Completion of the transfer of Fujifilm UK Limited's medical diagnostic division into Fujifilm Healthcare UK Limited, as stated in the strategic report of the FY2025 accounts. The same accounts record that all systems and activities were fully integrated during the year to 31 March 2025, and note 21 records that the company became a participating employer of the Fujifilm UK Pension and Life Assurance Scheme as part of the transfer.

NHS Supply Chain's Digital Diagnostic Solutions framework starts, running to 31 July 2027, reference 2025/S 000-043444, with Fujifilm Healthcare UK Ltd among 54 named suppliers. Re-read on the brief on 20/08/2026. It is the company's only framework outside the 2021 diagnostic equipment tender.

Fujifilm Healthcare UK Limited announces an asset acquisition relating to the endoscopy business of Aquilant Endoscopy Limited, stated in note 22 of its own FY2025 accounts at a cost of £13.9m, to complete on 1 December 2025 and to be funded by an intercompany share capital issue.

An SH01 is filed recording a statement of capital of GBP 13,500,000 following an allotment of shares on that date, with the enabling resolution of allotment filed on 25 November 2025. This is the funding step note 22 describes.

The Aquilant endoscopy transaction completes. Aquilant Endoscopy Limited's own strategic report for the year ended 30 December 2025 states that on this date a substantial portion of its trade was sold to a third party for consideration of £12,208,000, that the remaining trade and assets were then hived across to Aquilant Limited, and that from that date the company has ceased to trade and is expected to become dormant.
Full accounts for the year ended 31 March 2025 filed at Companies House: turnover £45,830,000, operating profit £2,137,000, profit before tax £2,339,000, 155 average employees.

Nine of the company's twelve NHS Supply Chain frameworks expire on this date. They were all awarded under one reference, 2021/S 000-007768, started on 1 April 2022 and run 72 months including two 24 month extensions: Bladder Scanners, Bone Densitometers, CT Scanners, Flexible Endoscopes, Magnetic Resonance Imaging Scanners, Mammography Imaging Systems, Mobile Image Intensifiers, Mobile X-Ray Systems, Static X-Ray and Ultrasound Scanners. Verified against the briefs; the Flexible Endoscopes brief was re-read live on 20/08/2026. This is a single renewal event covering most of the company's NHS Supply Chain footprint, not ten separate ones, and it is the most important date in this record.

hiring: No live vacancy list was verified for this company in this session, so nothing is claimed about what it is recruiting for today. What the filed accounts do show is the direction of travel in the workforce, and it is unusually clear. Average employees went from 88 to 155 in one year. Sales and sales support went from 32 to 64 and after-sales and technical from 37 to 86, while management fell from 12 to 1 and administration and distribution from 7 to 4. Some of that is the reclassification you would expect when a division transfers in and job families are mapped onto a new payroll, so do not read the management line as 11 people leaving. The sales and service lines are the ones to take at face value: this company roughly doubled both in the year to 31 March 2025, and directors' remuneration rose from £276,464 to £405,623 across a board that grew over the same period.
marketPosition: This company's NHS position is a narrow and deep one, and the Hub's own framework data shows it plainly. Every one of the twelve NHS Supply Chain frameworks that names a Fujifilm entity sits in a single category, Diagnostic Equipment and Services. There is no wound care, no consumables spread, no facilities line. Nine of the twelve were awarded under one reference, 2021/S 000-007768, all starting 1 April 2022 and all expiring 31 March 2028: Bladder Scanners, Bone Densitometers, CT Scanners, Flexible Endoscopes, Magnetic Resonance Imaging Scanners, Mammography Imaging Systems, Mobile Image Intensifiers, Mobile X-Ray Systems, Static X-Ray and Ultrasound Scanners. The other three are Digital Diagnostic Solutions (2025/S 000-043444, to 31 July 2027) and Laboratory Diagnostics, Point of Care Testing and Pathology Managed Services (2023/S 000-028831, to 11 March 2028).

The supplier lists on those briefs are short, which is the commercially useful part. Flexible Endoscopes names five suppliers in total: FUJIFILM Healthcare UK Limited, Karl Storz Endoscopy UK Ltd, Olympus KeyMed, Pentax Medical and Richard Wolf UK Limited, re-read live on 20/08/2026. Bone Densitometers names six, Magnetic Resonance Imaging Scanners and Mammography Imaging Systems seven each, CT Scanners eight, Mobile Image Intensifiers ten, Bladder Scanners eleven, Static X-Ray thirteen, Mobile X-Ray fourteen and Ultrasound Scanners twenty-one. Against that, Digital Diagnostic Solutions carries 54 named suppliers and Laboratory Diagnostics 122, so those two are a very different kind of framework and being on them says much less about position. No market share figure is given anywhere in this record, because none is verifiable.

⚠ The Hub's single supplier record for Fujifilm covers three separate registered companies, and this record does not merge them. Nine briefs name Fujifilm Healthcare UK Limited or Ltd. Three name FUJIFILM UK Ltd or Limited, which is company 01264514: Bladder Scanners, Laboratory Diagnostics Point of Care Testing and Pathology Managed Services, and Ultrasound Scanners. The Ultrasound Scanners brief separately names FUJIFILM Sonosite Ltd, company 04104159, as its own supplier alongside FUJIFILM UK Limited. The timing is consistent with the 1 October 2023 division transfer, since the 2021 tender was awarded while the diagnostics business still sat inside Fujifilm UK Limited, but NHS Supply Chain's briefs are not evidence that the contracting entity on those three has been novated to Fujifilm Healthcare UK Limited, and this record does not claim that it has. If the contracting entity matters to you, ask NHS Supply Chain or the company; do not infer it from the brief.

The Aquilant purchase is the one competitive move a rep should be able to talk about. Aquilant is already a supplier in this Hub, named on fifteen NHS Supply Chain briefs across its group entities, and two of those briefs name Aquilant Endoscopy Limited specifically: Ear, Nose and Throat (ENT) Endoscopes and Associated Options and Related Services, and Endoscopy, Endourology and Oncology Ablation Consumables and Associated Products. That company sold its trade on 1 December 2025, has ceased to trade and expects to become dormant, per its own filed accounts. Whether those two framework positions moved to Fujifilm Healthcare UK Limited, to Aquilant Limited (which received the residual trade), or to neither, is not stated on the briefs and was not verified in this session. It is an open question, not a finding, and it is a very good question to ask in an interview.

deepDive.interview: Read the FY2025 accounts before you go in, because three lines in them set up better questions than anything on the website. First, do not walk in praising 59% growth. The directors themselves say the year to 31 March 2025 was the first full year after Fujifilm UK's diagnostics division transferred in on 1 October 2023, so the comparative holds about six months of that business. Saying so, and then asking what underlying growth was on a like-for-like basis, will land better than the headline. Second, ask about the service annuity. £16.84m of £45.83m is rendering of services, 86 of 155 staff are after-sales and technical, and on capital imaging that mix is the whole commercial model: you are selling a scanner once and a maintenance contract for a decade. Ask how the sales team is measured across the two. Third, ask about 31 March 2028. Nine of the twelve NHS Supply Chain frameworks the Hub holds against Fujifilm expire on that single date, all awarded under one 2021 reference, so this is one renewal event covering nearly the whole NHS footprint rather than a rolling series of them. Anyone in a commercial role here will be working towards it. Two further pieces of context make you sound like an insider. This is the old Hitachi Medical Systems UK, renamed on 1 July 2021, so a candidate who knows the MRI and ultrasound heritage is not starting from Fujifilm cameras. And the going concern note calls the company a Limited-Risk Distributor with access to group cash pooling, which tells you the UK operating margin is largely a transfer-pricing outcome: pushing hard on price in the interview as though UK margin is locally controlled will read as naive. Finally, know the Aquilant story. Fujifilm Healthcare UK bought the endoscopy trade of Aquilant Endoscopy Limited on 1 December 2025, and the company itself has ceased to trade. Fujifilm is one of only five suppliers on the national Flexible Endoscopes framework. Asking how that acquisition is being integrated into the endoscopy field team is a question only someone who has read the filings can ask.
