background.heading: Ownership and parent
background.text: OWNERSHIP CHANGED AT THE HOLDING COMPANY ON 18 NOVEMBER 2025, AND NEITHER COMPANY HAS ANNOUNCED IT. Read at Companies House on 24/08/2026: the persons-with-significant-control register of Gama Healthcare Corporation Limited (10759004), the holding company above GAMA HEALTHCARE LTD, records the entries of Guy Braverman, Dr Allen Hanouka and Gama Investment Group Ltd (13805538) as ceased on 18 November 2025, and the entry of Deb Holdings Limited (04113118, of Denby Hall Way, Denby, Ripley, Derbyshire DE5 8JZ) as notified on the same day, holding 75% or more of the shares, 75% or more of the voting rights and the right to appoint or remove directors. Al Schretter was appointed a director of the holding company on 18 November 2025. Deb Holdings Limited's own PSC register names SC Johnson Professional Group Limited (04934334, previously DEB GROUP LIMITED, same Denby address) as holding 75% or more of its shares since 12 December 2017. So the register documents an unbroken chain of control from GAMA up to an SC Johnson entity. The register does not describe a transaction, no price or completion date is on file, and GAMA's own site says nothing about it, so the publishable facts are the dated register entries and the chain they form — not a deal. The 'private, founder-led, no outside owner' framing is out of date; both founders remain directors of both companies and are named Joint CEO on GAMA's own About us page. Full sourcing is in this record's deepDive. Vascular access tag clarification: GAMA makes no vascular access devices itself, but its HEXI brand (HEXI PREP skin antisepsis before cannulation, HEXI HUB for catheter-hub disinfection) supports vascular access procedures — the tag reflects skin and site antisepsis, not device manufacture, and GAMA's own product navigation carries Vascular Access as one of its use cases.

deepDive.tagline: The UK infection-prevention manufacturer behind Clinell: £70.3m of turnover in the year to 31 March 2025, six NHS Supply Chain frameworks, a commercial team it has halved in two years, and a change of control at its holding company on 18 November 2025 that neither it nor its new owner has announced.

links.label: Holding company: Gama Healthcare Corporation Limited (10759004)

deepDive.lede: Three things, and the first one is not on GAMA's website. On 18 November 2025 the persons-with-significant-control register of the holding company, Gama Healthcare Corporation Limited (10759004), recorded the entries of Guy Braverman, Dr Allen Hanouka and Gama Investment Group Ltd as ceased, and the entry of Deb Holdings Limited (04113118) as notified the same day with 75% or more of the shares, 75% or more of the voting rights and the right to appoint or remove directors; Al Schretter was appointed a director of that company on the same date. Deb Holdings' own PSC register names SC Johnson Professional Group Limited (04934334, formerly DEB GROUP LIMITED) as its 75%-plus owner since 12 December 2017. That is a documented chain of control from GAMA up to an SC Johnson entity. It is not a transaction: the register records entries and dates, not deals, no price or completion date is on file, GAMA's own news page carries nothing about it and its most recent post is dated 22 May 2026, and SC Johnson's own newsroom page does not mention GAMA. Second, the commercial shape, which is the most useful thing in this record. The average monthly number of employees fell from 235 to 187 to 136 across the three years to 31 March 2025, and the people in Sales and marketing fell from 98 to 70 to 48 — a little over half the commercial team gone in two years — while turnover went £63.3m, £61.8m, £70.3m and the company swung from an £8.3m loss before tax in FY2023 to £13.3m of profit before tax in FY2025. The directors' own explanation is a strategic review and an employee restructuring programme in March 2024, after hiring through COVID for growth that, in their words, did not materialise. Third, the UK is two thirds of this company but not most of its growth: of the £8,578,666 turnover increase in FY2025, £3.93m was the United Kingdom and £4.65m was Rest of Europe and Rest of the world. Both founders are still directors and are still named Joint CEO on the company's own About us page.

Prior year £61,754,034. The strategic report on page 1 states the increase in its own words: "the Company saw an increase in turnover by £8,578,666 to £70,332,700 (2024 - £61,754,034), an increase of 13.9%".

The strategic report on page 1 attributes it: "Following the strategic review undertaken by the group in March 2024, including an employee restructuring program, the company has seen a positive turnaround in its profitability." The tax charge was only £212,109 on £13.3m of profit, because a £1,040,066 current tax charge was met by an £827,957 deferred tax credit; note 12 on page 25 also shows a £315,008 patent box deduction in the reconciliation. Dividends were £Nil in both FY2025 and FY2024 (directors' report, page 4).

Note 8 of the 2024 accounts, page 23, gives the FY2023 column: Directors 2, Operating 47, Administrative 9, Finance, Legal and IT 24, Sales and marketing 98, Research and development 38, Others 17, total 235. So Sales and marketing went 98, 70, 48 and the whole company went 235, 187, 136.

Exceptional items tell the same story from the other side: note 13 of the 2025 accounts gives redundancy costs of £191,643, one-off leasehold renegotiation fees of £65,080 and a one-off supplier payment of £54,000; the FY2024 note gives redundancy costs of £2,010,883, one-off consulting costs of £367,318 and a dilapidation provision of £400,000.

prose: The margin moved more than the revenue did. Gross profit was £32,782,899 on £70,332,700 of turnover in FY2025 against £24,610,107 on £61,754,034 in FY2024, so the gross margin went from 39.9% to 46.6% — both percentages computed here from the two figures on page 10 of the respective filings, neither published by the company. Cost of sales barely moved (£37,549,801 against £37,143,927) while turnover rose £8.6m. Administrative expenses fell from £22,065,123 to £19,588,358. And FY2024's loss was substantially not trading: note 5 shows the change in fair value of financial instruments cost £2,455,457 in FY2024 against £131,598 in FY2025, and the 2024 strategic report says foreign currency contracts "reduced profit by £2.3m (2023 – £1.9m)".

Two details worth knowing before a meeting. The directors are paid almost nothing through this company: note 9 gives directors' emoluments of £23,078 plus £468 of pension contributions for FY2025 (FY2024 £22,559 and £431), with retirement benefits accruing to 2 directors. And the company earns from the group as well as from customers: note 10 shows £174,000 of interest receivable from group companies in FY2025 (FY2024 £197,000), and note 27 on page 32 lists balances with GAMA Healthcare (Foshan) Limited, GAMA Investment Group Ltd, Braver Investment Group Limited, Braver Property Group Limited, Han Group Limited and Han Property Limited, the last of which the company owed £1,100,000 at the year end (FY2024 £Nil). Note 27 also records £1,358,140 owed to the company by AGA Nanotech Limited, a company with common directors, against which a provision of the full £1,358,140 has been booked.

ownership: GAMA HEALTHCARE LTD, company number 05316871, registered office The Maylands Building, Maylands Avenue, Hemel Hempstead Industrial Estate, Hemel Hempstead, England, HP2 7TG, is a private limited company incorporated on 20 December 2004 and currently Active. Its one previous name, from the register's own table read 24/08/2026, is GUY ALLEN WIPES LIMITED (20 December 2004 to 18 April 2005) — the founders are Dr Guy Braverman and Dr Allen Hanouka. Its SIC codes on the register are 86101 hospital activities and 86210 general medical practice activities, which describe neither manufacture nor wholesale and should not be used to categorise this company; the holding company's SIC is 32500, manufacture of medical and dental instruments and supplies, which does.

The persons-with-significant-control register of the trading company, read 24/08/2026, holds one active entry: Gama Healthcare Corporation Limited, company 10759004, incorporated in England and Wales at the same Hemel Hempstead address, notified 1 August 2017, holding 75% or more of the shares, 75% or more of the voting rights and the right to appoint or remove directors. The two ceased entries are Dr Allen Hanouka (notified 12 June 2016, ceased 1 August 2017) and Mr Guy Braverman (notified 12 April 2016, ceased 1 August 2017). So the interesting register is one level up, and that is where it moved.

The chain of control, as the register records it on 24/08/2026, and stated as entries and dates rather than as a transaction. GAMA HEALTHCARE LTD (05316871) is 75%-plus held by GAMA HEALTHCARE CORPORATION LIMITED (10759004, incorporated 8 May 2017, previously GAMA CORPORATION LIMITED until 27 December 2018). That company's PSC register records Deb Holdings Limited (04113118, of Denby Hall Way, Denby, Ripley, Derbyshire DE5 8JZ) as notified on 18 November 2025 with 75% or more of the shares, 75% or more of the voting rights and the right to appoint or remove directors, and records the entries of Mr Guy Braverman, Dr Allen Hanouka and Gama Investment Group Ltd (13805538) as ceased on that same date. Deb Holdings Limited's own PSC register names SC Johnson Professional Group Limited (04934334, incorporated 16 October 2003, previously DEB GROUP LIMITED and before that DUALWISE GROUP LIMITED, at the same Denby address) as holding 75% or more of its shares, notified 12 December 2017. Every link in that chain is a PSC entry read at source with its own notification date. What the register does not carry is a transaction: no price, no completion date, no announcement. The evidence floor applied here is that a chain of PSC entries may be published as a chain of PSC entries, and nothing beyond that is asserted.

Neither company has said anything publicly, as far as this session could check. GAMA's own website — the homepage, the About us page, the Latest news index and the Careers page, all read 24/08/2026 — contains no mention of SC Johnson, Deb or a change of ownership, and the most recent item on its news index is dated 22 May 2026. SC Johnson's own newsroom page at scjohnson.com does not mention GAMA. That is four company pages and one newsroom page, not an exhaustive search of either company's communications, and it is stated that narrowly on purpose.

The filed accounts are now out of date on ownership, and a reader who checks them will be misled. Note 29 on page 33 of the accounts for the year ended 31 March 2025 says: "The immediate and ultimate parent undertaking is GAMA Healthcare Corporation Limited, a company incorporated in England and Wales", and "There is no ultimate controlling party." That was true when the board approved those accounts on 9 September 2025 and remained the position on 18 September 2025 when they were filed. Note 28 records no post balance sheet events, correctly: the PSC change is dated two months after the accounts were signed. The next filing, for the year to 31 March 2026, is the one that will carry it.

One dated sequence in the charges register, offered as a sequence and not as a cause. The register shows 12 charges, 4 outstanding and 8 satisfied, read 24/08/2026. Three long-standing HSBC securities were satisfied on 26 August 2025 — a debenture created 28 December 2012, a legal mortgage over freehold property created 6 April 2017, and a freehold charge over Sovereign House, 2 Regal Way, Watford created 28 April 2015 — and a 2013 legal assignment of contract monies was satisfied on 9 September 2025. A new charge, 0531 6871 0013, described as security over cash deposits in favour of HSBC UK Bank PLC, was created on 11 August 2025 and delivered on 22 August 2025, and is outstanding. So the company cleared its historic secured borrowing in the twelve weeks before the PSC change. The register does not say why, and nothing here says the two are connected; the rule applied is that dated filings may be listed in date order and the reader may draw their own conclusion.

marketPosition: The framework footprint is the independently checkable part, and it has just been renewed. NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs name this company on six frameworks, captured for this Hub on 24/08/2026 and listed with their dates, references and supplier counts on the framework panel of this record rather than restated here: Aids for Daily Living, Cleaning Equipment, Supplies and Associated Products, Environmental Decontamination, Hand Hygiene and Associated Products and Services, Skin Cleansing, Disinfection and Hygiene, and Wipes for Surface Cleaning and Disinfection. The briefs name it variously as "GAMA Healthcare Ltd" and "Gama Healthcare Ltd". Three of the six started in 2026 — Skin Cleansing, Disinfection and Hygiene on 16 February 2026, Environmental Decontamination on 30 March 2026 and Wipes for Surface Cleaning and Disinfection on 6 July 2026 — so the core positions were all re-competed and re-won within the last six months.

Where the field is small, the place is worth more, and GAMA's narrowest framework is its flagship one. On the briefs captured, it is one of 13 suppliers on Wipes for Surface Cleaning and Disinfection (6 July 2026 to 5 July 2029), one of 21 on Hand Hygiene and Associated Products and Services, one of 22 on Environmental Decontamination and one of 29 on Skin Cleansing, Disinfection and Hygiene. The wider two are Aids for Daily Living (31 suppliers) and Cleaning Equipment, Supplies and Associated Products (60). Those counts are the briefs' own and are recorded per framework on this record. No claim is made here about lot coverage or about being any customer's incumbent: a brief names suppliers on a framework and says nothing about volume.

One derived observation, with its rule stated so it can be judged. Dividing total company turnover by the average monthly number of employees in the Sales and marketing category in note 8 of the same filing gives roughly £0.65m per commercial head in FY2023 (£63,276,833 over 98), £0.88m in FY2024 (£61,754,034 over 70) and £1.47m in FY2025 (£70,332,700 over 48). That is a ratio computed here from two figures in the same set of accounts, is not a figure the company publishes, and says nothing about any individual's quota — note 4 shows a third of turnover is earned outside the United Kingdom and some of it will not pass through a UK field team at all. What it does say is that this business got materially more revenue per commercial head over two years while cutting that team in half, which is the context any conversation about resourcing, territory size or service expectations now sits inside.

On the product range: this Hub holds no own-site product capture for GAMA Healthcare, and no refusal either, because until this record was written the supplier index carried no website for the company at all and the crawler's eligibility test only reaches suppliers with a domain recorded. That is a gap in this Hub's coverage and not a fact about the company. The curated product list on this record — the Clinell surface, hand and sporicidal ranges, Clinell CHG skin wipes and shampoo caps, HEXI PREP and HEXI HUB, Clinell Contiplan, Carell, Cleanall, Rediroom and Rediair — was confirmed against NHS Supply Chain listings under GAMA HEALTHCARE LTD on 20/07/2026 and is unchanged. GAMA's own site groups the same range by use case as Everyday Decontamination, Enhanced Decontamination, Skin Health Hygiene and Integrity, Vascular Access, Body Decolonisation, Environmental Risk Reduction and Training and Evaluation Solutions.

Manufacturing and research sit outside Hemel Hempstead, and the company says so itself. Its About us page names three locations — the UK head office in Hemel Hempstead, the Fellows Research Centre in Halifax, and a China office with divisions for new product development, production and operations — while the careers page adds Spain ("Not only are we in the UK, but also China and Spain!"). The FY2025 strategic report calls the Halifax site a "state-of-the art Science and Innovation centre". The accounts also show a Chinese subsidiary, GAMA Healthcare (Foshan) Limited, in note 27, and the careers page quotes the CEO of GAMA Healthcare Australia saying that business "operates as a separate business" — so an Australian enquiry is not this legal entity's to answer.

deepDive.interview: Know the ownership before you walk in, and be careful how you use it. The register shows that on 18 November 2025 control of the holding company moved to Deb Holdings Limited, whose own 75%-plus owner is SC Johnson Professional Group Limited, and that an American director, Al Schretter, joined the holding company's board that day. GAMA has announced none of this and SC Johnson's newsroom does not mention GAMA, so treat it as register-documented and not as public knowledge: "I saw the PSC filings" is a fair thing to say, "I read about the SC Johnson deal" is not, because there is nothing to have read. What it tells you is that a founder-owned business now sits inside a large corporate group, that capital allocation and reporting lines will change even if the brand does not, and that anyone telling you this is still a private founder-led company is working from an out-of-date picture — including the filed accounts, whose note 29 still says there is no ultimate controlling party. Both founders are still directors and still named Joint CEO. Do not congratulate them on the growth without knowing the shape of it. Turnover went £63.3m, £61.8m, £70.3m, and the middle year was, in the directors' own words, a 2.4% fall "due to overstocking" after hiring through COVID for growth that did not come. What produced the £13.1m FY2025 profit was as much cost as revenue: the average monthly headcount fell from 235 to 136 in two years, Sales and marketing from 98 to 48, staff costs from £13.9m to £11.7m, and the gross margin went from 39.9% to 46.6%. The people you meet have been through a restructuring that cost £2.4m in redundancies in FY2024 and another £191,643 in FY2025. Ask what the commercial team covers now, not how it is growing. Two things that will make you sound like you have read the accounts. First, a third of this company is not the UK: £47.2m of £70.3m was the United Kingdom in FY2025, and more than half of the year's £8.6m increase came from Rest of Europe and Rest of the world, so a UK-only conversation is a conversation about two thirds of the business. Second, they take no cash out — dividends were £Nil in both FY2025 and FY2024 and directors' emoluments were £23,078 — which is the opposite of the Steris picture in this Hub and means a reinvestment case does not have to clear a dividend. On frameworks: three of their six NHS Supply Chain frameworks started in 2026, including Wipes for Surface Cleaning and Disinfection on 6 July 2026 with only 13 suppliers on it. They have just re-won the position their brand is built on, so this is a confident supplier in its core category, not a defensive one. And on route in: the statutory board is only the two founders, so the Chief Commercial Officer named on their own About us page is the commercial door, and the two open Account Development Manager vacancies — North London/Herts/Essex and South Yorkshire/Lincolnshire — tell you where they are putting field cover right now.

deepDive.lede: The story to know here: GBUK spent nearly a decade under one private equity owner (H2 Equity Partners, from 2016), then changed hands again in December 2023 when A&M Capital Europe took majority control. Since then it's bought three companies in under 18 months and been through a genuine changing of the guard at board level, with two long-serving directors and the company secretary all departing within the last year. This is a business mid-transformation, not a steady state, and that's exactly the kind of thing worth asking about in an interview.

prose: Filed accounts at Companies House show turnover climbing from £44m in the year to June 2019 to £74.8m in the year to June 2024, alongside £30.6m in net assets and £14.3m cash. Employee headcount in those same FY2024 accounts was 147, though that figure predates the three acquisitions made since, so the group is materially larger today than the last filed numbers show. Full accounts for the year to June 2025 were filed on 11 July 2026; the FY2025 figures have not yet been extracted from that document.

The real growth story since December 2023 has been acquisitive rather than organic: Care & Independence (patient handling, the first deal under new ownership), Severn Healthcare Technologies (added two new therapeutic areas), and GS Medical Limited (an Irish single-use device distributor spanning endoscopy, announced January 2025). GBUK also launched a new international arm, GBUK Global, alongside a dedicated global website, signalling an explicit push beyond the UK and Ireland.

ownership: Ultimate control sits with Enhancing Patient Care Limited, the UK holding vehicle A&M Capital Europe (AMCE) used to buy 75%+ of GBUK Group Limited in December 2023, from previous owner H2 Equity Partners. AMCE is a London-headquartered, middle-market private equity firm with around €650m under management; GBUK was its seventeenth transaction, advised by Weil Gotshal & Manges, Houlihan Lokey, Boston Consulting Group and EY among others, which tells you this deal had serious institutional backing behind it.

Underneath the holding company sits the original operating business, GBUK Ltd (trading since 2004), plus a cluster of subsidiaries built up over the years including GBUK Enteral, Intervene, R&J Medical and Blue Box Medical, alongside brands like It's Interventional and Frontier Medical Group. The three post-2023 acquisitions sit alongside these, with endoscopy added via GS Medical.

press.text: A&M Capital Europe announces its majority investment in GBUK Group, buying out H2 Equity Partners. GBUK continues under Mike Geering's leadership, with AMCE backing a stated strategy of bolt-on acquisitions in the UK, Europe and North America.
Three bolt-on acquisitions in quick succession: Care & Independence, Severn Healthcare Technologies, and GS Medical Limited, each announced as strengthening a specific therapeutic area or geography.

Notable board turnover: long-serving director Peter Spiller resigns (November 2025), followed by another director (February 2026), continuing a reshuffle that began with the company secretary's departure in January 2025.

hiring: GBUK doesn't publish a rolling count of roles filled, and its own careers page shows no live vacancies at the time of this check, so treat hiring as something that moves in bursts, likely tied to the acquisition integrations, rather than a steady drip. Recent live postings tracked via Indeed have skewed operational: warehouse, quality and supply chain roles based at Selby, rather than field sales.

The closest verifiable proxy is its own claim to be a top 20 supplier to the NHS and its stated position as a market leader in specific clinical niches, which is a company claim rather than an independently audited number.

deepDive.interview: This isn't a household name, it's a mid-size, PE-backed specialist mid-integration of three recent acquisitions, so ask about how those are bedding in. Know which of the group's therapeutic areas the role sits in. It's fair game to ask about the board changes and what AMCE's growth plans look like from here.

deepDive.tagline: Nasdaq: GEHC, no GE shareholding left since 2024 · UK legal entity GE Medical Systems Limited (00252567), UK head office Pollards Wood, Chalfont St Giles
deepDive.lede: The thing worth knowing before this interview: on 29 July 2026 GE HealthCare told the market it is "reviewing strategic options" for Patient Care Solutions — the segment that holds anaesthesia machines, ventilators, patient monitoring and maternal-infant care. That is not a side business as far as the NHS is concerned. It is the half of GE that sits on most of the 20 NHS Supply Chain frameworks this supplier is named on, including Anaesthesia Machines and Ventilators, Patient Monitoring, Pulse Oximetry and Capnography, and Respiratory Solutions. In the same quarter the company merged Imaging and Advanced Visualization Solutions into one segment, Advanced Imaging Solutions, and its CFO announced he was leaving. So you are walking into a company posting record orders and backlog that is simultaneously redrawing its own org chart, and if the role sits in PCS rather than imaging, ask about it. "Reviewing strategic options" is the company's own phrase, and it does not commit them to selling anything.

prose: No UK-only turnover figure is published here. GE Medical Systems Limited files full accounts at Companies House and its most recent set covers the year ended 31 December 2025, filed on 12 July 2026 and running to 175 pages, following a 176-page set for 2024 filed on 20 August 2025. Those accounts have not been read: this run had no Companies House API key, and picking a turnover line off a filing by position is a guess about which number is turnover. Whether the filing carries a machine-readable profit and loss account is therefore unknown rather than ruled out, and the accounts-figures step of the Monday company-intelligence workflow is what settles it. Every figure below is group-wide and as filed by GE HealthCare Technologies Inc., not derived and not UK-specific.

The group trajectory is steady rather than dramatic: $19.6bn in FY2023 (up 7%), $19.7bn in FY2024 (up 1%, a flat year the company attributed largely to China), then $20.6bn in FY2025, up 4.8% reported and 3.5% organic, with growth in Imaging, Pharmaceutical Diagnostics and Advanced Visualization Solutions and strength specifically called out in the US and EMEA. Q2 2026 continued that: $5.3bn, up 5.7%, book-to-bill above 1 and record backlog. FY2026 guidance is 3.0% to 4.0% organic revenue growth and adjusted EPS of $4.80 to $5.00, reaffirmed with the Q2 2026 results on 29 July 2026.

For a UK conversation the useful framing is that this is a mid-single-digit grower buying its way into software: $2.3bn on Intelerad in March 2026 for cloud-first enterprise imaging, aimed at specialist clinics and ambulatory care rather than the big hospital installed base it already holds. That is directly relevant to any NHS diagnostic-hub or community-diagnostics conversation.

ownership: GE HealthCare Technologies Inc. was spun out of General Electric on 3 January 2023 and listed on Nasdaq as GEHC. GE retained a minority stake at spin-off and sold it down in stages; GE — by then renamed GE Aerospace — completed its exit of the entire remaining holding in November 2024. There is no residual GE ownership. The GE brand is used under a trademark licence, which is why the company's own UK pages still carry the line "GE is a trademark of General Electric Company. Used under trademark license." A rep who describes GE HealthCare as part of GE is three years out of date, and it is the sort of thing an interviewer notices.

The UK operating entity is GE Medical Systems Limited, company number 00252567, incorporated 8 December 1930, registered office Pollards Wood, Nightingales Lane, Chalfont St. Giles, Buckinghamshire HP8 4SP — the same address the company gives as its UK head office. Its person with significant control is recorded at Companies House as GE UK Holdings, per a PSC05 filed 1 November 2023 for a change of details dated 28 April 2023. The full current PSC entry could not be read in this session: the Companies House PSC page returned empty on three attempts. Treat the intermediate UK holding layer as Not verified until that page is read; the operating entity, its number and its officers are confirmed.

Several other GE-named UK companies exist on the register and are easy to confuse with this one, including GE HEALTHCARE LIMITED (01002610, the former Amersham plc line), GE HEALTHCARE UK LIMITED (03337033) and GE HEALTHCARE CLINICAL SYSTEMS (UK) LIMITED (01334654). NHS Supply Chain's briefs name "GE Medical Systems Ltd" or "GE Medical Systems Limited" on 17 of the 20 frameworks, "GE Healthcare" on two and "GE" on one, so 00252567 is the entity that matters for framework work.

press.text: Completes the acquisition of Intelerad for a base price of $2.3bn in cash. Cloud-first enterprise imaging and workflow, aimed at specialist clinics and ambulatory care alongside the existing hospital installed base. Expected c.$270m revenue in the first full year, c.90% recurring, adjusted EBITDA margin above 30%.

Nuffield Health and GE HealthCare open an AI-enabled diagnostic imaging hub in Oxford serving both NHS and private patients, under the £200m collaboration the two announced in January 2024 to install close to 800 pieces of imaging, ultrasound, surgical and x-ray equipment across the Nuffield network. The clearest current example of GE's UK route to market outside trust capital tenders.

Q2 2026 results. Revenue $5.3bn, up 5.7% (3.5% organic), record orders and backlog with organic order growth in every segment. Imaging and Advanced Visualization Solutions merged into a new segment, Advanced Imaging Solutions, taking the company to three reportable segments. The company states it is reviewing strategic options for Patient Care Solutions while working to return it to growth and profitability.

CFO Jay Saccaro notified the company he was resigning, for a role outside the medical technology industry. His last day was 14 August 2026, so he has already gone. On 23 July the company named George Newcomb, its Controller and Chief Accounting Officer, as interim CFO effective 14 August 2026, and began a search for a permanent successor. Recorded in the Form 8-K filed 23 July 2026, not in the Q2 results release.

hiring: UK roles were visible at Chalfont St Giles at the time of this check, including a Global Digital Strategy and Projects Lead and a UK Medical Strategy Director, both listed on GE HealthCare's own careers site against the HP8 4SP postcode. No salary figures were published on those listings and none are stated here. This is a small sample surfaced by search rather than a full vacancy count, so read it as evidence the UK site is hiring, not as a measure of how much.
marketPosition: GE HealthCare's UK position is best evidenced by its framework footprint rather than by any market-share figure, and no verified market-share percentage was found in this session, so none is stated. It is a named supplier on 20 NHS Supply Chain frameworks confirmed against the briefs, spanning CT, MRI, ultrasound, mammography, fluoroscopy, nuclear medicine, mobile and static x-ray, bone densitometry, mobile image intensifiers, angiography and hybrid theatres, anaesthesia and neonatal equipment, patient monitoring, pulse oximetry and capnography, cardiac and pulmonary diagnostics, respiratory solutions, bladder scanners, electrodes and consumables, digital diagnostic solutions and total patient assessment. That is a genuinely unusual spread: most of the suppliers with comparable framework counts are consumables distributors, not capital-equipment manufacturers.

A practical caveat carried from this Hub's earlier catalogue work: an NHS Supply Chain check found no direct GE capital-equipment listings for CT, MRI, ultrasound or anaesthesia. That class of equipment is bought through trust tender and negotiation, not off the public catalogue. Framework presence means eligibility to be bought, not availability to order — worth being precise about in an interview, because getting it wrong signals someone who has read a list rather than sold anything.

Three other UK sites: Hatfield (learning centre and repair centre for Life Care Solutions and Ultrasound, 61 Great North Road AL9 5EN), Amersham (Pharmaceutical Diagnostics), and Lisburn, Lissue Industrial Estate BT28 2RF, covering sales and service in Northern Ireland.

deepDive.interview: Three things will make you sound like you have done the work. First, know that GE HealthCare is a standalone Nasdaq company and has been since January 2023, with GE fully out since November 2024 — it is not a division of GE. Second, know which segment the role sits in: Advanced Imaging Solutions is the newly merged, growing half; Patient Care Solutions is the half under a stated strategic review, and it is also the half that carries most of the NHS Supply Chain framework presence. Asking a calm, non-loaded question about what the review means for UK customers is fair game and shows you read the results, not the careers page. Third, be precise about route to market: capital imaging goes through trust tender and negotiation, the frameworks establish eligibility, and the Nuffield Health collaboration shows the private and diagnostic-hub route running alongside. If the role touches diagnostic hubs or community diagnostics, the Intelerad acquisition is the thing to bring up, because it is exactly a bet on imaging outside the acute hospital.

deepDive.lede: GenX MediCare Ltd (company number 09614874) is registered at 248 Lockwood Road, Huddersfield, with one director and sole person with significant control, Shabaz Khalil Ahmed. Its website, last confirmed live December 2023, showed a narrow catalogue: airway management tubes, enteral feeding and rectal tubes (GenX Ryles Tube, GenX Rectal Tube), and a handful of obstetrics and gynaecology disposables. Its accounts tell an equally small story: average headcount was zero to 31 March 2023, rising to one in each of the two most recent years; net assets grew from £2,240 (year to 31 March 2020) to £111,310 (year to 31 March 2025), but no turnover has appeared in any filing since at least 2021, under the small companies' exemptions. Against that, NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs name the company on eleven national frameworks awarded 2022–2025, several well outside its stated range, including total orthopaedic solutions, infusion pumps, and electrodes and defibrillation consumables. Expect a very small, tightly-held trading operation whose framework footprint outruns its balance sheet, headcount and current web presence, and ask what it actually supplies against each award.

prose: Net assets have grown roughly fifty-fold in five years, from £2,240 at 31 March 2020 to £111,310 at 31 March 2025, but the starting point was close to dormant: the company filed dormant-company accounts for its first two financial periods and had an average headcount of zero through to 31 March 2023. No profit and loss account has ever been filed, so nothing here says whether the company is trading profitably or simply retaining cash injected by its director; the FY2025 accounts show called-up share capital unchanged at £100 throughout, so the movement in reserves is the 'Profit and loss account' line, which rose from £91,216 to £111,210 over the latest year — consistent with, but not proof of, a trading surplus, since it could also reflect other equity movements not visible without the missing income statement.

The balance sheet shifted shape in the most recent year: stocks rose from £174,969 to £235,400 while cash at bank fell from £244,001 to £114,940 (Statement of Financial Position, accounts to 31 March 2025). One plausible reading is that cash was converted into inventory to support delivery against the frameworks won in 2024–2025 — this is inference, not a fact stated in the accounts, and is labelled as such.

The employee count is the sharpest single fact in the record: zero on average for every year to 31 March 2023, rising to one for the two most recent years, over exactly the period the company was being named on the bulk of its eleven NHS Supply Chain frameworks. A rep should treat the framework list as a procurement-eligibility footprint rather than evidence of operational scale.

ownership: GENX MEDICARE LTD, company number 09614874, is a private limited company incorporated in England and Wales on 29 May 2015 (Companies House, read 05/09/2026). It traded under its incorporation name, PRECISION SURGICARE LTD, until 14 May 2018, when a name change by special resolution dated 10 May 2018 was registered. The company was dormant at the outset: dormant-company accounts were filed for the periods to 31 May 2016 and 31 May 2017, and its accounting reference date was later shortened from 31 May to 31 March, effective from the 2018 financial year.

The registered office has been 248 Lockwood Road, Huddersfield, England, HD1 3TG since 11 May 2021 (Companies House form AD01). Before that date it was 10 Church Street, Paddock, Huddersfield, West Yorkshire, HD1 4TR — the same address given as the correspondence address of the company's first (resigned) director. Companies House records no filing before that showing a different address, but incorporation-era filings were not individually opened to confirm the address at 29 May 2015.

There is one person with significant control on the register: Mr Shabaz Khalil Ahmed, notified 29 May 2017, recorded as holding ownership of shares and of voting rights each in the 75% or greater band. No other PSC, and no corporate or trust PSC, is recorded. Called-up share capital has remained £100 (100 shares of £1) from incorporation through the year to 31 March 2025, the most recent filed accounts.

Two officer events are dated 23 June 2016: the appointment of Shabaz Khalil Ahmed as director, and the termination of the appointment of Khalil Shahrose Ahmed, who had been a director since incorporation on 29 May 2015. Companies House does not record succession and none is asserted here; nor is any family or other relationship between the two men stated in the public record.

No parent company, group undertaking or ultimate controlling party is disclosed in any filing read in this session; on the evidence available, GENX MEDICARE LTD appears to be an independent, single-director UK company. The FY2025 accounts carry an accountant's report (the company is exempt from audit, not merely from filing one) prepared by Myrtle Gund Ltd, whose address given in the accounts is 248 Lockwood Road, Huddersfield, HD1 3TG — the same address as the company's own registered office. The financial statements were approved by the director and signed by Shabaz Khalil Ahmed on 25 March 2026.

A Companies House company-name search for "genx" on 05/09/2026 returns exactly one company trading as a variant of "GenX Medicare": GENX MEDICARE LTD (09614874) itself. The other "GenX…" companies on the register at that date (GenX Accountants Ltd, GenX AI Limited, GenX Care Ltd, GenX Enterprises Ltd, and others) are unrelated businesses, registered separately, in different sectors and different UK cities. There is no second, similarly-named entity that could be confused with this one.

The register does not record succession, and none is asserted here. No relationship between the two men is stated in any source read. hiring: The company's own website could not be checked for a careers page today: genxmedicare.com does not load at all, and the live genxmedicare.co.uk is a single page carrying a footer and one Carbon Reduction Plan link, with no navigation and no careers page (both checked 05/09/2026). A full listing of every URL the Wayback Machine has ever crawled for genxmedicare.com (checked 05/09/2026) contains no page with 'career', 'job' or 'vacancy' in its address, and the site's last fully-archived content, from 11 December 2023, carried no careers or vacancies link in its main navigation. Given filed accounts showing an average headcount of one for each of the two most recent financial years, there is no basis in the public record for expecting an active recruitment pipeline; this should be confirmed directly with the company before an interview, not assumed from its NHS framework presence.
marketPosition: GenX MediCare Ltd's own site, in its 2021 'About Us' text (Wayback Machine capture, 16 January 2021) and its 'Our Mission' page (capture, 5 August 2020), describes itself as offering 'precision-made medical products' that are 'designed and manufactured' to improve clinical, surgical and patient safety outcomes, and states its products are 'certified to ISO 9001, ISO 13485, European Council Directive 93/42/EEC on medical devices' — a claim quoted here as the company's own disclosure and not independently checked against any certification register. Set against that self-description, the company's registered nature of business (SIC) on Companies House is 47190, 'Other retail sale in non-specialised stores', and 86900, 'Other human health activities' — classifications that describe a retail/wholesale trader, not a manufacturer. Whether GenX MediCare itself manufactures any product, or sources and rebrands product made by others, could not be established from any source read in this session.

The product range last seen live (Wayback Machine, most recent full crawl 11 December 2023; category listings captured 26 September 2022) sat in three categories only: Airway Management (18 products across four sub-ranges — Bougies & Stylets, Endobronchial Tube, Endotracheal Tube and Tracheostomy Tube, including a GenFLEX-branded endotracheal tube with a subglottic suction lumen), Enteral Feeding Tubes (four products: GenX Feeding Tube, GenX Levins Tube, GenX Rectal Tube, GenX Ryles Tube), and Obstetrics & Gynaecology (nine products: Amniotic Hook, CerviX Brush Endocervical Sampler, CerviX Cervical Spatula, CerviX Cervical Spoon, CerviX Endometrial Suction Curette, CerviX Sampling Brush, GynaSpec Vaginal Speculum, SoftGrip Umbilical Cord Clamp and UrinBag). No respiratory, urology, orthopaedic, infusion, electrode/defibrillation, endoscopy or medical-pulp product was ever listed on the site in any capture read.

Against that narrow catalogue, NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs name the company — as "Genx Medicare Ltd", "GenX MediCare", "GenX Medicare", "Gen X Medicare" or "GenX MediCare Ltd" depending on the brief — on eleven distinct frameworks, each opened and text-checked directly on 05/09/2026: Airway Management Products and Associated Equipment (2023/S 000-005729, 22 July 2024 to 21 July 2028, 54 suppliers, as 'Genx Medicare Ltd'); Electrodes, Ultrasound Gels, Defibrillation and Related Consumables (2023/S 000-030987, 1 February 2024 to 31 January 2028, 37 suppliers, as 'GenX MediCare'); Endoscopy, Endourology and Oncology Ablation Consumables and Associated Products (2024/S 000-029975, 1 October 2025 to 30 September 2027, 58 suppliers, as 'GenX MediCare'); Enteral Feeding, Bile Bags and Associated Products (2025/S 000-028317, 5 September 2025 to 13 July 2027, 19 suppliers, as 'GenX Medicare'); Infusion Pumps and Administration Sets and Associated Products (3 October 2022 to 30 September 2026, 27 suppliers, as 'GenX MediCare'); Maternity, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Sexual Health Products (2019/S 214-525123, 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2027, 57 suppliers, as 'Genx Medicare Ltd'); Medical Hollowware (2024/S 000-014263, 7 April 2025 to 6 April 2029, 8 suppliers, as 'GenX MediCare'); Medical Pulp, Macerators and Support Products (ITT_596, 3 July 2023 to 2 July 2027, 11 suppliers, as 'Gen X Medicare'); Respiratory Solutions (1 August 2022 to 15 June 2027, 37 suppliers, as 'Genx Medicare Ltd'); Total Orthopaedic Solutions 3 (2023/S 000-025037, 1 February 2024 to 30 January 2028, 106 suppliers, as 'GenX MediCare'); and Urology and Bowel Management (2023/S 000-011173, 21 February 2024 to 20 February 2027, 57 suppliers, as 'GenX MediCare Ltd').

In every one of the eleven briefs, GenX MediCare appears as a single name inside a flat, alphabetically-ordered list of the framework's awarded suppliers — the brief text gives no lot-level detail identifying which specific product or products within that framework the company actually supplies. That matters here more than usual: several of these frameworks (Total Orthopaedic Solutions 3, Infusion Pumps, Electrodes/Ultrasound Gels/Defibrillation, Endoscopy/Endourology/Oncology Ablation, Medical Pulp/Macerators) cover clinical categories with no visible overlap at all with the airway, enteral-feeding and obstetric/gynaecology disposables shown on the company's own site. Being named as an awarded supplier is a verified fact for each of the eleven frameworks; which lot, or how much of NHS trusts' spend under each framework actually flows to this company, is not shown by the briefs and is not asserted here. The most defensible reading — offered as inference, not as a sourced fact — is that GenX MediCare holds a small number of narrow consumable lots within each broad framework, rather than a wide presence across the framework's full clinical range.

The company's live web presence has a genuine gap that a rep should know before quoting the domain: as of 05/09/2026, genxmedicare.com serves a default Hostinger hosting-welcome page ('You Are All Set to Go!') behind a TLS certificate that expired 14 August 2025, not the company's real content, and the live site is genxmedicare.co.uk, a single page of about 3KB that carries the company name, a phone number, an email address on the dead .com domain, a trading address (Canal Mills, Hillhouse Lane, Huddersfield, HD1 1ED) different from the Companies House registered office, and one link, to a Carbon Reduction Plan page. That page offers the Cabinet Office's generic Schedule B9 guidance document rather than a completed plan of the company's own, and it is the only substantive content the company currently publishes anywhere. A Carbon Reduction Plan is a selection-stage requirement for bidding on in-scope public contracts, so the one thing the company keeps online is the one thing procurement asks for. The Wayback Machine's last full crawl of genxmedicare.com's real content is dated 11 December 2023, so the product range and self-description above are current only to that date; nothing found in this session shows what, if anything, has changed since.

Honest gaps: no manufacturing location, no production capacity, no current certification status, and no named commercial or sales contact beyond the sole director could be established from any source read. The phone number and email address printed on the archived site (+44 (0)330 133 2210, info@genxmedicare.com) were not tested and their current currency is not confirmed.

deepDive.interview: You're named on eleven separate NHS Supply Chain frameworks awarded between 2022 and 2025 — from airway management and enteral feeding through to total orthopaedic solutions, infusion pumps and defibrillation consumables — yet your filed accounts show an average headcount of one and net assets of £111,310 at 31 March 2025. Which lots do you actually hold on the frameworks that sit outside your stated product range of airway, enteral-feeding and obstetric/gynaecology disposables, and what share of that framework footprint is live business today? Your accounts are filed under the small companies' abridgement and audit exemptions, so there is no turnover or profit-and-loss figure in the public record for any year since at least 2021 — can you give a sense of actual trading scale? Your website at genxmedicare.com does not resolve at all today, while your email on that same domain still does, and genxmedicare.co.uk is a single page carrying a footer, a Huddersfield trading address different from your registered office, and one link, to Carbon Reduction Plan guidance — is the company migrating its web presence, and where should an NHS buyer go today for current product and contact information? Your own 2021 marketing described the company as designing and manufacturing precision medical products certified to ISO 9001 and ISO 13485, but your registered SIC codes are retail/wholesale rather than manufacturing — do you manufacture in-house, and if so where, or do you import and rebrand product made elsewhere? Stock on your balance sheet rose by more than a third between March 2024 and March 2025 while cash fell by more than half in the same period — is that inventory build tied to call-offs against specific frameworks, and which ones?

deepDive.tagline: Getinge Limited turned over £86.55m in the year to 31 December 2025 (up from £79.12m in 2024), selling, installing and servicing group-manufactured medical equipment across the UK on service and supply, not manufacturing anything itself.

deepDive.lede: Getinge Limited is the group's UK sales, installation and service company, not a manufacturer. Everything it sells is made by other Getinge AB group companies; the UK entity's own strategic report says so in as many words, every year. It turned over £86.55m in the year to 31 December 2025, up 9.4% on £79.12m in 2024, but gross margin fell to 22.2% from 24.4% as the mix shifted (operating lights and anaesthesia sales both dropped sharply while Life Science, driven by sterilisers, grew 35.1%). The company traded before as Maquet Limited (2004-2021) and, before that, ALM Taema/ALM Hospital Equipment, so the Maquet name on older contracts and the current Getinge name are the same legal entity, company number 02195291. A separate UK sales and service company, Getinge UK Limited, existed until its trade was absorbed into this one on 1 April 2021 and it has since been dissolved; there is no other live Getinge trading entity to confuse this one with. Getinge Limited's own immediate parent, Getinge Holding Ltd, is a UK-registered holding company, not a second trading operation. Average headcount was 288 in 2025 (166 service engineers, 122 sales and administrative staff), based at Chaddesden, Derby. The wider Getinge AB group, listed on Nasdaq Stockholm, reported worldwide net sales of SEK 34,969m for 2025.

prose: Turnover has grown every year bar one across this run, from £55.3m in 2020 to £86.6m in 2025, a rise of 56% over five years. Most of the step up between 2020 and 2021 (£55.3m to £69.7m) is not organic growth: the company's own strategic report for 2021 says the trade and assets of Getinge UK Limited, described as "the other Sales & Service entity in the UK", were transferred into Getinge Limited on 1 April 2021 as part of a UK simplification project, alongside a move onto SAP. The 2022 dip to £67.3m reflects the comparison year no longer benefiting from pandemic-era ventilator demand, which the 2021 report itself flags as an "extraordinary performance" unwinding.

Profitability has not tracked turnover in a straight line. Gross margin peaked at 25.9% in 2022 and 25.5% in 2023, then fell to 24.4% in 2024 and 22.2% in 2025. The 2025 strategic report attributes the mix shift to a 35.1% jump in Life Science (sterilisers and consumables) and 6.6% growth in Surgical Workflows, more than offset in profit terms by a 39.3% fall in operating-light sales and a 58.2% fall in anaesthesia within Acute Care Therapies; the same report also cites "the ongoing global supply chain challenges, exacerbated by the increase in energy prices and the impact of increased tariffs" as a live pressure. Operating margin has held close to 5.0% throughout 2021-2025 despite the gross-margin swings, implying distribution and administrative costs have been managed down as a share of sales.

Net assets fell from £10.65m to £8.57m in 2025 because a £6.0m dividend was paid to the parent against a profit for the year of only £3.9m — the second year running a dividend has exceeded profit (2024: £3.0m dividend against £2.9m profit). Debtor days rose (DSO 65.5 to 70.6 days) while inventory days fell; working capital days overall were broadly stable at 97.2 versus 99.7 the prior year. None of this points to distress — net current assets remained comfortably positive at £7.6m — but it does show the UK company upstreaming cash to its Getinge AB / Carl Bennet AB owners rather than retaining it.

ownership: Getinge Limited, company number 02195291, is a private limited company incorporated in England and Wales on 11 November 1987. Its registered office is Unit 3 Indurent Park, Andressey Way, Chaddesden, Derby, DE21 6YH (Companies House register, checked 05/09/2026); this matches the correspondence address given by all three current officers on the register. It was incorporated as WF 135 Limited, then ALM Hospital Equipment Ltd (1988-2000), ALM Taema Limited (2000-2001), ALM Hospital Equipment Limited (2001), Getinge Surgical Systems Limited (2001-2004) and Maquet Limited (2004-2021), before adopting its current name on 12 January 2021. That unbroken chain of previous names, confirmed on the live register, is the strongest identity evidence available and is the reason older NHS contracts and framework awards under the Maquet name and this company are the same legal entity.

The filed annual report and financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2025 (filed at Companies House 26 July 2026) print "Registered number: 02195291" on both the cover page and again beside the director's signature on the Statement of financial position, and name the same three directors — Duncan Macrae Normington, Amy Anne Rothwell and Cecilia Elenor Mellqvist — who appear as the company's active officers on the register today, alongside Avril Ann Forde, who resigned as a director on 28 February 2025 and is recorded as such in both the accounts and a Companies House TM01 filing dated 6 March 2025. Three of the four identity routes in this Hub's verification standard are therefore satisfied directly (previous names, the accounts' own stated registered number, and the accounts' directors matching the active register); the fourth, registered office printed on the face of the accounts, was not visible in the pages examined, though the officers' correspondence addresses on the register match the registered office exactly.

Note 23 to the FY2025 accounts, "Ultimate parent company and controlling party", states: "The immediate parent is Getinge Holding Limited, a company incorporated in the United Kingdom, with a 100% holding... The ultimate parent company and controlling party is Carl Bennet AB", and separately names "Getinge AB, Lindholmspiren 7A, P.O. Box 8861, SE-417 56 Göteborg, Sweden" as the parent of the smallest group preparing consolidated accounts. This is corroborated on the Companies House persons-with-significant-control register for 02195291, which shows Getinge Holding Limited (company number 02456321) as a PSC with ownership of 75% or more of shares (notified 17 February 2021) and Getinge AB (Swedish registration 556408-5032) as a PSC with more than 25% but not more than 50% (notified 30 June 2016, when the PSC register began) — a prior PSC entry for Maquet SAS of France, ceased 17 February 2021, tracks the same 2021 restructuring visible in the company's name change and Getinge UK Limited's trade transfer.

Getinge Holding Ltd (02456321), incorporated 29 December 1989 and previously named Getinge Industrier Holding UK Limited (1996-2002) and, before that, Arjo Holding Limited (1990-1996), is registered at the same Chaddesden, Derby address and carries SIC code 70100 ("activities of head offices"). It is a UK holding company, not a second trading or sales entity: this Hub record covers Getinge Limited, the operating company, and Getinge Holding Ltd's own accounts were not examined in this piece of research, so nothing is asserted about its balance sheet. A separate former operating company, Getinge UK Limited (01700190), was described in Getinge Limited's own 2021 strategic report as "the other Sales & Service entity in the UK" until its trade and assets were absorbed into Getinge Limited on 1 April 2021; it was later dissolved on 28 July 2026. A company search on "Getinge" at Companies House also surfaces several long-dissolved entities tied to the group's 2017/2018 demerger of its Arjo (patient-handling) business — Getinge Extended Care UK Limited and Getinge Production UK Limited (both dissolved 24 January 2023, formerly at the Boldon Business Park, Tyne & Wear site that is referenced as "vacant" and "formally exited" in Getinge Limited's own 2025 directors' report), Getinge IT Solutions Limited (dissolved 14 April 2026) and Getinge Disinfection Limited (dissolved 2015) — none of which are live today.

The FY2025 directors' report states: "Following a review of the Group's audit requirements, EY will be appointed as the company's auditor, replacing PricewaterhouseCoopers." PricewaterhouseCoopers therefore audited the FY2025 accounts; EY takes over from the next financial year. The FY2025 accounts were approved by the board and signed on its behalf by Cecilia Mellqvist, Director, on 15 July 2026, and filed at Companies House on 26 July 2026.

press.text: Getinge Limited's own strategic report for the year ended 31 December 2021 records that the trade and assets of Getinge UK Limited, "the other Sales & Service entity in the UK", were transferred into Getinge Limited on this date, alongside a migration onto SAP. Source: Getinge Limited FY2021 accounts, Companies House.

FDA "Letter to Health Care Providers: Safety and Quality Concerns with Getinge Cardiovascular Devices", naming the Cardiosave Hybrid and Rescue Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump and the Cardiohelp system/HLS Set. The letter states the FDA received 2,964 medical device reports on Cardiosave in the prior 12 months (15 involving serious injury or death) and 246 reports on Cardiohelp (33 involving serious injury or death), and recommended facilities consider transitioning to alternative devices where possible. Verified live at fda.gov, 05/09/2026.

FDA Class I recall (the most serious classification) of the Flow-c/Flow-e anaesthesia system on/off suction switch, manufactured by Getinge USA Sales Inc (formerly Maquet Critical Care AB) at Wayne, New Jersey: initiated 2 May 2022, posted 23 June 2022, 17 units across six US states, reason given as a potential crack in the switch preventing suction activation. Companies House / FDA record confirms this recall was terminated (closed) on 6 August 2024. Verified live at accessdata.fda.gov, 05/09/2026.

Getinge Limited's FY2025 directors' report records that notified body TÜV SÜD reinstated the CE mark for the Cardiosave Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump on this date, having been suspended since March 2024, leading to resumed UK deliveries in Q4 2025. Getinge AB's group 2025 Annual Report separately states European deliveries were pushed to Q2 2026 due to a delay in shipment of critical components.

Getinge AB's group 2025 Annual Report discloses a strategic decision to phase out the Surgical Perfusion product category (the HL40 heartlung machine, HCU40 heater-cooler unit and related consumables), reallocating resources to ECLS and Transplant Care, citing a global market share outside the US of 7% and limited market growth. Getinge Limited's own FY2025 accounts record the same intention as an "Events after the end of the reporting period" note. Source: Getinge AB 2025 Annual Report (published 26 March 2026) and Getinge Limited FY2025 accounts.

Getinge AB's 2025 Annual Report states that in February 2015 Getinge signed a Consent Decree with the US FDA covering four production units in the US and Germany over quality concerns; production units in Fairfield and Mahwah, US received further FDA warning letters in 2018-2019 following 2018 inspections; and in October 2022 the FDA expanded the Consent Decree to include Getinge's subsidiary Datascope over observations at its Wayne, New Jersey site from 2021-2022 inspections. The Annual Report itself headings this "Consent Decree with FDA - ongoing" and says Getinge has submitted and is working through an action/remediation plan. This is the group's own disclosure, not independently verified against FDA's own consent decree records in this research.

Getinge AB's 2025 Annual Report discloses an ongoing dispute with authorities in Brazil: settlement negotiations with the Brazilian Federal Prosecutor's Office (Ministério Público Federal) and the competition authority CADE, arising from government investigations into anti-competitive practices in the sale of medical devices, mainly to public hospitals, between 2004 and 2017. Source: Getinge AB 2025 Annual Report, "Dispute" section, published 26 March 2026.

hiring: Getinge's own careers portal (careers.getinge.com), checked 05/09/2026 with a United Kingdom location filter, listed live UK vacancies including four Field Service Engineer roles (Life Sciences, Surgical Workplaces, Endoscopy and Surgical Workflows specialisms) based in Derby, a Field Service Engineer - Surgical Workflows role in Leeds, a Clinical Account Manager - Cardiac Surgery and Vascular role in London, and Derby-based commercial/support roles (International Product Manager - Consumables, QRC Specialist UKI, Planning and Dispatch Manager, Solutions Sales Manager, Business Administrator).

The portal's own results counter showed a total that mixed in US postings alongside the UK ones when a UK filter was applied, so no reliable total UK vacancy count is quoted here — only the roles actually visible and clearly UK-located are listed above. The heavy weighting toward field service engineering matches the FY2025 accounts' own staff split (166 of 288 average employees are service staff).
marketPosition: Getinge Limited's own strategic report states its principal activity, unchanged across every filed year: "the sale, installation and service of medical equipment and supplies." The same report says plainly: "The Company's products are all manufactured by group companies which are committed to continuous improvement of product and service by investing heavily in research and development." The UK entity does not manufacture; it sells, installs and services equipment made elsewhere in the Getinge AB group, and all of its turnover "arises solely in the United Kingdom" (note 5 to the FY2025 accounts). Turnover splits into sale of goods (£61.0m in 2025) and servicing contracts (£25.5m).

On manufacturing location: Getinge AB's 2025 Annual Report names a manufacturing site in the town of Getinge, Sweden (the group's namesake town), and separately discusses production sites at Solna (Sweden), and in the US at Wayne (New Jersey), Merrimack (New Hampshire), Fairfield and Mahwah (the last two named in the FDA Consent Decree history). The Annual Report states "sales in the US are manufactured in the US. The remainder is mainly imported from Europe, which is the flow that is most affected by the tariffs" — implying UK and other non-US sales are predominantly sourced from Getinge's European manufacturing base, though no single UK-facing supply site is named in the material read for this record. All but one of the group's production facilities subject to the EU Medical Device Regulation had received their MDR certificate by the end of 2025, per the same report.

The stored Hub seed lists Getinge Limited as a named supplier on six NHS Supply Chain frameworks: Anaesthesia Machines, Ventilators, Neonatal Equipment and Phototherapy Systems (2 March 2026 - 28 February 2029, 25 suppliers, re-verified live on the NHS Supply Chain contract-launch brief 05/09/2026); Decontamination Capital Equipment, Endoscopy and Sterile Services (19 February 2025 - 18 February 2027, 20 suppliers); Digital Diagnostic Solutions (1 August 2025 - 31 July 2027, 54 suppliers); Instrument Decontamination and Accessories (22 May 2023 - 1 April 2028, 20 suppliers); Operating Theatres Equipment (12 April 2024 - 11 April 2028, 43 suppliers); and Perfusion Devices, Consumables and Associated Equipment (10 November 2025 - 9 November 2027, 9 suppliers). All were captured from NHS Supply Chain's own contract-launch briefs on 31/08/2026, with one re-checked live for this record; the remainder were not individually re-checked today. Because Getinge Limited is the only live UK trading entity in the group (see ownership), any framework award to "Getinge Limited" is not split with a sibling company — but a reader should note the accounts do not break out revenue by framework or NHS versus non-NHS customer, so the scale of NHS-specific trade within the £86.55m total cannot be stated.

Honest gaps: no UK-specific market-share figure exists or is quoted anywhere in this record (per the Hub's standing rule, none is asserted). Getinge Holding Ltd's own accounts were not opened, so nothing is said about the immediate parent's balance sheet. No single UK-facing manufacturing or distribution-centre address was found naming Getinge Limited's own warehousing arrangement (the FY2025 directors' report only mentions that "the vacant Boldon office and warehouse were formally exited during the year", i.e. a site closed, not the current one). UK commercial/sales leadership below main-board director level could not be verified.

deepDive.interview: Getinge's own FY2025 accounts show gross margin falling from 24.4% to 22.2% even as turnover grew 9.4% — worth asking directly what is driving that (the accounts point to a 39.3% fall in operating-light sales and a 58.2% fall in anaesthesia sales inside a shrinking Acute Care Therapies mix, against strong sterile-services growth). Ask what the phase-out of the Surgical Perfusion range (the HL40 heartlung machine and HCU40 heater-cooler) means in practice for existing UK customers still under service contract, and where resources are being redirected (the group names ECLS and Transplant Care). Ask about the current supply position on Cardiosave now that its CE mark has been reinstated (1 August 2025) and UK deliveries have resumed — is backlog demand still being worked through. Given the FY2025 accounts also disclose the auditor changing from PricewaterhouseCoopers to EY "following a review of the Group's audit requirements", it is fair to ask whether that review touched anything beyond the audit relationship. On the commercial side, with six live NHS Supply Chain framework listings spanning theatres, decontamination, perfusion and diagnostics, ask which of those frameworks the interviewer's own team actually sells against day to day, since the accounts give no framework-level revenue split. Finally, average headcount rose only from 284 to 288 while turnover rose 9.4%, worth asking how that productivity gain was achieved and whether it is sustainable.

deepDive.lede: This is a UK subsidiary that has been at the same Gloucestershire address, in one form or another, since 1989 — Managing Director Shabir Ahmed said as much in the company's own words when announcing a new purpose-built warehouse in 2023: "Greiner Bio-One Ltd having been based in the local area since we established a UK subsidiary in 1989." The registered company, GREINER BIO-ONE LIMITED (02734565), was itself incorporated in 1992 as Greiner Labortechnik Manufacturing Limited and has carried three names since, which is worth knowing before searching Companies House by the trading name alone. Its statutory accounts describe a business most people outside pathology and phlebotomy have never heard of by name but have very likely been touched by: VACUETTE evacuated blood collection tubes and sets, MiniCollect capillary tubes, and CELLSTAR cell culture plastics for laboratories, sold in the UK under a Preanalytics, BioScience and OEM structure that mirrors the group's own global divisions. The second thing worth knowing before an interview is live and ongoing: NHS Supply Chain's own Important Customer Notice 2802 records an MHRA-granted derogation, first issued in 2025 and still being updated as of 28 May 2026, covering specific VACUETTE blood collection product codes affected by what the notice calls "legacy stock that was manufactured prior to the MDR certification administrative error." One code, KFK593, is being run down to depletion and delisting. A candidate should be able to talk about what that means for a customer-facing conversation, not just recite the framework list.

ownership: GREINER BIO-ONE LIMITED, company number 02734565, was incorporated on 27 July 1992 and is active. It has carried three names: Greiner Labortechnik Manufacturing Limited from incorporation to 9 November 1993, Greiner Labortechnik Limited to 11 December 2000, and its current name since. Its registered SIC code is 46460, wholesale of pharmaceutical goods, which undersells what the company actually sells — blood collection devices and laboratory plastics — in the same way Essity UK Limited's paper-goods SIC code undersells its medical business; a Companies House industry search will not reliably surface this company. The registered office is Unit 2, Pear Tree Way, Stonehouse, Gloucestershire GL10 3XG, which the company's own gbo.com imprint page confirms as its trading address too, with VAT number GB556262827.

The company's own press material states it has traded in the UK, at or near this address, since 1989, six years before the company itself was incorporated under a different name — the 1989 date most likely refers to an earlier unincorporated or differently-structured UK presence and is recorded here as the company's own claim, not independently verified against a second source. The gbo.com site footer reads © 2026 Greiner Bio-One International GmbH, and the company's Modern Slavery and Compliance & Whistleblowing pages link out to greiner.com, the wider Greiner Group's own site, consistent with Greiner Bio-One being part of the Austria-headquartered Greiner Group. This record does not independently verify the ownership chain against a Companies House PSC filing or a Group set of consolidated accounts; that is Not verified and should be checked before quoting a parent entity name to a candidate.

This company is a full-category filer, which means its accounts carry a full profit and loss account rather than the abbreviated filing many small UK subsidiaries use — useful context when comparing it with the medtech subsidiaries in this Hub for whom no turnover line is available at all.

deepDive.peopleNote: Current officers per the statutory register as extracted into company-financials.json on 31/08/2026, not independently re-read from the Companies House officers page in this session. The register also shows a cluster of resignations on 31 December 2020: Jonathan Frank Richard Pearson (both Secretary and Director), Noel Christopher Ennett (Director) and Thomas Milligan Woods (Director), the same date Shabir Ahmed's predecessor as the sole listed director effectively cleared the board down to him. The company's own 2023 press release still names Jonathan Pearson as "UK Finance Director" and Noel Ennett as "UK Operations Director" two years after both resigned as statutory directors — a genuinely useful discrepancy for a candidate to be aware of: this company plainly separates a person's day-to-day job title from whether they sit on the UK board, so a LinkedIn or press title should not be read as a Companies House directorship, in either direction. No sales director, commercial lead or NHS account manager is named anywhere this session could verify; treat named UK commercial leadership as Not verified and check nearer interview date.

press.text: Greiner Bio-One UK announces a new purpose-built 53,500 sq ft warehouse and office facility at Stroudwater 13, Stonehouse, about 800m from the existing site, planned for completion by the end of 2023. Managing Director Shabir Ahmed is quoted; the company's own group CFO Thomas Scheurecker is pictured attending the groundbreaking alongside UK Finance Director Jonathan Pearson, UK Operations Director Noel Ennett, UK Marketing Manager Nick Rudge and Paula Dummer (then UK Operations and Finance Manager). Read from gbo.com's own press page.

NHS Supply Chain first issues Important Customer Notice 2802 on Greiner Bio-One Ltd blood collection products, the first of six dated updates through to 28 May 2026 on record on the notice's own page.

Most recent update to ICN 2802: the supplier has secured a further 6-month MHRA derogation extension covering 12 named VACUETTE blood collection product codes, attributed to legacy stock manufactured before an MDR certification administrative error. A 13th code, KFK593, is being sold through remaining stock only and will then be delisted. The notice states it will be updated again by 27 November 2026.
Shabir Hussain Ahmed resigns as a director on the Companies House register, having been appointed 9 November 2020.
Paula Elizabeth Dummer appointed director, the day after Ahmed's resignation.

marketPosition: The verifiable measure of this company's NHS position is its framework footprint: named supplier on 5 NHS Supply Chain frameworks per this Hub's seed record — Blood Collection Devices, Blood Draw Tools and Accessories, Intravenous Cannula and Associated Products, Laboratory Diagnostics/Point of Care Testing and Pathology Managed Services, and Syringes, Needles and Associated Products. The Blood Collection Devices brief (reference 2024/S 000-033791, live 13 October 2025 to 12 October 2027) was re-read directly on 04/09/2026 and confirms Greiner Bio-One Ltd as a supplier offering a National Pricing Matrix on that framework; the brief states the framework's own anticipated first-year spend at circa £61,000,000, circa £244,000,000 over its maximum term, across all suppliers on it — a framework-level figure, not this one company's revenue.

This Hub's NHS Supply Chain catalogue cache holds no National Product Codes recorded against this supplier, and there is no own-site product crawl on file either. Neither is evidence the company's catalogue presence is thin; it is evidence this Hub has not yet captured it, and both are worth closing in a future run.

The live operational detail worth carrying into an interview is ICN 2802, not the framework list. An MHRA derogation tied to an "MDR certification administrative error" on legacy stock has been running since January 2025 and was still being updated in May 2026, with one product code being run down to delisting. A candidate should expect NHS customers to ask about it directly and should know it is a supply/regulatory administration issue on specific product codes, not a quality recall across the VACUETTE range.
deepDive.interview: Two things to read before you go in, because neither is on the company's own marketing pages. First, the corporate history: this is not a company that arrived on an NHS framework recently — its own press material puts a UK presence back to 1989, and the registered company itself, incorporated in 1992 under a different name, has been at the same Stonehouse address (or 800m from it) throughout, moving into a purpose-built 53,500 sq ft facility completed in 2023. Second, the live regulatory issue: NHS Supply Chain's Important Customer Notice 2802 has been open since January 2025 and was still being updated in May 2026, covering an MHRA derogation on 12 named VACUETTE blood collection codes tied to an "MDR certification administrative error" on legacy stock, with a 13th code being run down to delisting. Knowing that notice exists, and being able to describe it accurately rather than vaguely, is a genuinely useful thing to walk in with for anyone selling into pathology or phlebotomy. On leadership, tread carefully: the company's own 2023 press piece names Shabir Ahmed as Managing Director and several named UK functional directors, but the Companies House register shows most of those people resigned as statutory directors back in December 2020, and Ahmed himself resigned as a director on 30 June 2026, with Paula Dummer — named in 2023 as UK Operations and Finance Manager — appointed the next day. None of that proves who runs the business day to day now; it proves the register and the job titles on the press page are not the same thing, and it is worth asking directly rather than assuming continuity either way.

deepDive.tagline: Family-owned Welwyn Garden City distributor trading since 1948, turnover £6.13 million for the year to 31 March 2025, down slightly on £6.17 million the year before (Companies House, filed 4 October 2025).
deepDive.lede: Henleys Medical Supplies Limited is a small, independent, family-owned distributor based in Welwyn Garden City, trading since 1948 and now run by the third generation of the Henley family. It does not manufacture; it distributes for around 33 third-party brands (FLAEM, Neotech, HEINE, Medin, Cardinal Health and others) plus its own house-branded line, across respiratory care, blood pressure and pulse oximetry, ECG, thermometry, ultrasound, neonatal and general medical consumables. Turnover has held close to £6.1-6.4 million for the last four years on file, but profit before tax has fallen from £708,729 in the year to March 2022 to £276,159 in the year to March 2025 as costs have outpaced sales. It carries no debt (all 15 registered charges are satisfied), holds £2.38 million cash, owns its freehold premises, and is named on nine current NHS Supply Chain frameworks, an unusually broad footprint for a company this size.
