prose: Turnover has been essentially flat for four years, moving in a narrow band between £6.13 million and £6.36 million: £6,276,495 (FY2022), £6,361,136 (FY2023), £6,170,628 (FY2024), £6,130,072 (FY2025). There is no growth story here; if anything the last two years show a small decline from the FY2023 peak.

The more telling trend sits below the turnover line. Gross margin has narrowed from 35.4% of turnover in FY2022 (£2,220,230 gross profit) to 33.2% in FY2025 (£2,033,903), while distribution costs and administrative expenses have both risen in cash terms even as turnover fell. The combined effect is a sharp fall in profit before tax: £708,729 (FY2022), £521,985 (FY2023), £405,079 (FY2024), £276,159 (FY2025), a drop of 61% over three years on turnover that moved by only a few per cent. (All figures: statements of comprehensive income, accounts for years ended 31 March 2023 and 31 March 2025.)

The balance sheet has stayed conservative throughout: net assets of £4.68 million at 31 March 2025 (£4.69 million a year earlier), £2.38 million cash at bank, freehold property carried at £1.06 million net book value, and no registered charges outstanding since November 2022. Dividends paid to the director-shareholders rose from £198,696 (FY2024) to £211,718 (FY2025) even as profit fell, drawing down retained reserves slightly (profit and loss account reserve: £4,342,056 to £4,333,377). Pension contributions rose from £138,064 to £183,509 over the same year (note 10, accounts to 31 March 2025).

None of this is disclosed as a strategic report; as a small company Henleys is not required to file one and does not, so there is no board commentary on why margins are compressing. A rep meeting this company should treat the margin trend, not the flat turnover, as the number worth asking about.

ownership: Henleys Medical Supplies Limited, company number 00452882, was incorporated in England and Wales on 21 April 1948. Companies House records no previous company names for this number. Its registered office was 'Brownfields, Welwyn Garden City, Herts, AL7 1AN' until an AD01 filed 18 September 2025 updated it to '39 Brownfields, Welwyn Garden City, England, AL7 1AN', the same site with the house number added; the company's own website (footer of the /terms page and the /contact page) independently states its registered office as Brownfields, Welwyn Garden City, and prints the registered number as 452882, matching Companies House. The accounts for the year ended 31 March 2025 are signed by 'D Turner, Director', matching Danielle Turner's active directorship on the Companies House register (appointed 6 April 2004). On the strength of the matching registered number, matching registered address, matching signing director, and the absence of any other UK-registered company sharing this exact name (a Companies House name search for 'Henley Medical' returns Henley Medical Aesthetics Limited, Henley Medical Writing Ltd and The Henley Medical Group Ltd, all separately incorporated 2013-2023 at unrelated addresses, none of which is this company), this record treats identity as established, not merely probable.

The company has two registered persons with significant control, both notified 6 April 2016: Mr Scott Henley and Mrs Danielle Turner, each recorded as holding 'more than 25% but not more than 50%' of shares and voting rights. Both filed PSC04 changes of detail on 29 September 2025 (a details update, not a change of stake). Because neither individual holds more than 50%, and because note 12 of the accounts for the year ended 31 March 2025 states in the directors' own words that 'In the opinion of the directors the company has no ultimate controlling party', this is independently confirmed as family-owned, not a subsidiary of any group, UK or overseas, and there is no parent company to report on.

The company's own /about page states it was founded in 1948 by Donald Henley, that Laurence Henley (his son) led the business from the 1970s, and that Scott Henley and Danielle Henley (now Turner) are the third generation now running it. This is consistent with, though not identical to, the Companies House officer record: Donald Frederick Henley was a director (appointed before 2 January 1991, resigned 31 March 1999, date of birth March 1920); Laurence Michael Henley remains an active director (appointed before 2 January 1991, date of birth November 1943); Scott Henley and Danielle Turner have both been active directors since 6 April 2004. Companies House records dated appointment and resignation events only; it does not record family relationships or the succession the website describes, so the generational narrative above is attributed to the company's own website, not to Companies House.
Share capital is unchanged year on year: 75,925 'A' ordinary shares of £1 (one vote each) and 92 'B' ordinary shares of £1 (no voting rights), £76,017 in total (note 13, accounts to 31 March 2025).

The accounts were audited by Hillier Hopkins LLP (Registered Auditor); the auditor's report was unqualified and signed on 24 September 2025 by Samuel Hodson BSc ACA as Senior Statutory Auditor (note 15, accounts to 31 March 2025). Both the accounts and the auditor's report were completed and signed the same day.

The website also names four territory managers (Emma Haigh, Andy Wright, Mark Rogers, Will Gill) covering the North of England, North Thames and East of England, Wales/West Midlands/South West, and South Thames and South Coast respectively, none of whom appear on the Companies House officer register, which only records directors and the secretary.

press.text: Henleys announced its appointment as official UK distributor for FLAEM, an Italian manufacturer of aerosol therapy and respiratory devices, launching three nebuliser models (HospiNeb, NebulAir+, AirMate), the FLAEM Airfeel Mucus Clearance Device, Airfeel IMT inspiratory muscle trainer, and a FLAEM suction range. Reported on the company's own news page, henleysmed.com/news/henleys-appoint-as-flaem-official-uk-distributor, read 05/09/2026.

Henleys announced its appointment as official UK distributor for Neotech, a US neonatal/paediatric intensive care device brand. Reported on the company's own news page, henleysmed.com/news/henleys-partner-with-neotech, read 05/09/2026.

Henleys announced an updated Medin nCPAP accessory, the medin-NC3 Sync & Connect, for neonatal non-invasive ventilation. Reported on the company's own news page, henleysmed.com/news/updated-medin-nc3-sync-connect-introduced-for-neonatal-niv, read 05/09/2026.

hiring: Henleysmed.com publishes no careers, jobs or vacancies page. Checked 05/09/2026: /careers, /jobs, /vacancies, /work-for-us and /join-us all return HTTP 404, and no such page appears in the site's own XML sitemap (page-sitemap.xml, read the same day, lists 26 pages, none of them careers-related). There is therefore no live vacancy to report, and no way to establish current headcount plans from the site.

The only route into the company shown on the site is the general contact channel: phone 01707 385 226 or email welcome@henleysmed.com (henleysmed.com/contact, read 05/09/2026). The site does not name a recruitment contact, does not describe benefits or working conditions, and gives no indication of whether it is currently hiring.
marketPosition: Henleys is a distributor, not a manufacturer. Its own /about page states this directly: it 'functions as a distributor rather than manufacturer' and its business model is a UK-wide sales team selling an 'extensive catalogue of both technical and non-technical products and services', supported by clinical specialists who provide training. The company's /brands page lists around 33 manufacturer brands it distributes for, including FLAEM, Neotech, HEINE, Medin, Cardinal Health, DeRoyal, KaWe, Parker Laboratories, PDI, Salter Labs and Sony, alongside its own house-branded line. This is a multi-brand distribution business, not a single-product agency.

The website's own navigation groups its range into: Blood Pressure Monitoring, Diagnostic Instruments, ECG Products, Electrosurgical Instruments, General Medical Consumables, Labels, Medin nCPAP Systems & Accessories, Neonatal Products, Proctological Products, Pulse Oximetry, Respiratory Care, Thermometry, and Ultrasound Products (henleysmed.com, read 05/09/2026). This is the company's own categorisation, not a Hub-assigned speciality, and it is noticeably broader than the four specialities (anaesthesia and critical care, ultrasound, women's health and maternity, respiratory) the Hub's existing record had inferred purely from framework names; the framework-only inference under-represented the neonatal, ECG, electrosurgical, proctological and general-consumables side of the business.

Quality: the company holds a current ISO 9001:2015 certificate (No. Q8977, issued by Interface NRM Ltd, first issued 4 June 2025, expiring 20 May 2028), scoped to 'storage and distribution of electro-medical devices, disposable devices, reusable devices, and sterile medical devices' (certificate PDF hosted at henleysmed.com, downloaded and read 05/09/2026). Note for anyone checking this themselves: the same accreditations page also links to an older, now-broken PDF whose filename implies an expiry of 31 January 2026; that link 404s and appears to be a stale leftover from a 2023 upload, superseded by the current 2025-issued certificate above, which is the one a rep should rely on.

Framework footprint: Henleys is named on nine current NHS Supply Chain frameworks, spanning Rehabilitation and Community, Medical and Surgical Consumables, and Diagnostic Equipment and Services categories (see stats, above, for the full list and the counting rule). This is a large number of framework awards for a company with 34 average employees and £6.13 million turnover, and it is worth being precise about what it does and does not mean. Being named on a framework confirms this supplier was awarded a place, at the rates and terms in that framework's own documentation; it does not by itself say what volume the company actually sells through the NHS, what share of any one framework's business goes to Henleys against the other 25 to 57 suppliers named alongside it, or whether an individual trust chooses to call off from Henleys at all. No NHS spend or market-share data exists to answer that question, and none is asserted here.

Financially the company is conservatively run: debt-free since November 2022, £2.38 million cash, a freehold property base, and dividends drawn by the family shareholder-directors rather than reinvested. The genuine open question, visible only from the trend rather than any single year, is the margin compression described in growth.prose: turnover has held steady but profit before tax has fallen 61% in three years. Nothing in the filed accounts or on the website explains why; a small company is not required to file a strategic report, and Henleys does not.

deepDive.interview: Henleys' own numbers set up three fair questions. First, turnover has sat between £6.1 million and £6.4 million for four straight years while profit before tax has fallen from £708,729 to £276,159 over the same period: what is driving the margin compression, and is it cost inflation, pricing pressure, or a deliberate reinvestment the accounts don't show, since as a small company Henleys files no strategic report to explain it. Second, the company is named on nine current NHS Supply Chain frameworks, a wide footprint for a 34-employee distributor: which of those frameworks actually generate meaningful call-off volume for Henleys today, and which are more nominal presence than active business, given several of those frameworks carry 25 to 57 awarded suppliers. Third, the company describes itself on its own website as third-generation family-run, with Scott Henley as Sales and Marketing Director and Danielle Turner (Henley) as Managing Director; worth asking directly how decisions get made day to day between the family directors and the wider leadership team (a finance director and a director of business development also sit on the board), and whether the family intends the business to pass to a fourth generation or is open to a trade sale, since Companies House shows no group parent and no external shareholder of any kind. None of these questions has an answer in the public record; they are simply where the public record stops.

deepDive.origin: supplier-deep-capture scheduled run, 02/09/2026. Editorial deepDive built from Companies House (company overview, officers, persons with significant control and filing history for HOSPITAL SERVICES LIMITED NI005155 and for its parent HOSPITAL SERVICES GROUP LIMITED 09740301), and from the group's own filed statutory accounts for the years ended 30 September 2024 (filed 10 October 2025) and 30 September 2022 (filed 30 June 2023); from Hospital Services Limited's own UK site at hsl.co.uk (home, about, contact, careers, frameworks, news, modern slavery statement) and its Irish site at hsl.ie; from Asker Healthcare Group's own press-release archive; and from NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs already captured into this record's frameworks array on 31/08/2026. Both accounts filings are SCANNED PDFs with no iXBRL tagging - ?format=xhtml returns HTTP 500 on each - so every figure below was read off the page the company itself labelled it on, one filing at a time, under the method in company-intelligence-capture-process.md. All read in this session.
deepDive.tagline: Belfast-registered specialist distributor of imaging, endoscopy, ophthalmic and theatre equipment to the NHS and the Irish health service, trading as HSL, majority-owned since February 2025 by the Stockholm-listed Asker Healthcare Group.
deepDive.lede: Three things set this one up. First, the growth is real and it is fast: group turnover went from £30,788,920 in the year to 30 September 2021 to £56,675,734 in the year to 30 September 2024, up 84% in three years, with the last year alone up 25.7%. Second, the 2024 accounts nevertheless show a loss before tax of £3,029,906, and it would be a mistake to read that as the business turning down - £7,365,592 of exceptional administrative expenses sit in that year, of which £7,275,879 is a share based payment charge and £89,713 is legal and professional fees the company itself describes as "relating to the sale of the group". On the directors' own adjusted EBITDA measure the year was £7,871,957 against £5,981,711. Third, that sale happened: the company's own note 32 records that following the balance sheet date the Hospital Services Group was acquired by Asker Healthcare Group in February 2025, and Asker Healthcare Group AB is listed on the Stockholm Stock Exchange. A rep walking in on the strength of a pre-2025 briefing will have the ownership, the chief executive and the acquisition programme all wrong.

prose: Turnover, group, every figure read off the line the company itself labels Turnover on the face of its consolidated statement of comprehensive income: £30,788,920 for the year to 30 September 2021 and £37,002,978 for 2022 (both from the accounts made up to 30 September 2022, filed 30 June 2023, page 10), then £45,094,529 for 2023 and £56,675,734 for 2024 (both from the accounts made up to 30 September 2024, filed 10 October 2025, page 12). That is 84% growth across three years and 25.7% in the last of them, and it is organic growth plus a run of acquisitions rather than either on its own - see the ownership section.

Operating profit tracked turnover until 2024 and then broke from it: £2,866,795 (2021), £3,333,370 (2022), £4,109,344 (2023), then an operating loss of £2,386,618 in 2024. The break is accounted for in one line. Note 11 of the 2024 accounts sets out £7,365,592 of exceptional administrative expenses - a share based payment charge of £7,275,879, plus £89,713 of legal and professional fees the company describes as relating to the sale of the group - against £59,325 the year before. Strip those out and the trading direction is the one the directors report on their own adjusted EBITDA measure: £7,871,957 in 2024 against £5,981,711 in 2023.

Two other lines are worth carrying into a conversation. Amortisation of intangible assets and goodwill was £2,571,048 in 2024 against £1,523,666 in 2023 (note 5), which is what a decade of buying businesses looks like on the profit and loss account. And interest payable was £679,455 in 2024 against £1,004,420 in 2023, on net assets that rose from £7,992,777 to £12,633,427.

What is NOT available, and why. Note 4 of the 2024 accounts reads in full: "No analysis of turnover is presented as the directors consider such disclosure to be prejudicial to the interests of the Group." So there is no UK/Ireland split, no divisional split and no product split in the filings, and none is estimated here. Neither filing is tagged iXBRL - `?format=xhtml` returns HTTP 500 on both - which is why this Hub's Companies House pipeline shows no turnover for NI005155 while this record carries a four-year series: the figures were read off the scanned pages by hand, not extracted by a script.

ownership: HOSPITAL SERVICES LIMITED, company number NI005155, registered office 30 Wildflower Way, Belfast BT12 6TA, is an active private limited company incorporated on 5 February 1962, SIC 47749, retail sale of medical and orthopaedic goods in specialised stores. Its auditor is Grant Thornton (NI) LLP of Donegall Square West, Belfast. The identity is confirmed rather than inferred: the Belfast office address HSL publishes on its own contact page, "30 Wildflower Way, Adelaide Industrial Estate, Belfast, BT12 6TA", is the registered office on the register, and the accounts filed under NI005155 carry the HSL name and that address on their company information page.

The chain, in the company's own words. Note 34 of the 2024 accounts names the ultimate parent undertaking as Hospital Services Group Limited, Unit 1 Riverside Park East Service Road, Raynesway, Derby DE21 7BF - company 09740301 on the register - and says the directors consider there to be no ultimate controlling party of that company. The same note then records that "subsequent to the year end, the Company's ultimate parent undertaking, Hospital Services Group Limited, was acquired by Asker Healthcare Group AB, a company incorporated and registered in Sweden", listed on the Stockholm Stock Exchange. Note 32, post balance sheet events, dates it: the group "was acquired by Asker Healthcare Group, in February 2025".

The register carries the same change as a sequence of dated events, and they are worth reading because the Hub's own supplier files and most public profiles of this company still describe the previous owner. On 09740301: Foresight VCT plc ceased to be a person with significant control on 4 February 2025; Asker Healthcare AB (Swedish company 556824-6069) was notified on 31 January 2025 and ceased on 27 March 2025; Asker Healthcare Group AB (559184-9848, Danderyd, Stockholm) has been the active person with significant control since 27 March 2025, on ownership of 75% or more of shares and voting rights. On NI005155 itself, Hospital Services Group Limited remains the active person with significant control, notified 6 April 2016 at 75% or more; Asker Healthcare Group AB was notified there on 4 February 2025 and ceased on 3 February 2026. The register does not say why that second entry ceased while Asker remains the active controller of the parent, and nothing here reads a sale into it.

HSL's own history page frames the same transaction differently, and the difference is worth knowing before a meeting: it says "Asker Healthcare Group has placed a significant investment, alongside current management in HSL". The filed accounts say acquired and the register records 75% or more. Both are quoted; this record does not reconcile them.

The group HSL heads is a real one, not a shell. Note 33 of the 2024 accounts records that Hospital Services Limited guarantees the liabilities of Medtech UK Limited (13739470), Orca Medical Limited (10907715) and Orca Resource Limited (13092629), all registered in England and all claiming audit exemption under section 479A. The strategic report names the acquisition of Orca Medical Limited and Orca Resource Limited on 13 March 2024 as the most notable event of that financial year. HSL's own history page adds the rest of the sequence: Ergoviewing (2017), MDi Medical (2021), Video South (2022), Fleetwood Healthcare (2023), Orca Medical (2024), HNC and novus med (2025) and Murray Surgical (2026).

marketPosition: The measurable part of this company's NHS position is its framework footprint, and the rule used here is narrow: a framework counts only where NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch brief names this supplier. On that test there are ten, all captured from those briefs on 31/08/2026. What makes them worth reading is how few suppliers are on several of them: Lithotripsy and Associated Options and Related Services has three named suppliers, Surgical Navigation Systems six, Mobile Image Intensifiers ten, Fluoroscopy eleven, Static X-Ray thirteen and Mobile X-Ray Systems fourteen. Those six share the reference 2021/S 000-007768 and all run from 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2028. The other four are Decontamination Capital Equipment (20 suppliers, to 18 February 2027), Digital Diagnostic Solutions (54, to 31 July 2027), Medical Healthcare Furniture (51, to 11 May 2027) and Operating Theatres Equipment and Related Accessories and Services (43, to 11 April 2028). No market share is stated here and none is calculable from any of it - a supplier count is not a share of spend.

HSL publishes its own framework list, and it is materially wider than the NHS Supply Chain set, which matters for anyone mapping routes to market. Read at hsl.co.uk/frameworks on 02/09/2026, the Great Britain routes it names beyond NHS Supply Chain include Crown Commercial Service G-Cloud 15 for Medical IT and AV, NHS Shared Business Services' Audio Visual Solutions and Integrated Operating Theatres 2, the NHS North of England Commercial Procurement Collaborative Tech Devices Link 4 framework, an Immersive, Simulation and Related Technologies DPS, Flexible Video Endoscopy Consumables and Single Use Scope (NP103/25) and Surgical Endoscopy Suite Goods and Services (2024/S 000-026243). A long separate list covers the Irish health service under HSE reference numbers.

One conflict is left standing rather than resolved. For two frameworks the company's own page and NHS Supply Chain's own brief give different procurement references: HSL lists Decontamination Capital Equipment as 2024/S 000-024385 and Digital Diagnostic Solutions as 2025/S 000-003009, where the briefs this Hub captured give 2024/S 000-017758 and 2025/S 000-043444. The Hub's rows follow NHS Supply Chain's own brief, which is this repo's sourcing rule for framework data. Which reference is the correct one for each agreement was not established in this session and is not asserted either way.

This supplier holds no entries at all in the Hub's NHS Supply Chain catalogue cache, refreshed 30/08/2026. That is consistent with what the frameworks say it sells - capital imaging, endoscopy, theatre and decontamination equipment with the services around them, bought through framework call-off rather than stocked on the catalogue - but it is a statement about that cache on that date, not a finding that the company sells nothing through NHS Supply Chain.

Its own catalogue was crawled on 27/08/2026 and gives 331 products across eleven of the company's own categories: Ophthalmology (135), Healthcare Technologies (74), Surgical Equipment (36), Xray (26), Diagnostic Imaging (20), Endoscopy (19), Ergonomic Furniture (6), Mounting Solutions (5), Brands (4), Medical Cart (3) and Breast Health (3). Read that with a caveat this record puts in writing: the crawl read hsl.ie, the Irish site, and the company runs a separate UK site at hsl.co.uk which carries a top-level Rental Options section the Irish site does not. The Hub's index holds one domain per supplier, so the captured range should not be read as the UK range, and an absent category is not evidence of an absent capability.

deepDive.interview: Read the 2024 accounts and the ownership note before you go anywhere near this one, because both have changed recently enough that most briefings are out of date. On the numbers, do not open with the loss. Turnover has gone from £30.8m to £56.7m in three years and the £3.03m loss before tax in 2024 is a £7.28m share based payment charge and the fees on the sale of the group; the directors' own adjusted EBITDA rose from £5.98m to £7.87m in the same year. The question that shows you have read the filing is what happens to margin as the acquisitions integrate - amortisation of intangibles and goodwill nearly doubled to £2.57m, which is the arithmetic of buying eight businesses in nine years, and gross margin still improved to 39.50%. On ownership, know that Foresight exited in February 2025 and the group is now majority-owned by Asker Healthcare Group AB, listed in Stockholm; saying "Foresight-backed" would date you by eighteen months, and so would naming Dominic Walsh as chief executive - he is Chairman and John Lyng, formerly of MDi Medical which HSL itself bought in 2021, is Chief Executive. On the commercial side, the framework position is the strongest card and the most specific thing you can talk about: three named suppliers on Lithotripsy and six on Surgical Navigation Systems is a genuinely narrow field, and all six of the 2021/S 000-007768 imaging frameworks expire on 31 March 2028, which makes successor procurement a live subject rather than a theoretical one. Finally, understand the shape of the business: it is a distributor and a service organisation - Shimadzu, Hologic, Canon, Richard Wolf and Konica Minolta agencies by its own account - with a Healthcare Technologies division the strategic report says grew on the back of NHS investment in digital health and remote diagnostic reporting. It is not a manufacturer, and a pitch built on manufacturing will land wrong.

background.heading: Ownership change
background.text: Smiths Medical International Limited was officially renamed to ICU Medical International Limited on 2 October 2024 (Companies House 00362847) — also historically traded as Portex Limited (1940-2004), which is why 'Portex' persists as a live brand under this entity. Separately, ICU Medical completed a 60% divestiture of its IV Solutions (large-volume parenteral fluids) manufacturing business to Otsuka Pharmaceutical Factory, forming 'Otsuka ICU Medical LLC' (1 May 2025) — this is North America manufacturing-focused (Austin, TX + Otsuka's Asian plants) and does not appear to affect any UK-relevant device brand currently listed (Plum, Medfusion, CADD, Clave, Portex, Level 1, Jelco, Pneupac, ChemoLock/ChemoClave, Plum 360, Transpac).

deepDive.tagline: Ashford-based UK arm of Nasdaq-listed ICU Medical, Inc., built from the old Portex/Smiths Medical business bought from Smiths Group in January 2022. It stopped manufacturing in the UK in 2023 and now designs, distributes and sells; its two UK trading entities were merged on 1 February 2026.

links.label: Companies House — ICU Medical International Limited (00362847)
Companies House — ICU UK Medical Limited (10442778)

deepDive.lede: Do not walk in with the turnover figure. ICU Medical International Limited files turnover of £188.4m for the year to 31 December 2024, and note 5 of the same accounts says £19.7m of it was sold into the United Kingdom — about one pound in ten. The UK number fell, from £21.0m; the growth was £38.7m of services billed to other group companies, double the year before, which the directors put down to larger inter-company sales with their US counterpart. The second thing to know is that this is no longer a manufacturer: the strategic report says the UK factories closed in 2023, and the employee note shows Factory/Operations headcount at zero against 27 the year before. Sales and marketing headcount went from 66 to 58 over the same year. And the entity itself has moved — what was Smiths Medical International Limited until 2 October 2024 absorbed the group's other UK trading company on 1 February 2026, so check which company name is on the paperwork in front of you.

stats.n: £188,361,000, against £174,424,000 in 2023. Read from the line the company itself labels Turnover on the face of its statement of comprehensive income, page 13, in the audited accounts of ICU MEDICAL INTERNATIONAL LIMITED (00362847) for the year ended 31 December 2024, filed at Companies House on 24 December 2025 and audited by Deloitte LLP. The filing is a scanned PDF with no iXBRL tagging, which is why this Hub's company-financials.json shows no turnover for the company while this record does.

stats.l: Of which sold into the United Kingdom
stats.n: Note 5 of the same filing, page 25, analysis of turnover by country of destination: United Kingdom £19,689,000 (2023: £20,989,000), Rest of Europe £77,261,000 (2023: £82,237,000), Rest of the world £91,411,000 (2023: £71,198,000). The UK line fell 6.2% while the total rose 7.4%. This is the company's own split, not an estimate.

stats.l: Turnover that was services, not goods
stats.n: Note 5, same page: turnover was generated from sale of goods of £149,648,000 (2023: £155,282,000) and provision of services of £38,713,000 (2023: £19,142,000). Goods fell by £5.6m and services rose by £19.6m, and note 5's own opening line attributes turnover to design, distribution and sale of medical devices "as well as the provision of services to other group companies".

Note 8 of the same filing, page 27, average monthly number of employees by function: Distribution 67 (2023: 70), Factory/Operations 0 (2023: 27), Administration 132 (133), Research & Development 51 (48), Sales & Marketing 58 (66). Total 308 (2023: 344), of whom 227 UK (258) and 81 overseas (86). The strategic report gives the reason in its own words: administration and exceptional costs "reduced significantly in 2024 as we closed our factories in the UK in the previous year".

stats.l: Turnover of the other UK entity, ICU UK Medical Limited
stats.n: £12,308,577 for the year ended 31 December 2024 (2023: £10,572,500), of which note 5, page 18, puts £12,307,102 in the United Kingdom and £1,475 in Europe. Audited accounts of ICU UK MEDICAL LIMITED (10442778), filed 8 July 2025, auditor Forvis Mazars LLP. Gross margin fell from 30.2% to 21.0% and profit after tax was £376,705 (2023: £264,308).

stats.l: The two UK trading entities merged
stats.n: Note 31, post balance sheet events, in the 00362847 accounts for the year ended 31 December 2024: "It has been announced that, effective 1st February 2026, two UK trading entities will be consolidated", with ICU UK Medical Limited transferring its trade and assets to 00362847 at carrying value, and the shares of 00362847 being sold by ICU Medical Group Limited to ICU Medical BV in the Netherlands. Companies House shows the matching change: ICU Medical Group Limited ceased as a person with significant control on 18 December 2025.

Named supplier on fourteen NHS Supply Chain contract launch briefs, which is the count this Hub holds for the company. Ranking rule, so you can judge it: count the briefs that name the company, one per framework, across the 1,191 suppliers in this Hub's seed. On that count 1,145 suppliers are named on at least one brief, 26 are named on more than ten, and ICU Medical is joint fourteenth with Essity UK, Fujifilm Healthcare UK and Reliance Medical. It counts frameworks, not revenue, lots or market share, and nothing here is inferred from product ranges.

Companies House company 00362847, read 26/08/2026. Status Active, SIC 22290, registered office 1500 Eureka Park, Lower Pemberton, Ashford, Kent TN25 4BF. The register's previous-name record for that number runs PORTEX LIMITED (1940–1996), SIMS PORTEX LIMITED (1996–2001), PORTEX LIMITED (2001–2004), SMITHS MEDICAL INTERNATIONAL LIMITED (2004 to 2 October 2024). The company's own strategic report says "we have been in business since 1941"; the register says the company was incorporated on 16 August 1940. Both are recorded here and neither is reconciled.

prose: The 2022 bar is seventeen months long and everything else on the chart is twelve, so the shape is an artefact of the year-end change and not a boom. On the company's own prorated basis the twelve-month equivalent was £183.9m, which makes the real sequence roughly £227m, £184m, £174m, £188m: a fall of about a fifth across the acquisition, then a further dip, then a partial recovery. The directors' explanation for the fall, in the 2022 strategic report, is stock shortages from global supply chain problems, with gross margin down 2.2% on product mix and foreign exchange, and distribution costs up particularly on air and sea freight.

The 2024 recovery is not a UK recovery. Turnover rose £13.9m, and note 5 splits it: sale of goods fell £5.6m to £149.6m while provision of services to other group companies rose £19.6m to £38.7m, and turnover sold into the United Kingdom fell £1.3m to £19.7m. The strategic report says the increase in revenue "is lead by larger inter-company sales within the group, mainly with our US counterpart". A rep quoting £188m as this company's presence in the UK market is out by a factor of about ten.

Profit tells a different story from sales, and it is worth separating the two. Operating profit went from £17.2m in the twelve months to July 2021, to £2.5m across the seventeen-month period, to £5.7m in 2023, to £18.1m in 2024. Almost all of the 2024 jump is cost: administrative expenses fell from £22.1m to £12.9m after the UK factories closed and the transitional contracts with Smiths Group ended in 2023, while gross margin actually slipped from 26.1% to 25.3%. Below operating profit the picture changes again: £15.9m of the £33.7m profit before tax is interest receivable on an intercompany loan, so profit before tax is not a measure of how the trading business did. Exceptional costs of £1,208,000 in 2024 (2023: £2,462,000) are, in note 6's own words, redundancy and legal expenditure from the ongoing integration project.

Cash is leaving. Interim dividends of £23,000,000 were authorised in the year to December 2024 against £nil in 2023, and note 31 records a further £24,500,000 of interim dividends approved in April 2025. Retained earnings still stood at £200,236,000 at the year end.

ownership: ICU MEDICAL INTERNATIONAL LIMITED, company number 00362847, registered office 1500 Eureka Park, Lower Pemberton, Ashford, Kent TN25 4BF, is a private limited company incorporated on 16 August 1940 and currently Active, SIC 22290 (manufacture of other plastic products). It has traded under four names: PORTEX LIMITED to 1996, SIMS PORTEX LIMITED to 2001, PORTEX LIMITED again to 1 March 2004, SMITHS MEDICAL INTERNATIONAL LIMITED to 2 October 2024, and its current name since. That chain is why Portex is still a live brand under this entity and why older NHS paperwork and framework listings carry the Smiths Medical name.

The 2022 strategic report sets out how it changed hands, in the directors' own words: "In January 2022, ICU Medical, Inc. announced that it had completed it's acquisition of the Smiths Medical Division, which includes the Company, from Smiths Group plc", creating "a leading infusion therapy company with estimated pro forma combined revenues of approximately £2 billion". Note 31 of the 2024 accounts dates the completion to 6 January 2022. The same report explains the seventeen-month accounting period: the year-end was extended to align with ICU Medical, Inc.

Control has moved twice since, and the register carries both moves. Note 30 of the 2024 accounts records the immediate parent as ICU Medical Group Limited (a UK company, 05137144, formerly Smiths Medical Group Limited and before that Smiths Medical Holdco Limited), with ICU Medical, Inc. as ultimate parent and ultimate controlling party. Companies House then shows ICU Medical Group Limited ceasing as a person with significant control on 18 December 2025 and a single active person with significant control notified on the same date: Icu Medical, Inc, of 951 Calle Amanecer, San Clemente, California, governing law Delaware, place registered "Delaware - Nasdaq", registration number 2284646, holding 75% or more of shares and of voting rights and the right to appoint or remove directors. The filing history shows the entry going on as "Icu Medical B.V." on a PSC02 filed 7 January 2026 and a PSC05 change of details filed 5 February 2026; the register as read on 26/08/2026 names ICU Medical, Inc. Both are recorded here; the reason for the change of details is not stated on the register and none is inferred.

The UK group is being simplified, and the deadline has already passed. Note 31 of the 2024 accounts says that effective 1 February 2026 two UK trading entities would be consolidated: ICU UK Medical Limited (10442778) transferring its trade and assets to 00362847 at carrying value, and the shares of 00362847 being sold by ICU Medical Group Limited to a fellow group company, ICU Medical BV in the Netherlands. Separately the Nijmegen warehouse transfers from 00362847 to ICU Medical BV, with the lease changing hands and the inventory moving "within the next 24 months"; staff there were notified on 1 November 2025 and moved to ICU Medical BV on 1 February 2026. ICU UK Medical Limited is still an Active company at Companies House as at 26/08/2026, with accounts to 31 December 2025 due by 30 September 2026, so the transfer of trade has not dissolved it. Companies House also records a statement of capital following an allotment of shares in 00362847 on 1 February 2026, taking called-up capital from £43,217 to £43,219.

Five other UK companies sit at the same Ashford address and carry the group's name: ICU MEDICAL GROUP LIMITED (05137144), ICU MEDICAL (SM) LIMITED (00995550, formerly Graseby Medical Limited), ICU MEDICAL 2020 LIMITED (12103805, formerly Smiths Medical 2020 Limited), ICU MEDICAL BIDCO LTD (13730094, incorporated 8 November 2021, two months before completion) and ICU UK MEDICAL LIMITED (10442778). A separate ICU MEDICAL LIMITED, 09400155, of Liverpool, was dissolved on 11 July 2024 and is not part of this group; do not attach it to this supplier.

deepDive.peopleNote: Companies House lists five active appointments for 00362847 against 48 resignations, which is what a company that has changed owner twice looks like on the register. The dated changes worth knowing: Brian Bonnell, Ramon De Ridder and Cornelis De Rooij were all appointed on 25 January 2022, nineteen days after the acquisition completed; and the directors' report for 2024 records Louis Jones resigning on 30 June 2025 and Andrew Dawe being appointed on 30 June 2025. Those are dated register events and nothing here asserts a succession between them. Four of the five are the same people who sign for ICU UK Medical Limited, and only one, Andrew Dawe, is resident in the United Kingdom, so the person a rep or a trust meets will not be on this list. Commercial job titles — sales leadership, category management, NHS account ownership — could not be verified: Companies House records legal directorships only, and no named UK leadership team was published on the pages of the company's own site read in this session. Not verified.
marketPosition: The company describes its own market for you, and it is worth quoting because it is the frame its people are working in: the 2024 strategic report says "the consumable medical device segment of the health care industry and in particular the infusion products market is intensely competitive and continues to experience both horizontal and vertical consolidation", and lists the things it thinks competition turns on — product innovation, quality, convenience and reliability, access to distribution channels, patent protection and pricing. Nothing in this Hub measures market share and no share figure exists anywhere in this system; this is the company's own characterisation, reported as such.

Fourteen NHS Supply Chain frameworks is the checkable footprint, and its spread is the useful part: infusion pumps and administration sets, intravenous cannula, needlefree connection systems, central venous catheters, extension sets and lines, intravenous and pressure monitoring accessories, syringes and needles, blood collection devices, airway management, respiratory solutions and patient temperature management. That is a vascular access and infusion company with a serious airway and temperature business attached — the Portex and Level 1 inheritance — rather than a single-category supplier.

The framework picture in front of a rep right now has one change in it. The Find a Tender contract award notice for the 2027 Intravenous Cannula and Associated Products framework, published 18 August 2026 and re-read at source on 26 August 2026, names 21 suppliers, and "Smiths Medical International Ltd" of 1500 Eureka Park, Ashford TN25 4BF, contact MWATUKContracts@icumed.com, is one of them — that is company 00362847 under the name it held until 2 October 2024. "ICU UK Medical Ltd", which held a separate place on the outgoing 2023-2027 framework, is not on the award notice. So the group keeps a place and loses a second one, and the timing sits beside the 1 February 2026 consolidation of those same two entities. The notice gives no reason and none is asserted here. NHS Supply Chain's own commercial launch brief for the new framework had not been published when this was checked, and "not on the award notice" is not the same statement as "will not supply under this framework".

It is not a UK manufacturer any more, and that changes what can honestly be said about lead times and UK content. The 2022 accounts describe the principal activity as "the design, manufacture, distribution and sale of medical devices"; the 2024 accounts, for the same company, say "the design, distribution and sale of medical devices". The word manufacture has gone, the strategic report says the UK factories closed in 2023, average Factory/Operations headcount is zero against 27, and depreciation of tangible fixed assets is down to £237,000 on £188m of turnover. What has stayed in the UK is research and development — 51 people on average, up from 48, with £2,432,000 charged as an expense.

The Hub's crawl of icumed.com on 11/08/2026 read 181 products across eight divisions the company organises itself: Infusion Therapy (84), Airway Management (38), Temperature Management (17), Hemodynamic Monitoring (13), Pain Management (13), Pharmacy Preparation (8), Veterinary (6) and Renal Care (2). This Hub currently tags the supplier on vascular access and oncology/infusion only, and that is narrower than the company's own division tree; the gap is reported here rather than acted on, because a speciality is a published claim about a company and belongs in a reviewed change with its evidence.

One risk the directors name themselves is worth carrying into a pricing conversation. The 2024 strategic report says the majority of sales are under long-term contracts with long pricing periods, that contractual protections may not adequately mitigate inflation, and that "we are trying to anticipate inflation in our price negociations this will be a feature from now on after a long period of low or no inflation". The 2024 business review adds that margin fell because supplier price increases "have not been fully reflected on our sales prices", and that "as we carry on renewing tenders we will adjust our prices". They are telling you, in a filed document, that they intend to push price at re-tender.

deepDive.interview: Start by establishing which company you are actually contracting with, because it changed on 1 February 2026: ICU UK Medical Limited transferred its trade and assets into 00362847, the entity that was Smiths Medical International Limited until October 2024, and the shares of that entity moved to ICU Medical BV in the Netherlands. Old purchase orders, framework listings and price files will carry at least three different names for the same business. On the numbers, do not be impressed by £188m: £19.7m of it was sold into the United Kingdom and that line fell, while £38.7m of the total was services billed to other group companies. If you want a like-for-like UK comparison, the other entity's £12.3m was almost all UK and it grew 16%. On supply, this is no longer a UK manufacturer — the factories closed in 2023 and Factory/Operations headcount is zero — so anything said about UK production or short domestic lead times deserves a follow-up about where the product is actually made and shipped from; the Nijmegen warehouse is moving to the Dutch entity over 24 months, which is a live logistics change. On price, their own strategic report says they intend to recover supplier inflation at re-tender, so expect that conversation and have your position ready. And on people, four of the five registered directors sit in the United States or the Netherlands, sales and marketing headcount fell from 66 to 58 in a year, and £23m of dividends went out in 2024 with a further £24.5m approved in April 2025 — find out early who in the UK can actually sign off a price.

Companies House: the company overview, officers, persons with significant control and filing history pages for ICU MEDICAL INTERNATIONAL LIMITED, company number 00362847; the company overview and accounts filing history for ICU UK MEDICAL LIMITED, 10442778; and a register search for "ICU Medical" and for "Smiths Medical International", which returns 00362847 as the only company that has ever held the latter name. Filed accounts, downloaded from Companies House and read page by page as rasterised images because all of these filings are scanned PDFs with no text layer and no iXBRL tagging: the audited accounts of 00362847 for the year ended 31 December 2024 (filed 24 December 2025, auditor Deloitte LLP) — strategic report pages 1-3, directors' report pages 5-6, statement of comprehensive income page 13, note 5 turnover and note 6 operating profit page 25, note 8 employees pages 26-27, note 9 directors' remuneration page 27, and notes 27 to 31 page 39; the accounts of the same company for the 17-month period ended 31 December 2022 (filed 10 June 2024 under the name Smiths Medical International Limited) — strategic report page 1 and statement of comprehensive income page 15, which also carry the comparatives for the year ended 31 July 2021; and the audited accounts of ICU UK MEDICAL LIMITED for the year ended 31 December 2024 (filed 8 July 2025, auditor Forvis Mazars LLP) — company information page 1, directors' report page 2, profit and loss account page 9, and note 5 turnover page 18. Every figure above is quoted from the line the company itself labels, with the page given, and none is derived by position or by any parser. Find a Tender: contract award notice 2026/S 000-078334 for Intravenous Cannula and Associated Products, read at source. The company's own site: the UK home page at icumed.com/en-gb, and the product structure captured by this Hub's crawler from the icumed.com sitemap on 11/08/2026. Coordinates for the registered office postcode from postcodes.io. IMPORTANT, on why this record carries figures the rest of the Hub does not: company-financials.json holds 00362847 at matchConfidence "probable", so it publishes no turnover, no headcount and no officers for this company. That is not a doubt about identity. It is a tokeniser artefact — the corroboration test drops words of three characters or fewer and drops "medical", "international" and "limited" as corporate noise, so the registered name "ICU MEDICAL INTERNATIONAL LIMITED" yields no significant tokens at all and can never corroborate anything. Identity was instead established at source four ways: the register's own previous-name record for 00362847; the registered office on the register matching the address on the accounts; the accounts stating their own registered number 00362847 on the company information page; and the directors named in the accounts matching the active officers on the register. Not verified and deliberately omitted: any named commercial, sales or category leadership below board level, which Companies House does not record and the company's own site did not publish on the pages read here; current vacancies, which were not read; any market share figure, which does not exist in this system; dated press or announcements, none of which were read from a source in this session; and the FY2025 results for either company, which are not filed.

background.heading: Ownership change
background.text: Major corporate change: Rhône (US private equity) completed acquisition of Invacare Holdings S.a.r.l. (Invacare Europe & APAC -- covers this UK entity) and Direct Healthcare Group (DHG) on 30/01/2026, merging them into a new combined company 'DHCare'; ARCHIMED (DHG's former backer) retains a minority stake. This is separate from, and post-dates, Invacare Corporation's 2023 US Chapter 11 -- the US lineage kept only North America, which was itself sold on again (to MIGA Holdings, Nov 2024). Invacare UK (Pencoed, Wales) is now part of DHCare, not the original US Invacare Corporation. No visible rebrand on invacare.co.uk as of this check -- still 'Invacare GB' branding, likely mid-transition. DHG's brands (Dyna-Form, System RoMedic, Raizer) are now sister brands under the same DHCare parent, no longer independent competitors.

background.heading: Ownership and stage
background.text: Genuinely UK-owned: Companies House confirms 100% ownership by sole director Mr Lee James Quickmire (British, UK-resident), not a subsidiary. Incorporated 09/09/2024, first accounts filed 26/03/2026 as a micro-entity — genuinely early-stage. Zero results on NHS Supply Chain: not on the national framework, consistent with selling direct to trusts, ambulance services and local authorities.

background.heading: The catalogue is wider than the store front page
background.text: The jeenie.uk store landing page and the Jeenie Products menu both show a curated subset; the full store-products sitemap lists 32 products, including a seated transfer slide board, a handling belt and two turning aids that appear nowhere in the site navigation. Read the sitemap, not the store page. RESOLD THIRD-PARTY LINES, resale not confirmed with Jeenie: the LOCO- prefixed board, belt and turners share their SKU scheme and product names with Select Healthcare's Locomotor range (LOCO-501/LOCO-600 turners, S.U.P.A Slide, Uni Slides); "Oxford" is Prism Healthcare Group's sling brand; "Rota Stand" is a Direct Healthcare Group product name. Same pattern as the Bariquin training mannequin, which is a resold third-party brand and not a Jeenie-owned product — it is made by Bariatric Training Mannequins Ltd, trading as "Bariquins", a separate UK company.

background.heading: How the company describes itself
background.text: Mission stated as "empowering caregivers, preserving dignity and fostering collaboration"; the company reads its own name as an acronym — "Jeenie Enables Empowered Nursing, Inclusivity and Excellence". Products are built to an internal "LAMP" design framework (Limit Risk, Act With Ease, Move Safely, Promote Better Care); training is delivered through "WISH" (Workforce Development, Integrated Care Planning, Safe Systems of Work, Hands-On Training), aimed at NHS manual handling teams, falls leads, tissue viability specialists, link assessors, ward staff and procurement teams, with travel and meals covered for NHS attendees and quarterly on-site support visits. UNCONFIRMED, check before repeating to a customer: jeenie.uk states "20 years of frontline experience" while the company's LinkedIn About states "over 18 years' experience"; the Leadership panel resolves this as rounding on one career, but neither page itself names whose experience it is. LinkedIn states company size as 2–10 employees, which is a self-reported band, not the accounts figure — Companies House recorded an average headcount below one for the year to 30/09/2025.

background.heading: Centre for Excellence
background.text: A 443 sqm simulated training facility at the same Wetherby address as the registered office (Unit 416B, Street 7, Birch Park, Thorp Arch Estate, Wetherby LS23 7FG): a replica hospital ward (gantry and mobile hoists, specialist beds and chairs), a confined bedroom set, a stairwell rig and bathroom/bathtub rescue scenarios. Hired out to independent trainers and organisations, or run as bespoke courses for hospitals, councils and larger organisations. Training on offer: a "Free the Jeenie" escape-room challenge, a CPD-badged "Comprehensive Care for Plus-Size and Bariatric Patients" course (accrediting body not named on the site), an Advanced Manual Handling Workshop using weighted mannequins, and bespoke sessions. Four case studies are listed by title only (complex evacuation, evacuation from upstairs, complex care evacuation, complex care relocation), with no trust name, outcome or date on the public pages, so none is usable as a reference.

deepDive.tagline: MedTech segment of Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) · UK & Ireland HQ: Wokingham · UK orthopaedics base: Leeds
deepDive.lede: The single most important thing to know before this interview: J&J announced in October 2025 that it's spinning off its Orthopaedics business, DePuy Synthes, into a standalone company within 18 to 24 months, putting completion at roughly April to October 2027. If the role touches orthopaedics or sits at the Leeds site, that separation will very likely come up, and you should have a view on it.

prose: MedTech is J&J's smaller segment by revenue (it sits alongside Innovative Medicine, the pharma side) but it's currently the faster-growing one. Segment sales went from $30.4bn in FY2023 to $31.86bn in FY2024 (up 4.8%) to $33.79bn in FY2025 (up 6.1%). Those are the three years verifiable on a clean, consistent basis from J&J's own filings; the segment's product scope shifted around the 2023 Consumer Health spin-off (Kenvue), so the comparison is deliberately not stretched further to avoid mixing different segment definitions.

Within FY2024, Surgery and Orthopaedics were the two biggest franchises, together worth around $19bn, more than half of segment revenue. Surgery brought in $9.84bn (down 1.9%) and Orthopaedics $9.16bn. Cardiovascular, which covers electrophysiology, Abiomed and the newer Shockwave business, is the fastest mover: up 12.6% to $2.21bn in a single quarter (Q3 2025), and it's explicitly where J&J says future MedTech investment is being weighted.

ownership: J&J runs two segments: Innovative Medicine (pharma, about 64% of group revenue) and MedTech (about 36%). MedTech is organised into four franchises: Orthopaedics (DePuy Synthes), Surgery (Ethicon, Mentor, Acclarent), Cardiovascular (Biosense Webster, Cerenovus, Abiomed, Shockwave) and Vision. In September 2023 the MedTech and pharma brands were folded under the single Johnson & Johnson name, retiring some of the old standalone product-line branding.

The live structural story is the Orthopaedics separation. J&J is carving DePuy Synthes out as its own standalone, investment-grade company, targeting a $50bn+ global orthopaedics market and roughly seven million patients a year. J&J's own framing is that it would be the largest, most comprehensive orthopaedics-focused company in the sector on completion. For scale, DePuy Synthes generated around $9.2bn in 2024, over 10% of J&J's total revenue and about 29% of MedTech segment sales. Its named competitors post-separation are Stryker ($22.6bn total revenue in 2024, including $9bn from orthopaedics) and Zimmer Biomet ($7.7bn total revenue).

deepDive.peopleNote: Companywide leadership (Duato, and MedTech's own Executive Committee members) changes periodically; worth a quick LinkedIn check on the day for anyone you know is interviewing you.

press.text: J&J announces intent to separate its Orthopaedics business into a standalone company, DePuy Synthes, within 18 to 24 months. Namal Nawana named Worldwide President to lead it through and beyond the separation. This is still in progress and is the single biggest structural fact about this employer right now.

Johnson & Johnson MedTech signs a Memorandum of Understanding with Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust, tied to the government's New Hospital Programme and the Leeds General Infirmary rebuild, to collaborate on MedTech innovation, R&D and skills in the city where DePuy Synthes has its UK manufacturing and R&D base.
J&J unifies its MedTech and pharmaceutical businesses under a single Johnson & Johnson brand, retiring separate product-line branding in external communications.
J&J MedTech UK opens an Innovation Suite at its Wokingham Pinewood Campus: a replica operating room and surgical skills zone used to train healthcare professionals.

hiring: J&J doesn't publish a rolling count of UK roles filled over the last 12 months, so no verified historical figure is given here. What's checkable: their own UK careers page currently lists around 40 open roles, spanning functions from Customer Management and HR (both Leeds) to Finance (Wokingham), which gives a live snapshot of where hiring is concentrated right now rather than a full year's history.

place.caption: DePuy Synthes, St Anthony's Road, Beeston, Leeds LS11 8DT. Street level imagery isn't available here, so this is the satellite view. The UK HQ and Innovation Suite sit at Pinewood Campus, Nine Mile Ride, Wokingham RG40 3EW.

glassdoor.summary: MedTech doesn't have its own Glassdoor listing, its reviews sit inside the main Johnson & Johnson page tagged by business segment, so treat this as directional rather than MedTech-specific. The recurring pattern: people value the compliance discipline and the genuine global scale, and push back on a layered, hierarchical structure that can slow things down.

deepDive.interview: Have a view on the DePuy Synthes separation, expect it to come up if the role is anywhere near orthopaedics. Be clear whether the role sits in MedTech or Innovative Medicine. Expect a formal, competency-based process built around Our Credo, J&J's founding values statement. Know Hugo Breda's name if you're interviewing into the UK & Ireland business.

suppliers.ownership: Not an acquisition. Kimberly-Clark Corporation spun off its health care division to its own shareholders on 31 October 2014 as Halyard Health, Inc.; Halyard Health, Inc. was renamed Avanos Medical, Inc. on 28 June 2018. Separately, on 30 April 2018 the Surgical and Infection Prevention business, including the 'Halyard Health' name itself, was sold to Owens & Minor, Inc. So the old Kimberly-Clark surgical consumables sit with Owens & Minor under the Halyard brand, while Avanos holds only pain management and specialty nutrition. Effective 31/10/2014. Source: Halyard Health, Inc. Form 10-K for 2014, filed with the SEC 13/03/2015, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1606498/000160649815000009/halyardhealth_10k2014.htm, read 21/08/2026: 'On October 31, 2014, Kimberly-Clark distributed all of our capital stock to its shareholders and completed the previously announced spin-off of its healthcare division'. Avanos Medical, Inc. Form 10-K for 2018, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1606498/000160649819000018/avns2018form10k.htm, read 21/08/2026: 'On April 30, 2018, we closed the sale of our Surgical and Infection Prevention (S&IP) business, which included the name Halyard Health ... to Owens & Minor, Inc.' SEC EDGAR company record CIK 0001606498, read 21/08/2026: name AVANOS MEDICAL, INC., former name Halyard Health, Inc. from 2014-05-06 to 2018-06-28. Cross-checked against avanos.com (read 21/08/2026), whose portfolio is MIC-KEY, CORTRAK, NEOMED, GAME READY, COOLIEF and ON-Q only, and kimberly-clark.com/en-us/company/about (read 21/08/2026), whose brand navigation lists only Adult Care, Baby and Child Care, Family Care, Feminine Care and Kimberly-Clark Professional, with no healthcare or medical device category.

deepDive.tagline: Hereford-based UK arm of the German compression and orthotics manufacturer medi - turnover up in each of the last three years, £18.3m to £23.9m, on 42 people and a 47% gross margin.
deepDive.lede: This is the cleanest growth record of any supplier in this batch, and it is the only one where every year is read from tagged accounts rather than a scan. Turnover has risen in each of the last three years - £18,317,661 for 2022, £20,052,001 for 2023, £21,893,050 for 2024 and £23,854,087 for 2025 - a 30% increase over three years on an average of 42 people. Operating profit rose with it, £2,254,155 to £2,446,968 in the latest year, and £850,000 was paid up to the German parent as a dividend. The directors' own going concern note tells you where the confidence comes from: medi UK has "developed alternative routes to market and launched successful brand-new product concepts", and has agreed a five-year extension from August 2025 with its UK service provider Limbco.

prose: Turnover, every figure read from tagged (iXBRL) accounts at Companies House: £18,317,661 for the year to 31 December 2022, £20,052,001 for 2023, £21,893,050 for 2024 and £23,854,087 for 2025. Year on year that is 9.5%, 9.2% and 9.0%, and 30.2% across the three years. Very few suppliers in this dataset show three consecutive years of growth that steady, and none of it is acquisition: the register shows no previous names and the accounts show no business combinations.

Margin has stayed high and moved very little. Gross profit was £10,516,059 in 2024 and £11,235,538 in 2025, which is 48.0% then 47.1% of turnover. That is a manufacturer's margin, not a distributor's, and it is roughly ten points above the distributors in this batch. Distribution costs rose from £3,027,492 to £3,235,486 and administrative expenses from £5,234,412 to £5,553,084 - both growing more slowly than turnover.

Operating profit was £2,254,155 in 2024 and £2,446,968 in 2025, so operating margin held at about 10.3%. Profit before taxation was £2,283,514 then £2,469,628, and profit for the financial year £1,709,605 then £1,839,484. Interest is immaterial in both years: this is trading profit, not financing.

The company is cash-generative enough to pay dividends up to Germany in both years - £1,500,000 in 2024 and £850,000 in 2025 - while still adding to reserves, which closed 2025 at £6,054,355. The directors' going concern note names two things behind the trading position: alternative routes to market and new product concepts, and a five-year service contract extension agreed from August 2025 with the UK service provider Limbco, which they say allows for stability across their trading. No group turnover is quoted here: medi Holdings 2009 GmbH is a German company and files no UK-readable turnover.

ownership: MEDI UK LTD, company number 02110690, registered office Plough Lane, Hereford HR4 0EL, is an active private limited company incorporated on 13 March 1987, SIC 46460, wholesale of pharmaceutical goods. There are no previous company names on the register. Called up share capital is 100,000 ordinary shares of £1.

Note 18 of the accounts for the year ended 31 December 2025 states the position in the company's own words: medi Holdings 2009 GmbH, incorporated in Germany, is regarded by the directors as the company's ultimate parent company. Note 8 records that dividends were paid to it directly. The parent also gave a going concern assurance recorded in the accounting policies: it has confirmed it will continue to provide support as and when required for at least twelve months from the date the financial statements were signed.

Two of the three ownership facts previously held in this record's background note are now confirmed from the filing itself - the German parent and the family-owned group - and the third, the medi GmbH & Co. KG operating name, is not asserted here because it does not appear in anything read this session. What does appear, and is worth knowing, is a UK operational dependency: the directors name Limbco as the UK service provider and record a five-year contract extension from August 2025.

press.text: NHS Supply Chain's Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions framework (2025/S 000-032216) started, running to 3 August 2028 with 40 named suppliers, medi UK among them. From NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch brief, captured into this record 31/08/2026. This is the newest of the company's four verified framework positions.

Medi UK Ltd filed its accounts for the year ended 31 December 2025 at Companies House, reporting turnover of £23,854,087, a third consecutive year of growth, and an £850,000 dividend to its German parent.

The company agreed a five-year extension of its service contract with its UK service provider, Limbco. Recorded by the directors in the going concern note to the accounts for the year ended 31 December 2025, where they say it allows for stability in all areas of their trading. The accounts give the month, not a day.

hiring: No vacancy source was read in this session and this supplier is not covered by this repo's rotating careers collector, so nothing is asserted about live openings. The useful context is the ratio rather than a count: 42 people carrying £23,854,087 of turnover is roughly £568,000 each, and turnover has grown 30.2% over three years. A business growing at that rate on a headcount that small either hires or changes how it sells, and the directors' own note points at the second - alternative routes to market, new product concepts, and a five-year service contract with Limbco.
marketPosition: The measurable part of medi UK's NHS position is its framework footprint, and the rule used here is narrow: a framework counts only where NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch brief names this supplier. On that test there are four, all captured 31/08/2026 - Advanced Wound Care (1 September 2025 to 31 August 2027, 56 suppliers), Orthotics, Podiatry and Immobilisation (3 March 2025 to 2 March 2027, 63 suppliers), Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions (4 August 2026 to 3 August 2028, 40 suppliers) and Vascular Therapy and Associated Products (28 February 2024 to 27 February 2028, 23 suppliers).

Those four line up with what the company actually makes. medi is a compression and orthotics manufacturer, and the Hub's crawl of mediuk.co.uk's XML sitemap, verified 25/08/2026, captured 173 products led by the mediven compression range and by orthotic supports - Mediven Elegance, medi Arm Sling, medi Arm Fix, medi SAS Multi and so on. Names are derived from URL segments rather than read from a product record, so they show range breadth rather than a catalogue.

There is a scope caveat in this record worth naming. The supplier's speciality tag in the seed is Wound care alone, which does not describe a compression and orthotics manufacturer sitting on the Orthotics, Podiatry and Immobilisation framework alongside 62 other suppliers. That is a gap in the Hub's own tagging, not a fact about the company, and under the Differentiator Phase A rule no speciality has been added to this record in this run.

Two rows in the frameworks array are not counted in the four and should not be quoted as current: an undated NHS Supply Chain Advanced Wound Care row marked 'verify lot at source', which duplicates the verified row, and an NHS SBS SBS10142 reference carried from the Hub's retired supplier directory. No market share is stated and none is calculable from anything read this session.

deepDive.interview: Lead with the growth, because it is genuinely unusual and because you can quote it precisely. Turnover has risen in each of the last three years - £18,317,661, £20,052,001, £21,893,050, £23,854,087 - which is 9.5%, then 9.2%, then 9.0%, and 30.2% across three years. Steady is harder than spiky, and a candidate who says so, with the numbers, sounds like someone who reads accounts rather than press releases. Then ask what is behind it, because the directors half-answer it themselves: their going concern note credits alternative routes to market and brand-new product concepts, without saying what either is. That is an open door. The second thing to have straight is the shape of the business. Gross margin is 47.1%, roughly ten points above the distributors this company gets compared with, because medi manufactures compression and orthotic products rather than reselling other people's. And the scale is small: 42 people carrying £23.9m, about £568,000 each. Ask how a team that size covers four NHS Supply Chain frameworks, including Orthotics, Podiatry and Immobilisation where there are 63 named suppliers, and you are asking the resourcing question the sales director thinks about. One detail that will mark you out: the accounts name Limbco as the UK service provider and record a five-year contract extension agreed from August 2025. Knowing that the fitting and service side is contracted, and asking how the commercial team works with it, is the sort of specific almost no candidate will have.

suppliers.note: Genuine multi-speciality distributor and the UK arm of the Mediq group. Named on ten NHS Supply Chain frameworks, including Enteral Feeding, Bile Bags and Associated Products and Urology and Bowel Management - but framework presence is not product range: the live catalogue range is theatre procedure packs, wound care and infection control (see background, 21/07/2026). Companies House 00062537 — the NHS Supply Chain catalogue names the supplying legal entity as "MEDIQ HEALTHCARE UK LIMITED", and the register holds exactly one active company of that name (MEDIQ HEALTHCARE UK LIMITED). Confirmed by catalogue legal name on 07/08/2026. Merged 21/08/2026 by merge_duplicates.py: one company was showing as 2 suppliers. Folded in: "Mediq Healthcare Uk Limited Ex Bunzl Hea". Company number 00062537. One company written two ways. NHSSC's contract launch brief for Respiratory Solutions (1 August 2022 to 15 June 2027, 37 suppliers) lists the supplier as "Mediq Healthcare Uk Limited Ex Bunzl Hea" - the brief's own former-name designation, truncated. The Companies House register settles it: MEDIQ HEALTHCARE UK LIMITED (00062537, Mediq House, Castle Donington) was registered BUNZL RETAIL & HEALTHCARE SUPPLIES LIMITED until 12/06/2023, and no company of the NHSSC spelling exists on the register. The survivor already carries the confirmed number and the financials record; the folded record had neither. Checked at the register and against the brief on 21/08/2026. Company number re-checked at the register on 21/08/2026 and independently corroborated by the company's own website footer, which publishes “Registered number 0062537” (https://www.mediq.co.uk/). Merged 21/08/2026 by merge_duplicates.py: one company was showing as 2 suppliers. Folded in: "Bunzl Retail & Healthcare Supplies Ltd". Company number 00062537. The same legal entity under its pre-2023 registered name. Companies House shows MEDIQ HEALTHCARE UK LIMITED (00062537) with BUNZL RETAIL & HEALTHCARE SUPPLIES LIMITED as a previous name, ceased 12/06/2023; the only other register hit for that name is NF004224, an oversea-company registration that is converted-closed and never traded as a separate business. The folded record's two NHSSC framework rows (Examination Gloves 2023/S 000-016807 and Infusion Pumps Project_12 ITT_382) are Mediq's and move with it. Checked at the register on 21/08/2026; merged on Lou's decision the same day. MERGED 03/09/2026 per the Identity Decision Pack (02-Elevate-and-Thrive/Hub/company-aliases/IDENTITY-DECISION-PACK-2026-09-03.md), §1(e): Companies House 00062537 MEDIQ HEALTHCARE UK LIMITED carries BUNZL RETAIL & HEALTHCARE SUPPLIES LIMITED as a previous name — one number, both names — corroborated by Mediq's own legal page (mediq.co.uk, company number 0062537, VAT GB 286 014 266, same registered office) and by NHS Supply Chain naming the same account both ways ("Bunzl Retail & Healthcare Supplies Ltd" on Examination Gloves 2023/S 000-016807, "Mediq Healthcare Uk Limited Ex Bunzl Hea" on Respiratory Solutions). Folded in the 'Bunzl Healthcare' record and its Extension Sets and Lines framework. Bunzl Catering and Bunzl UK Ltd are SEPARATE live SCCL accounts retained by Bunzl plc after the December 2022 divestment and must never be aliased here — recorded as distinct in alias-overlay.json.

voice.angle: one national distribution centre, one relationship
voice.line: Mediq consolidated four sites into a single national distribution centre in 2024 and is absorbing H & R Healthcare's trade - so lead with breadth of range through one account, and expect a buyer who has been sold consolidation already. With 61 people in selling against £155m of turnover, coverage is thin on the ground: that is where a specialist competitor wins, and where Mediq will push its framework coverage instead.

background.heading: Group and ownership
background.text: The UK company sits under Mediq Holding UK Limited (Companies House 12477997, same Castle Donington address); the filed accounts name Mediq Top Holding B.V. as the ultimate controlling company and record its written confirmation of continued financial support. The Mediq group has been owned by Advent International since 2013; Bloomberg reported in November 2024 that Advent had revived a sale process valuing the group at about €1 billion. No completed sale was found as at 21/08/2026 — an October 2025 Irish CCPC merger notice still describes Mediq International B.V. as ultimately controlled by Mediq Top Holding B.V., a portfolio company of Advent International, in its acquisition of Medguard Healthcare. Treat the ownership position as live and re-check before quoting it. Sources: filed accounts for FY2024 (notes 1 and 19); https://www.ccpc.ie/enforcement-and-regulation/mergers/find-a-merger-case/details/advent-international-medguard

background.heading: Filed accounts, year ended 31 December 2024
background.text: Read directly from the full accounts filed at Companies House on 14/03/2025 (a scanned PDF, so these figures were read off the page, not parsed). Turnover £155,094,000 for the 12 months to 31/12/2024, against £187,176,000 for the FIFTEEN-month period to 31/12/2023 — the two are not comparable, and the directors’ own strategic report puts underlying sales growth against the previous 12 months at 3.7%, with increasing sales into both the NHS and the private sector. Operating loss £4,481,000, which the strategic report says includes £6,202,000 of one-off costs for business restructure and site consolidation. Loss before tax £6,645,000; loss for the year £5,131,000; net assets £16,223,000 (2023: £20,354,000). Turnover by destination: UK £151,472,000, Europe £3,501,000, Rest of World £121,000. No dividend was paid in 2024 (2023: £68,400,000). Source: https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/00062537/filing-history

background.heading: Headcount — and the size of the sales force
background.text: Average monthly headcount in 2024 was 352 (2023 period: 351), split Selling 61 (2023: 71), Distribution and warehouse 227 (2023: 216), General and administration 64 (2023: 64). Aggregate payroll £16,249,000. A selling headcount of 61 against £155m of turnover is roughly £2.5m of revenue per salesperson, and selling headcount fell by ten over the year while warehouse headcount rose by eleven — consistent with the distribution-centre consolidation described in the same accounts. Source: note 7, https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/00062537/filing-history

background.heading: One national distribution centre since 2024
background.text: The strategic report records that during 2024 the business “underwent significant restructure” with four sites consolidated into one national distribution centre, alongside new systems, which the directors say gives “significant scope for future product and customer expansion”. The £6.2m of one-off costs in the year are that programme. Registered office and hub: Mediq House, Arundel Avenue, Castle Donington, Derby DE74 2HJ. Source: https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/00062537/filing-history

background.heading: H & R Healthcare’s trade moved into this company on 01/01/2025
background.text: Post balance sheet events (note 19) record that on 1 January 2025, as part of a group reorganisation, the trade, assets and liabilities of H & R Healthcare Limited were transferred to this company at a book value of £3,258,000, and the strategic report says the intention is full integration. H & R Healthcare Limited (Companies House 05817827, Melton, Hull) remains an active company at 21/08/2026 and the Hub holds it as a separate supplier record with its own NHS Supply Chain framework rows — those rows are correct, but commercially the two are now one operation under Mediq Holding UK Limited. The records are deliberately NOT merged: they are two live registered companies, and NHSSC still names H & R separately. Sources: https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/00062537/filing-history ; https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/05817827

background.heading: What the company itself says it sells
background.text: Mediq UK’s own site (read 21/08/2026) groups its range as surgical supplies (face protection, gowns, drapes, theatre consumables), clinical care (diagnostics, injection/infusion, oxygen therapy, patient care, urology), infection control (hand hygiene, PPE, sharps and waste, medical gloves) and wound care, and names 365 Healthcare, Cardinal Health, Hartmann, Klinion/Kliniderm, PolyMem and Safecare among the brands it carries alongside own-brand lines. It states its customers as NHS trusts and community services, private clinics, care homes, pharmacies, distributors, pack manufacturers and procurement hubs. The footer also carries GB, XI (Northern Ireland) and IE VAT registrations, consistent with the accounts showing £3.5m of turnover into Europe. Source: https://www.mediq.co.uk/

background.heading: MHRA wholesale dealer's licence — Mediq can wholesale medicines
background.text: Mediq Healthcare UK Limited holds wholesale distribution authorisation UK WDA(H) 34759 for medicinal products for human use at Mediq House, Castle Donington, covering procurement, holding, supply and import, for Prescription Only Medicines, Pharmacy medicines, General Sales List medicines and homeopathic products. The authorisation document is dated 14/08/2026, so it is current as at 21/08/2026 (that date is the document date on the register entry, not an expiry). Commercially this puts Mediq in a different bracket from a device-and-consumables distributor. Source: https://cms.mhra.gov.uk/mhra/wda/uk-wdah-34759

background.heading: The Castle Donington site
background.text: The company announced its HQ relocation to Castle Donington on 07/08/2024, together with a new office at Cheshunt (https://mediq.co.uk/mediq-uk-relocates-headquarters-to-castle-donington). Trade press reported the site as 280,000 sq ft at the East Midlands Distribution Centre, built at a cost of £30m including a £6m fit-out (TheBusinessDesk East Midlands, 18/04/2024) — trade-press figures, attributed as such, corroborated by the company's own relocation announcement but not by any filing. The accounts confirm the four-into-one consolidation independently.

background.heading: Third record folded in (21/08/2026) — the pre-2023 registered name
