background.heading: Speciality re-tagging
background.text: SIRT (selective internal radiation therapy) is a percutaneous, catheter-based procedure performed by interventional radiologists within a hepatobiliary/liver MDT -- IR is the operating speciality, oncology the referring/MDT context. NHS England routinely commissions SIRT specifically for chemotherapy-refractory/intolerant, unresectable colorectal cancer liver metastases (per the 2014-2017 Commissioning through Evaluation review with NICE, Oct 2017); SIRT for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma is explicitly NOT routinely commissioned. Routine-commissioning status for primary HCC specifically could not be confirmed either way.
background.source: NHS England specialised commissioning policy library / British Liver Trust

background.heading: Product attribution correction
background.text: Owned since 2018 by a consortium of CDH Genetech (CDH Investments) and China Grand Pharmaceutical and Healthcare Holdings (Grand Pharma 51% / CDH 49%), delisted from the ASX 24/09/2018 -- no ownership change found since. Main competing product is TheraSphere Y-90 glass microspheres, which belongs to Boston Scientific (via its 2019 BTG acquisition), NOT Sirtex -- do not conflate the two companies' Y-90 products or their respective dosimetry software (Sirtex/MIM's SurePlan LiverY90 vs Boston Scientific/Mirada Medical's Simplicit90Y).

deepDive.tagline: FTSE 100 medical technology group founded in Hull in 1856, on 4 confirmed NHS Supply Chain frameworks -- and the UK entity behind the NHS business turns over £653.1m with 1,119 people, 405 of them in marketing, selling and distribution

links.label: Companies House -- Smith & Nephew Healthcare Limited (00156031)

deepDive.lede: Smith+Nephew is the rarest thing in this Hub's supplier list: a global medical technology major that is genuinely British, founded in Hull in 1856, still manufacturing there, and listed on the FTSE 100 (LSE:SN, NYSE:SNN) with sales of $6.2bn in 2025 across three global business units -- Orthopaedics, Sports Medicine & ENT, and Advanced Wound Management. The UK legal structure is worth understanding before an interview, because the name on the NHS Supply Chain contract is not the company with the money in it. NHS Supply Chain's own briefs name "Smith & Nephew Healthcare Ltd" (company 00156031), and that company filed dormant-company accounts for the year to 31 December 2025 on 13 July 2026 and gives its own nature of business as SIC 74990, non-trading. The trading entity is T.J.Smith and Nephew,Limited (00093994), incorporated in 1907 and registered at 101 Hessle Road, Hull: turnover of £653.1m in the year to 31 December 2025, profit before tax of £100.3m, and an average of 1,119 employees, of whom 405 sit in marketing, selling and distribution. Its own directors' report states that it acts as principal in an agency relationship with Smith and Nephew Medical Limited and Smith and Nephew Orthopaedics Limited as agents, who collect income and purchase goods for its account. Four confirmed NHS Supply Chain frameworks sit on this supplier's record, including Negative Pressure Wound Therapy, on which NHS Supply Chain's own brief names just six suppliers.

stats.l: UK entity turnover, year to 31 December 2025
stats.n: £653,051,000, against £637,504,000 in the year to 31 December 2024, an increase of £15,547,000 or 2.4%. Read from the profit and loss account (page 19) of the full audited accounts of T.J.Smith and Nephew,Limited (00093994) for the year ended 31 December 2025, signed 14 August 2026 and filed at Companies House on 26 August 2026, read 28/08/2026. The strategic report attributes the increase primarily to strong performance in the Advanced Wound Care and Bioactives products. Note 3 splits the turnover by geographical market: United Kingdom £186,260,000, Continental Europe £192,116,000, America £127,006,000, and Africa, Asia, Latin America and Australia £147,669,000 -- so this is a UK manufacturer and exporter, and only about 28.5% of its turnover is sold in the UK. Cost of sales was £355,902,000 and gross profit £297,149,000, a gross margin of 45.5% against 41.7% the year before.

Average monthly number of persons (including one director) employed during the year, from note 5 of the same filing: production 434, marketing, selling and distribution 405, administration 41, research and development 239. The comparative for 2024 is 1,192, split 500 / 392 / 50 / 250 -- so headcount fell by 73 overall while the marketing, selling and distribution line grew by 13 and production fell by 66. Aggregate remuneration was £86,551,000 (wages and salaries £66,315,000, social security £10,067,000, pension £7,562,000, share-based payments £2,607,000). This figure and the profit and loss account were both re-read from the rendered page image, because the filing is a scanned PDF and the text extraction misread the 2025 total.

Named supplier, confirmed against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs and captured into this supplier's frameworks array on 24/08/2026: Advanced Wound Care (1 September 2025 to 31 August 2027, 56 suppliers), Negative Pressure Wound Therapy (29 March 2021 to 28 March 2027, 6 suppliers), Total Orthopaedic Solutions 3 (1 February 2024 to 30 January 2028, 106 suppliers) and Urology and Bowel Management (21 February 2024 to 20 February 2027, 57 suppliers). Three further entries on this supplier's record -- an NHS SBS reference carried from the Hub's retired supplier directory, and duplicate general references to TOS3 and Advanced Wound Care -- are not confirmed against a brief and are not counted in the 4. Being one of six named suppliers on the Negative Pressure Wound Therapy brief is the tightest framework position this supplier holds.

stats.l: Profit before taxation, UK entity FY2025
stats.n: £100,332,000 against £67,077,000 in 2024, from the profit and loss account in the same filing. Operating profit was £97,161,000 against £65,297,000, on total operating expenses that were essentially flat at £199,988,000 (2024: £200,235,000). Research and development costs were £34,234,000, down from £39,792,000; marketing, selling and distribution costs were £90,734,000, up from £79,120,000. Profit for the financial year was £90,191,000 against £63,806,000. No dividend was declared or paid for either year. Audited by Deloitte LLP (Cameron Cooley, senior statutory auditor), report dated 14 August 2026.

Smith & Nephew plc's Half-Year Report, released to the London Stock Exchange on 4 August 2026 for the half ended 27 June 2026: revenue $3,097m, underlying growth 2.3% and reported growth 4.6% after a 230bps currency tailwind; trading profit $566m, up 8.1%, with the trading profit margin up 60bps to 18.3%; operating profit $448m, up 4.3%; EPSA up 11.0% to 47.7 cents; interim dividend up 4.0% to 15.6 cents. Q2 revenue was $1,597m with underlying growth of 1.6%, which the company attributes to continued strength in Sports Medicine offset by softness in US Orthopaedics and Advanced Wound Bioactives. Full-year revenue guidance was cut in the same statement, from around 6% to around 4%; trading profit, free cash flow and adjusted ROIC guidance were unchanged. The group reported annual sales of $6.2bn for 2025.

ownership: T.J.SMITH AND NEPHEW,LIMITED, company number 00093994, was incorporated on 2 July 1907 and is active, registered at 101 Hessle Road, Hull HU3 2BN, with SIC codes 20590 (manufacture of other chemical products) and 32500 (manufacture of medical and dental instruments and supplies). This is the entity that files the turnover, profit and headcount figures above. Its sole person with significant control is Smith & Nephew Trading Group Limited (UK company 00681256), notified on 6 April 2016 as holding 75% or more of the shares and voting rights and the right to appoint or remove directors.

SMITH & NEPHEW HEALTHCARE LIMITED, company number 00156031, is the entity NHS Supply Chain's own briefs name as the supplier on the Urology and Bowel Management framework, and it is the company number this Hub's Companies House record for Smith+Nephew is matched to. It is active and incorporated on 13 June 1919, but its registered nature of business is SIC 74990, non-trading company, and it filed accounts for a dormant company made up to 31 December 2025 on 13 July 2026. Both facts are stated on its own Companies House record, read 28/08/2026. Nothing is inferred here about how the NHS contract is serviced -- the point for a member is only that the named contracting entity files no turnover, no headcount and no accounts of substance, and that the operating figures for this supplier have to be read from 00093994 instead.

SMITH & NEPHEW PLC, company number 00324357, incorporated 17 February 1937, is the listed ultimate parent, registered at Building 5, Croxley Park, Hatters Lane, Watford, Hertfordshire WD18 8YE. A separate SMITH & NEPHEW UK LIMITED (04421171, incorporated 19 April 2002, also at Croxley Park) carries SIC 70100, activities of head offices; it is a head-office company rather than the trading one, and its number should not be used for the manufacturing or NHS-facing business.

The directors' report of T.J.Smith and Nephew,Limited states that an agency relationship exists between that company as principal and Smith and Nephew Medical Limited and Smith and Nephew Orthopaedics Limited as agents, the agents being authorised to collect income and fees for the principal's account and to purchase goods and services on its behalf. The same report records that Smith & Nephew plc has given a letter of support committing to fund the company as required for at least twelve months from the date the accounts were approved, and that the company had net current assets of £265,091,000.

deepDive.peopleNote: All four directors of the trading entity are British and UK-resident, and three of the four give the Hull site as their correspondence address -- unusual in this Hub's supplier list, where most large medtech UK subsidiaries are run by a small board of overseas-resident officers. That is a statutory register fact about the legal entity, not a claim about who runs UK commercial teams day to day. No UK country manager, sales director or business unit head was found and verified as a Companies House officer in this session, and this routine does not access LinkedIn: treat UK commercial leadership as Not verified and check nearer interview date on the company's own site. Group-level names above come from Smith & Nephew plc's own regulatory announcements, not from the register.
hiring: Smith+Nephew's own Workday careers board (smithnephew.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/External) returned 42 postings against a United Kingdom search on 28/08/2026, and roughly a quarter of them are customer-facing commercial roles: Account Manager (Wound Care) in Central London, Account Manager (Trauma & Extremities) in Birmingham, Account Manager (Orthopaedics) across three locations, Account Manager (Sports Medicine) at the Hull GBU office, Senior Orthopaedic Sales Specialist across four locations, Sales Associate (Knee Specialist cover) UK-Field, Surgical Solutions Manager for both Sports Medicine (Liverpool) and Orthopaedics (Central London), Commercial Manager - Recon UK-Field, Complex Wound Specialist across three locations, Surgical Training Specialist at Watford and a Medical Education Manager for Non-Healing Wounds UK-Field.

The rest of the board is heavily weighted to Hull and Watford rather than the field: Senior Analytical Chemist, Junior Manufacturing Engineer, Quality Engineer, Quality Engineering Lead, Director of Operational Excellence and a Senior Director, Site Lead for Hull & Melton all sit at the Hull manufacturing site, alongside Global Master Planner and Global Asset Operations Manager roles for Advanced Wound Management at the Hull GBU office. Watford carries the group functions -- legal, finance, IT and a cluster of SAP S/4HANA and AI transformation posts. For a candidate, that mix is the tell: this is a UK employer with real manufacturing, R&D and global-function jobs behind the sales roles, not a sales office with a warehouse attached.
marketPosition: The verifiable NHS measure is the same one this Hub uses throughout: named supplier on 4 NHS Supply Chain frameworks, each confirmed against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch brief -- Advanced Wound Care, Negative Pressure Wound Therapy, Total Orthopaedic Solutions 3, and Urology and Bowel Management. That is a framework count, not a revenue or market-share figure, and nothing here is inferred from the product list. The Negative Pressure Wound Therapy brief names 6 suppliers in total, so that is a narrow field; Total Orthopaedic Solutions 3 names 106 and Advanced Wound Care 56, which are not.

At group level the half-year picture is mixed and the company said so itself on 4 August 2026: H1 underlying revenue growth of 2.3% with the full-year outlook cut from around 6% to around 4%, against trading profit up 8.1% and margin up 60bps. The company attributed Q2's 1.6% underlying growth to strength in Sports Medicine offset by softness in US Orthopaedics and Advanced Wound Bioactives. Two UK-relevant items sit in the same statement: a $51m increase in first-half capital expenditure relating largely to the construction of a new UK Wound factory, and 90bps of trading-profit dilution from the acquisition of Integrity Orthopaedics, the deal Reuters and MedTech Dive reported on 12 January 2026 at up to $450m and which is already recorded in this supplier's press.

The UK trading entity's own strategic report adds two structural facts a candidate would not otherwise see. The Warwick manufacturing facility, which produced Birmingham Hip Resurfacing products, closed in early 2025, and manufacturing is now concentrated at Hull and Suzhou. And the company reassessed its provision for metal-on-metal hip claims during 2025, recognising a net credit of £367,000 against a charge of £1,848,000 the year before; the underlying claims are brought against Smith & Nephew Orthopaedics Limited, which T.J.Smith and Nephew,Limited has financially indemnified.

Coordinates approximate: HU3 2BN is recorded as a terminated postcode in the ONS postcode dataset (terminated December 2018, as large-user postcodes routinely are), and the latitude and longitude are the ones held against that record, read 28/08/2026.

deepDive.interview: Three things are worth knowing before this one. First, get the entity right. NHS Supply Chain contracts name Smith & Nephew Healthcare Ltd, and that company files dormant accounts and registers itself as non-trading; the business you would actually be joining reports through T.J.Smith and Nephew,Limited in Hull, which turned over £653.1m in 2025 and employs 1,119 people. Knowing that distinction, and that the UK company acts as principal with Smith and Nephew Medical and Smith and Nephew Orthopaedics as its agents, is the kind of detail that separates a candidate who has read the accounts from one who has read the website. Second, know where the growth is and is not. The group cut its full-year revenue guidance from around 6% to around 4% on 4 August 2026, naming softness in US Orthopaedics and Advanced Wound Bioactives against continued strength in Sports Medicine -- so if you are interviewing into Sports Medicine you are interviewing into the part that is working, and if you are interviewing into Orthopaedics or Bioactives you should have a view on what turns it round. Third, the UK story is genuinely a manufacturing one: founded in Hull in 1856, still making advanced wound management products there, with a new UK Wound factory under construction absorbing a $51m step-up in first-half capex, and Warwick closed in early 2025 with production consolidated to Hull and Suzhou. On the NHS side, being one of six named suppliers on the Negative Pressure Wound Therapy framework is the single strongest framework position this supplier holds, and it is worth asking how they intend to defend it. Note that the group is between CFOs -- John Rogers announced his departure on 19 August 2026 with Pierre Palassian acting as interim -- which usually means cost discipline is front of mind.

deepDive.tagline: The UK and Ireland trading company of the STERIS group: sterilisation and decontamination equipment, endoscope reprocessing, theatre equipment and GI/endoscopy consumables, on ten NHS Supply Chain frameworks, with a Republic of Ireland branch that is roughly a quarter of its turnover.
deepDive.lede: Three things, and the first one will keep you out of trouble. STERIS Solutions Limited has grown turnover from £77.5m to £98.5m to £110.6m across the three years to 31 March 2025, and its own directors attribute the rise in both of the last two years to trade and assets moved in from fellow group companies rather than to business won: the 2024 strategic report says increases "were driven by the acquisition of certain trade and assets from fellow group companies during the prior year", and the 2025 one says the increase was "predominantly driven" by the same thing, contributing an estimated £12m. Turnover rose £12.0m that year. So the underlying number is close to flat, and a growth line quoted off the headline is a line the directors themselves do not make. Second, this is not a UK-only company: of £110.6m in FY2025, £77.9m was United Kingdom and £29.9m was Republic of Ireland, from a branch the accounts say it continues to run. Ireland has sat between £29.4m and £29.9m for three straight years while the UK went from £46.8m to £77.9m, so every pound of growth in this company is a UK pound. Third, the commercial shape: 126 people in Sales out of 258 employees, three fewer than the year before while turnover rose 12%, and £7,000,000 of dividends paid out of a £4,025,978 profit — the strategic report says in terms that shareholder's funds fell because the dividend exceeded the year's profit. The registered office moved from Syston, Leicester to Basingstoke on 31 July 2026.

stats.n: £110,563,286. Read from the line the company itself labels Turnover on the face of its statement of comprehensive income, page 11, and repeated in the key performance indicator table on page 1 and in note 3 on page 20, in the full accounts for the year ended 31 March 2025 filed at Companies House on 20 December 2025 (02767165, 32 pages, audited by Ernst & Young LLP). Prior year £98,543,685. The filing IS tagged iXBRL, but it carries no turnover tag among the tags it does carry, which is why company-financials.json in this Hub shows no turnover for the company while this record does.

£29,885,017 of £110,563,286, or 27.0%, from the turnover-by-geographical-market table in note 3, page 20 of the 2025 accounts. United Kingdom £77,949,106, Rest of the world £2,729,163. The comparatives in the same note and in note 3 of the 2024 accounts give Republic of Ireland £29,435,050 (FY2024) and £29,732,856 (FY2023) against United Kingdom £67,948,380 and £46,795,014. The strategic report states the company "continues to have a branch in the Republic of Ireland".

stats.l: Estimated turnover contributed by the Diagmed transfer, FY2025
stats.n: Note 21 of the 2025 accounts, page 27: "On 1 April 2024 the company acquired the business of Diagmed Healthcare Limited", total identifiable net assets £1,256,210 (inventories £1,359,677, trade and other receivables £1,200, trade and other payables £(104,667)), consideration £1,256,210 satisfied in cash, and "Since the acquisition, it is estimated that the contribution to turnover has been £12m and the contribution to Profit after tax has been £1.4m." Turnover rose £12,019,601 that year. The company's own section 172 statement describes the same transfer, calling the entity "Diagmed Healthcare UK Limited", and says several of its employees continued with STERIS Solutions.

Note 6 of the 2025 accounts, page 21: Sales 126 (2024: 129), Technical support 85 (83), Administration 47 (43), total average monthly number of persons including directors 258 (255). Note 6 of the 2024 accounts gives the FY2023 split as Sales 103, Technical support 61, Administration 40, total 204. So the sales force grew by 26 in FY2024 and fell by 3 in FY2025. Aggregate remuneration FY2025 £21,111,026 — wages and salaries £17,307,388, social security £2,109,790, pension £1,693,848.

£4,726,223, down from £5,359,996, from the statement of comprehensive income on page 11. Gross profit was £36,302,611 against £36,343,616 — flat on £12.0m more sales, so the gross margin fell from 36.9% to 32.8% (percentages computed here from the two figures on that page). The strategic report on page 1 gives the directors' own explanation: "rising costs of raw materials only saw gross profit rise by £2m", distribution expenses rose, and "salaries rising by ~£1m was the main driver in the increase in administrative expenses". Profit before taxation £5,163,053, tax £1,137,075, profit for the financial year £4,025,978.

£7,000,000, from the statement of changes in equity in the 2025 accounts and repeated in the section 172 statement ("The company paid dividends of £7,000,000 during the year to 31 March 2025"). FY2024 £5,000,000 (note 10 of the 2024 accounts, "Final paid"), FY2023 nil. So £12,000,000 has left the company over two years against profits for those financial years of £4,918,863 and £4,025,978. Shareholder's funds fell from £8,536,152 to £5,878,504, and the strategic report says so directly: "The shareholder's funds dropped due to the declaration of a dividend during the year in excess of profit in the year." Current assets as a percentage of current liabilities fell from 119.5% to 107.5% (both figures from the company's own KPI table, page 1).

prose: The split of turnover by class of business, from note 3 of each filing, is worth carrying into a meeting because a third of this company is not product sales. FY2025: sale of goods £86,813,059, sale of services £17,267,465, provision of services to group companies £6,482,762. FY2024: £75,992,736, £15,146,834 and £7,404,115. So services to other STERIS companies were 5.9% of turnover in FY2025 and 7.5% in FY2024 — revenue that has nothing to do with any NHS customer, and which the strategic report reflects when it describes the principal activities as including "the provision of management services to group operations throughout Europe".

Directors' remuneration appears in this company for the first time in FY2025: note 7 gives remuneration for qualifying services £119,325 and company pension contributions £7,432, a total of £126,757, against nil in FY2024. Note 7 of the 2024 accounts explains the nil: "Directors' remuneration for all the directors have been borne by another group company." The audit fee for the audit of the company's own financial statements was £52,347 (FY2024 £51,070).

ownership: STERIS SOLUTIONS LIMITED, company number 02767165, registered office 2200 Renaissance Basing View, Basingstoke, Hampshire, England, RG21 4EQ, is a private limited company incorporated on 24 November 1992 and currently Active, SIC 46460 wholesale of pharmaceutical goods. Its previous registered names, from the register's own table read 23/08/2026, are STERIS LIMITED (2 March 1998 to 20 October 2015), AMSCO (U.K.) LTD. (19 January 1993 to 2 March 1998) and WEIGHTVIEW PROJECTS LIMITED (24 November 1992 to 19 January 1993) — which is why AMSCO, still a live product name in this Hub's range for the company, is also the name this legal entity traded under thirty years ago.

The persons with significant control register, read 23/08/2026, holds one active entry: Steris Dover Limited, company 11241200, incorporated in England, of 2200 Renaissance, Basing View, Basingstoke RG21 4EQ, notified 26 March 2018, holding 75% or more of the shares and 75% or more of the voting rights. The only other entry is a ceased one, Steris Plc, company 09257343, incorporated in England, of Chancery House, 190 Waterside Road, Hamilton Industrial Park, Leicester LE5 1QZ, notified 6 April 2016 and ceased 26 March 2018.

The accounts describe the chain differently from the PSC register, and both are recorded here rather than reconciled, because reconciling them would be a guess. Note 24 of the 2025 accounts states: "The company's immediate parent undertaking is STERIS Holdings BV, a company incorporated in the Netherlands. The ultimate parent undertaking and controlling party is STERIS plc a company incorporated and domiciled in Ireland. The largest and smallest group for which consolidated financial statements are prepared is STERIS plc", with copies available from its registered office at 70 Sir John Rogerson's Quay, Dublin 2, D02 R296, Ireland. So the register names an English company as the controller and the accounts name a Dutch immediate parent and an Irish ultimate parent. What is not in doubt is that the UK trading company is a subsidiary several layers below a listed group, and that its dividend policy is set above it.

The registered office moved on 31 July 2026. The AD01 filed that day records the change "from Chancery House Rayns Way, Watermead Business Park Syston Leicester LE7 1PF United Kingdom to 2200 Renaissance Basing View Basingstoke Hampshire RG21 4EQ on 31 July 2026". The accounts filed in December 2025 still print the Leicester address. DIAGMED HEALTHCARE LIMITED, company 04707660, whose business this company acquired on 1 April 2024, is registered at the same Basingstoke address, remains Active on the register with accounts last made up to 31 March 2025, and is a separate legal entity from this one. There is no company on the register called Diagmed Healthcare UK Limited, the name the section 172 statement uses.

deepDive.peopleNote: Companies House records 28 officers and 24 resignations for 02767165, leaving three people in four active appointments, all listed above. No commercial leadership is published for the UK company: steris.com is a group site and names no UK managing director, sales director or commercial director, so unlike several other records in this Hub there is no company-published leadership list to set beside the register, and none is invented here. The dated board events on the register since 2016 are: Dennis Patrick Patton resigned as director and as secretary on 30 June 2016, and Julia Kipnis was appointed director and Ronald E Snyder secretary the same day; John Patrick Ubbing was appointed director on 6 September 2022 and Julia Kipnis resigned the same day; Ronald E Snyder resigned as director and as secretary on 30 August 2024; Allan John Rowley was appointed director and John Patrick Ubbing secretary on 16 September 2024; Michael Joseph Tokich resigned as director on 14 November 2025 and Karen Louise Burton was appointed the same day. Those are dated register events only. Nothing here says any person replaced any other, because succession is not a register fact and several of these dates coincide for reasons the register does not give. Two of the three directors are resident in the United States; the practical read for a rep is that UK commercial decisions are unlikely to sit with the statutory board.
marketPosition: The framework footprint is the independently checkable part, and it is broad rather than deep. NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs name this company on ten frameworks, captured for this Hub on 20/08/2026 and listed with their dates, references and supplier counts on the framework panel of this record rather than restated here: Decontamination Capital Equipment, Digital Diagnostic Solutions, Electrosurgical Consumables, Endoscopy Endourology and Oncology Ablation Consumables, Instrument Decontamination and Accessories, Operating Theatres Equipment, Patient Temperature Management, Pressure Area Care and Patient Handling, and Tray Wrap and Sterilisation Equipment. The briefs name it variously as "Steris Solutions Limited", "STERIS Solutions Limited" and "Steris Solutions Ltd", which independently ties the Hub record to company 02767165.

Where the field is small, that place is worth more. On the briefs captured, this company is one of 8 suppliers on Tray Wrap and Sterilisation Equipment, one of 18 on Patient Temperature Management, and one of 20 on each of Instrument Decontamination and Accessories and Decontamination Capital Equipment. On the wider ones it is one of 58 (Endoscopy, Endourology and Oncology Ablation Consumables), one of 54 (Digital Diagnostic Solutions) and one of 53 (Pressure Area Care and Patient Handling). Those counts are the briefs' own and are recorded per framework on this record.

On the product range: this Hub holds 733 items for Steris, read on 07/08/2026 from the steris.com XML sitemap. That is the GROUP's global catalogue, not a UK availability list, and its own division names are American-spelled ("Sterilizers"). The largest divisions are Surgical Table Accessories (245), Endoscopy Devices (119), Sterility Assurance and Monitoring (57), Endoscope Reprocessing (51) and Washing and Decontamination Systems (39). Treat it as the shape of what the group makes, and check NHS Supply Chain or the company before telling a customer any single line is available to them here.

One derived observation, with its rule stated so it can be judged: adding the FY2025 turnover-by-class figures to the FY2025 employee split shows £110,563,286 of turnover against 126 people in Sales, or roughly £0.88m of turnover per sales head, and 85 in Technical support against a business whose principal activities include servicing installed capital equipment. This is a ratio computed here from two figures in the same filing, not a figure the company publishes, and it says nothing about individual quota. What it does suggest is a capital-equipment-and-service model rather than a consumables-volume one, which is consistent with the frameworks it sits on.

Before 31 July 2026 the registered office was Chancery House, Rayns Way, Watermead Business Park, Syston, Leicester LE7 1PF, which is the address printed in the accounts filed in December 2025, and earlier officer records give Chancery House, 190 Waterside Road, Hamilton Industrial Park, Leicester LE5 1QZ. deepDive.interview: Do not quote the growth. Turnover went £77.5m, £98.5m, £110.6m across the three years to March 2025, and the directors attribute both rises to trade moved in from fellow group companies — in FY2025, an estimated £12m of a £12.0m increase, from the Diagmed Healthcare business acquired on 1 April 2024 for £1,256,210 in cash. Saying "you've grown 12%" to someone who signed those accounts will land badly; asking what the Diagmed integration has actually done to their endoscopy coverage will not. Know that Ireland is roughly a quarter of the company — £29.9m of £110.6m — and that it has not moved in three years while the UK has, so if you are being told a UK growth story, the Irish branch is the flat part of it. On margin, the honest read is a business absorbing cost it cannot pass on: gross profit was flat at £36.3m on £12m more sales, the directors name raw material costs, and operating profit fell to £4.73m. And the money leaves: £5m of dividends in FY2024 and £7m in FY2025 against a £4.03m profit, with the strategic report saying plainly that shareholder's funds dropped because the dividend exceeded the profit. That is an owner taking cash out, not reinvesting, which is the opposite of the Mediq picture in this Hub and tells you what a capital business case here has to clear. On people: 126 in Sales, down three while turnover rose, and 85 in Technical support — this is a service-and-capital business, so the service contract is often the real conversation and the installed base is the real barrier. Do not expect the board to be your route in: three directors, two of them resident in the United States, one company secretary who is also a director, and no UK commercial leadership published anywhere. Finally, if you are searching for this company, search all of "Steris Solutions", "STERIS Limited" and "AMSCO" — the register shows all three as names of company 02767165 — and note the registered office moved to Basingstoke on 31 July 2026, so anything filed under Leicester is out of date.

deepDive.tagline: NYSE-listed (SYK), FY2025 group net sales $25.1bn · UK entity Stryker UK Limited, Stryker House, Hambridge Road, Newbury · recovering from a global cyber attack that forced NHS England to run a national stock SitRep in March 2026

links.label: NHS England letter on the disruption

deepDive.lede: The thing worth knowing before this interview: on 11 March 2026 Stryker was hit by a cyber attack that took down its internal Microsoft environment worldwide, halted production and stopped electronic ordering. It was serious enough that NHS England wrote to every acute, community, mental health and ambulance trust, ran a national stock SitRep with a 4pm deadline, cancelled every Stryker order placed between 11 and 16 March, and stood up an interim ordering route through NHS Supply Chain and Stryker's logistics partner DHL. Some patient-specific implant cases were rescheduled. Then the company recovered: Q2 2026 sales were $6.6bn, up 9.4%, and the full-year guidance held. That sequence — a fortnight of disrupted ordering during the cyber attack, followed by a full recovery in the same quarter — is the single most useful thing to have a view on in this interview.

prose: There is no readable UK turnover for Stryker. Stryker UK Limited (company number 03669454) files full accounts, most recently made up to 31 December 2025, but they are filed as a PDF with no tagged figures, so nothing is read from them: picking the turnover line off a PDF by position would be a guess, not a reading. Every financial figure here is therefore group-wide and comes from Stryker's own published releases.

FY2025 was a strong year on any measure. Group net sales reached $25,116m, up 11.2% reported and 10.3% organic, with MedSurg and Neurotechnology up 15.7% to $15,647m and Orthopaedics up 4.3% to $9,469m. The Orthopaedics number understates the underlying business, because Spinal Implants fell 73.9% to $185m after the US spinal implants sale completed on 1 April 2025; strip that out and the rest of Orthopaedics grew 10.9%. Vascular grew 50.6% to $1,968m on the Inari Medical acquisition. Reported operating margin was 19.5%, adjusted 26.3%.

2026 has been the cyber year. Q1 2026 net sales were $6.020bn, up just 2.6%, with reported gross margin pressed to 63.3% by idle production time, and the company missed consensus. Kevin Lobo told investors the incident 'meaningfully' affected growth and hit each business differently depending on its route to market. Q2 2026 then came in at $6.6bn, up 9.4% reported and 9.0% organic, with reported net earnings up 44.3%, and Stryker held its full-year organic growth guidance of 8.0% to 9.5% and adjusted EPS of $14.90 to $15.10.

There is no private-equity or family owner to know about: the relevant ownership fact for a UK candidate is simply that decisions on portfolio, pricing and structure are made in Michigan and land in Newbury.

press.text: Stryker completes the sale of its US spinal implants business to Viscogliosi Brothers, LLC, forming VB Spine, LLC. VB Spine gets exclusive access to Mako Spine and Copilot for use with its implants. Certain international markets were stated as transferring later. Stryker's own release.
Kevin Lobo, Stryker's Chair and CEO, joins GE HealthCare's board of directors, effective this date, per GE HealthCare's own announcement.

Cyber attack causes a global disruption to Stryker's internal Microsoft environment, halting order processing, manufacturing and shipping. Stryker states its products, connected and otherwise, were not affected and remain safe to use.

NHS England issues an EPRR publication (PRN02438) to trust COOs, medical directors, heads of procurement, EPRR and nursing directors: UK stock estimated at around two weeks at normal ordering volumes, orders placed 11 to 16 March cancelled, an interim ordering route stood up via NHS Supply Chain and Stryker's logistics partner DHL, six NHS Supply Chain stocked lines put under Control Demand Management, and a mandatory national SitRep from every acute, community, mental health and ambulance trust by 4pm on 19 March. Trusts told to organise mutual aid and to engage independent-sector providers.

Stryker confirms some patient-specific implant cases scheduled for the week of 16 March were rescheduled because of shipping delays, and thanks the White House National Cyber Director, FBI, CISA, DHA, HHS and H-ISAC for support.

Stryker states the incident is contained. Its investigation with Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 identified a malicious file used to run commands and hide activity, revising the company's earlier position that there was no indication of malware. Unit 42 issued a general assurance letter finding no evidence the threat actor reached customer, supplier, vendor or partner systems.

Stryker completes the acquisition of Amplitude Vascular Systems, adding a CO2-generated pressure wave intravascular lithotripsy platform for complex peripheral arterial disease. Terms undisclosed, closed under a month after announcement.
Q2 2026 results: net sales $6.6bn, up 9.4% reported and 9.0% organic; reported net earnings up 44.3%. Lobo describes 'significant progress in our recovery from the cyber incident'.

hiring: Stryker recruits UK field sales through its own careers site (careers.stryker.com) rather than through a job board feed this pipeline can read, so a live UK vacancy count was not captured in this session and is not asserted. What is verifiable is that Stryker's own guidance during the March 2026 disruption leaned heavily on the field force: customers were told repeatedly to direct all product questions to their local sales representative, that reps would arrange manual ordering where electronic ordering was down, and that it was safe for reps to be on site in hospitals. That is a company whose UK commercial model runs through people in theatres, which is worth knowing before an interview for one of those roles.
marketPosition: Stryker describes itself as 'a global leader in medical technologies' and says it impacts more than 150 million patients annually; those are the company's own words and its own figure, not an independently audited claim, and no verified market-share percentage was found in this session, so none is stated. The clearest UK-specific evidence of scale is its NHS Supply Chain footprint: named supplier on 14 separate live frameworks confirmed against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs, spanning total orthopaedic solutions, operating theatre equipment, surgical navigation, rigid endoscopy, minimally invasive surgery, electrosurgical consumables, wound closure, external defibrillation, pulse oximetry and capnography, pressure area care and patient handling, medical healthcare furniture, CT scanners, electrodes and ultrasound gels, and medical chart paper.

NHS England's own March 2026 letter is a second, blunter measure of position: it lists trust dependency on Stryker across trauma and orthopaedics, neuroradiology including microwires, other surgical technology and consumables, connected devices, rehabilitation and community, diagnostics and equipment services, and facilities and office solutions, and judged the national exposure serious enough to require a return from every acute, community, mental health and ambulance trust. Few suppliers reach that far into an NHS trust.

Pin is the RG14 5AW postcode centroid, not a surveyed building position. Group headquarters is 1941 Stryker Way, Portage, Michigan.

glassdoor.scale: /5 on Glassdoor UK, from 49 reviews by employees based in London, England
glassdoor.summary: 79% of London-based employees would recommend Stryker to a friend. Sub-scores for the London sample: compensation and benefits 3.9, work-life balance 3.6, diversity and inclusion 4.2, culture and values 4.1, career opportunities 4.0, each of which sits below the company-wide equivalent. The company-wide review base is large, over 7,200 reviews, but the company-wide star rating was not captured in this session and is not stated here. Treat a 49-review London sample as indicative, not definitive, and note it is not the same population as the Newbury commercial team.

deepDive.interview: Bring the cyber incident up yourself, carefully. Do not use it as a gotcha; use it to show you understand what a supplier owes an NHS customer. A good question sounds like: what changed in UK order management and business continuity after March, and what would a rep do differently if it happened again? Know the shape of the portfolio too: Stryker sold its US spinal implants business to VB Spine on 1 April 2025 and stayed in spine only through Interventional Spine, Neurotechnology and Enabling Technologies, so do not walk in describing Stryker as a spinal implants company. Know which segment the role sits in, because MedSurg and Neurotechnology grew 15.7% in FY2025 while Orthopaedics grew 4.3% on a reported basis, and the two have very different momentum stories. Mako, Triathlon, LIFEPAK and ProCuity are the names most NHS clinicians will recognise. If the role touches trauma and orthopaedics, expect procurement to remember March 2026 clearly.

deepDive.lede: The most useful thing about this supplier is that almost all of it is British. Turnover for the year to 31 March 2025 was £48,086,638, and note 2 of the same accounts puts £43,199,331 of that in the United Kingdom, roughly nine pounds in ten, with £4,887,306 in Europe. It has grown in every year since the pandemic: £33.0m in the year to March 2021, £48.1m four years later. Do not read the profit line as a performance signal, though. The strategic report says in terms that the company "acts as a Limited Risk Distributor (LRD) for Terumo Europe" and that Terumo "operate a LRD model with a targeted profit before tax (3.5%-4%), achieved through a transfer pricing agreement with Terumo Europe N.V, the parent company". Profit before tax came in at £2,300,900, which is 4.8% of turnover. A number a transfer pricing agreement is designed to produce says very little about how well the UK business is trading. The third thing to know is how small the UK team is: an average of 54 people across the whole company in FY2025, every one of them filed under the single heading Sales and administration, with all research and development at group level and, in the company's own wording, "no key management personnel noted in Terumo UK Ltd".

stats.n: £48,086,638, against £44,139,870 in the year to 31 March 2024. Read from the line the company itself labels Turnover on the face of its profit and loss account, page 12, in the audited accounts of TERUMO UK LIMITED (04571001) for the year ended 31 March 2025, filed at Companies House on 17 April 2026 and audited by WP Audit Limited (Philippa Duckworth, senior statutory auditor, signed 1 April 2026). The same figure is printed again in the company's own key performance indicator table on page 5. This filing is a scanned PDF with no iXBRL tagging and no text layer, which is why this Hub's company-financials.json shows no turnover for the company while this record does.

stats.l: Of which sold in the United Kingdom
stats.n: Note 2 of the same filing, page 20, analysis of turnover by geographical market: UK £43,199,331 (2024: £39,792,342), Europe £4,887,306 (2024: £4,347,528). This is the company's own split, not an estimate. It is worth knowing because the UK entities of several other multinational suppliers on these frameworks book most of their turnover outside the UK, so a headline turnover figure is not comparable between them without this note.

Note 4, page 20, average number of persons employed by the company including directors, analysed by category: Sales and administration 54 (2024: 52), and that single category is the whole total. Aggregate payroll cost was £3,674,285 (2024: £3,740,552), made up of wages and salaries £2,523,605 (2024: £2,716,077), social security £368,961 (2024: £359,705) and other pension costs £781,719 (2024: £664,770). Headcount rose by two while wages and salaries fell by £192,472; the accounts give no explanation for that and none is asserted here.

stats.l: Profit before tax as a share of turnover, against a group target of 3.5% to 4%
stats.n: Profit on ordinary activities before taxation of £2,300,900 on turnover of £48,086,638, both from the profit and loss account on page 12, is 4.78%. The company's own key performance indicator table on page 5 prints the same 4.8%. Read it alongside the sentence beneath that table: "Terumo operate a LRD model with a targeted profit before tax (3.5%-4%), achieved through a transfer pricing agreement with Terumo Europe N.V, the parent company." One caution on that table, because a reader could otherwise quote a trend that is not there: it prints the prior year's net profit before tax margin as 3.6%, while the same table's own 2024 figures, £2,121,754 on £44,139,870, work out at 4.8%. The 2024 percentage as printed does not reconcile with the 2024 pounds as printed. The pound figures are used here and the percentage is not.

Treated in the accounts as a non-adjusting event under FRS 102. Separately, the directors' report on page 3 records a dividend of £1,503,000 approved during the year in respect of the year ended March 2024 and paid to Terumo Europe N.V. on 10 April 2025, and says no dividend had yet been declared for the current year.

Derivation, so you can judge it: this Hub holds seven framework entries against this supplier, and counted by distinct notice reference they are four framework subjects, not seven. Syringes, Needles and Associated Products (2026/S 000-002484) is held twice, once from the Find a Tender award notice and once from NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch brief. Intravenous Cannula and Associated Products is held twice because both the outgoing framework (2022/S 000-005941, 27 March 2023 to 31 March 2027) and its replacement (2026/S 000-078334, awarded 6 July 2026) are recorded, which is one framework subject across two terms. The other two are Endoscopy, Endourology and Oncology Ablation Consumables and Associated Products (2024/S 000-029975, 58 suppliers) and Perfusion Devices, Consumables and Associated Equipment (2024/S 000-033613, 9 suppliers). The seventh entry is a catalogue listing (Surflo, FSB524) carrying no notice reference, so it is not counted as a framework. prose: The shape is a pandemic dip and a long recovery. Turnover fell from £39.2m in the year to March 2020 to £33.0m in the year to March 2021, a drop of 15.7%, which is what you would expect of a company whose stated focus is interventional cardiology, endovascular and cardio-vascular systems: those are largely planned procedures, and planned procedures were what stopped. It then took two years to get back to where it started, £39.5m and £39.6m in the years to March 2022 and March 2023, before adding £4.6m and then £3.9m in the two years since. FY2025 is 46% above FY2021 (£48,086,638 against £33,018,035) and 22.8% above the pre-pandemic FY2020.

The company gives its own reasons for the most recent year, and they are worth having in front of you before a price conversation. The strategic report names two drivers of the increase: "Implementation of price adjustments across the entire product portfolio" and "Expansion of the product portfolio with the launch of new products". It introduces those as three key factors and then lists two; the third is not printed. Gross profit rose from £8,645,328 to £9,107,611 while gross margin fell from 19.6% to 18.9%, both figures as printed in the company's own key performance indicator table on page 5, so the extra gross profit came from volume and price rather than from a better margin.

Read the whole series with the transfer pricing arrangement in mind. Turnover here is a real measure of what the company sold in the United Kingdom, and note 2 confirms nine tenths of it was. Profit is not a comparable measure, because the accounts say it is targeted at 3.5% to 4% before tax by agreement with the parent.

ownership: TERUMO UK LIMITED, company number 04571001, registered office Building 2 Ground Floor, Meadows Business Park, Blackwater, Camberley, Surrey GU17 9AB, is a private limited company incorporated on 23 October 2002 and currently Active, SIC 47789 (other retail sale of new goods in specialised stores). It has held one previous name, TERUMO EUROPE UK LIMITED, from incorporation until 1 April 2003. Its accounting reference date is 31 March; the last accounts filed are for the year ended 31 March 2025 and the next are due by 31 December 2026.

Ownership runs Camberley to Leuven to Tokyo, and the accounts and the register agree on it. Note 18 of the FY2025 accounts, page 25, says the company "is controlled by Terumo Europe N.V. by virtue of it holding 100% of the allotted share capital" and that "the ultimate controlling party is Terumo Corporation, registered in Japan". The smallest group in which the results are consolidated is headed by Terumo Europe N.V. of Research Park Zone 2, Interleuvenlaan 40, 3001 Leuven, Belgium; the largest is headed by Terumo Corporation of 2-44-1 Hatagaya, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo 151-0072, Japan. Companies House carries a single active person with significant control, Terumo Corporation, at that same Tokyo address, notified on 6 April 2016, governing law Japan, legal form Corporation, place registered Ministry of Justice, registration number 0110-01-015116, holding 75% or more of shares and of voting rights and the right to appoint or remove directors.

The relationship with the parent is not only ownership, it is the commercial model. The strategic report states that "Terumo UK Ltd acts as a Limited Risk Distributor (LRD) for Terumo Europe", that "All research and development occur at Group level", and that the central treasury function of Terumo Europe N.V. is responsible for the availability and flexibility of funding and for managing the group's and the company's credit, interest rate, liquidity and foreign exchange risk. Note 5, page 20, adds that the directors are remunerated by Terumo Europe N.V. and that during the year no recharge was made to this company for their services. Note 16, page 24, records that the company has taken the FRS 102 exemption from disclosing transactions with its parent and fellow subsidiaries, and from disclosing key management compensation, so the size and terms of the intra-group trading that produces the targeted margin are not in the public record.

The principal activity, in the company's own words on page 5, is "the sale and distribution of medical products, predominantly in the UK but also have a branch in Ireland". The Irish branch is confirmed independently by note 6, page 21, where the double tax relief of £27,989 (2024: £24,898) is stated to relate to "the Terumo UK's Ireland Branch".

Two other Terumo companies file in the United Kingdom and neither is this one. TERUMO AORTIC LIMITED, SC593256, incorporated 4 April 2018, registered office Vascutek Ltd, Newmains Avenue, Inchinnan, Renfrew PA4 9RR, is the Scottish vascular graft business. TERUMO BCT LTD, NI049717, incorporated 18 February 2004, registered office Old Belfast Road, Millbrook, Larne, County Antrim BT40 2SH, is the blood and cell technologies business. Both were confirmed Active on the register on 30/08/2026. This Hub's supplier record covers 04571001 only, so a turnover or headcount figure quoted here should not be attached to Terumo's aortic or transfusion business.

Both current directors were appointed within sixteen days of each other in April 2023, and the FY2025 directors' report on page 3 names the same two as the directors who held office during the year. The register shows no UK commercial leadership at all, and the accounts explain why: note 5, page 20, says the directors are remunerated by Terumo Europe N.V. with no recharge to this company because "the time spent was minimal", and then states plainly that "There are no key management personnel noted in Terumo UK Ltd". marketPosition: The checkable footprint is four NHS Supply Chain framework subjects, and the spread tells you what kind of supplier this is. Syringes, Needles and Associated Products (2026/S 000-002484, 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2029). Intravenous Cannula and Associated Products, on the outgoing framework (2022/S 000-005941, 27 March 2023 to 31 March 2027) and on its replacement. Endoscopy, Endourology and Oncology Ablation Consumables and Associated Products (2024/S 000-029975, 1 October 2025 to 30 September 2027, 58 suppliers). And Perfusion Devices, Consumables and Associated Equipment (2024/S 000-033613, 10 November 2025 to 9 November 2027, 9 suppliers). Nothing in this Hub measures market share and no share figure exists anywhere in this system, but the perfusion framework is worth noticing on its own terms: nine named suppliers is a narrow field, against 58 on endoscopy and endourology.

It keeps its place on intravenous cannula. The Find a Tender contract award notice for the 2027 Intravenous Cannula and Associated Products framework, 2026/S 000-078334, published 18 August 2026 and read at source on 30 August 2026, names 21 suppliers, and "Terumo UK Ltd" is one of them. The award decision date is 6 July 2026 and the earliest date the contract will be signed is 17 September 2026, so this is awarded and not yet signed. Contract value on the notice is £140,000,000 excluding VAT (£168,000,000 including VAT) for a single lot. This matters against the wider picture the Hub already holds for that framework, which is that several incumbents are not on the new award notice.

One practical warning about paperwork. The two award notices give different addresses for the same organisation. On the syringes and needles notice the supplier is "Terumo UK Limited", with "Companies House: 04571001" printed on the notice itself, at the current registered office in Camberley, region UKJ37 North Hampshire. On the intravenous cannula notice the supplier is "Terumo UK Ltd" at Otium House, 2 Freemantle Road, Bagshot GU19 5LL, region UKJ25 West Surrey. Both carry the same Public Procurement Organisation Number, PQRR-7332-BCJQ, and the same tender contact address, tender.uk@terumo-europe.com, so they are the same organisation. Bagshot is an address this company has used before: it is the correspondence address recorded at Companies House for three directors who served between 2006 and 2020. Expect both addresses to be in circulation on live NHS paperwork.

The syringes and needles notice is also the cleanest identity proof this Hub has for the company, and it is worth saying so: the notice publishes the company number 04571001 against the supplier name itself, which is an award notice and the register agreeing without anyone having to match on the name.

On product range, read the captured list with care. This Hub's crawler read 159 product names from the XML sitemap of www.terumo-europe.com on 07/08/2026, grouped into four divisions by the company's own URL structure. That is Terumo's pan-EMEA site, not a UK catalogue, so it describes what the group publishes across Europe rather than what Terumo UK Limited sells into the NHS, and the names come from URL slugs rather than from a product record. The twelve products curated on this supplier's record are the UK-relevant set: Surflo intravenous catheters, Surshield Surflo safety sets, SurGuard3 safety needles, SurFlash, the Radifocus Introducer II, Glidewire, Glidewire Advantage, Glidecath and Glidesheath Slender, Angio-Seal VIP and Evolution and FemoSeal for vascular closure, and the TR Band for radial compression. A separate crawl of www.terumo.com for Terumo Aortic was refused on 20/08/2026, so no product range is recorded against that entity and its absence here is a read outcome, not a statement about that company.

deepDive.interview: Go in knowing that the profit number is set, not earned. The accounts say the company is a Limited Risk Distributor working to a targeted profit before tax of 3.5% to 4% under a transfer pricing agreement with Terumo Europe N.V., and it delivered 4.8%. So a margin conversation held with the UK company is a conversation with someone who does not own the margin, and pressing on price is a question for Leuven. What the UK company does own is volume, and volume is the honest measure here: £48.1m of turnover with £43.2m of it sold in the United Kingdom, up 46% on the pandemic year, with the strategic report naming price adjustments across the entire portfolio and new product launches as the drivers. If a price rise comes up, that first driver is their own published wording and you can quote it. On people, plan for a small, flat organisation: an average of 54 staff, all filed under Sales and administration, only two registered directors, one of them the only UK resident, and the accounts stating there are no key management personnel in the UK entity at all. Find out early who can actually sign off a price and whether that person is in this country. On frameworks, the useful line is that they hold their place on intravenous cannula into the 2027 term, awarded 6 July 2026 and not signed before 17 September 2026, so anything said about the new framework before that date is about an award and not a contract. And check which address is on the paperwork in front of you: Camberley is the registered office, but Bagshot is printed against the same organisation on the cannula award notice. Finally, if the conversation turns to supply resilience, note that this is a distribution company. All research and development is at group level, there is no UK manufacturing in these accounts, and treasury sits with the parent, so questions about lead times and continuity are questions about a European supply chain rather than a British factory.

deepDive.tagline: Basildon anaesthesia, general medical and surgical instrument maker, family-owned and trading since 1964 on its own account, named on 8 NHS Supply Chain frameworks · turnover fell from £12.8m to £9.0m as PPE income vanished, and £15m left the company as dividends in the same year
deepDive.lede: The thing worth knowing before this interview: Timesco had one extraordinary pandemic year, on PPE revenue, and distributed a large share of the proceeds as dividends the same year. Its own audited accounts for the year to 28 February 2023 record turnover of £8,965,149 against £12,787,629 the year before, and the directors say why in their own strategic report: "2022 was a bumper year mainly due to PPE related revenue." The class-of-business note makes that literal. PPE turnover was £3,929,193 in FY2022 and £2,366 in FY2023. In the same year the company paid an interim dividend of £75,000 per share, £15,000,000 in total, and net assets fell from £23,299,686 to £8,828,814. Since then it has taken audit exemption and filed abridged accounts, which by law deliver no income statement, so no turnover figure after February 2023 exists on the public record and none is invented here. What the balance sheets do show is a steady contraction: retained earnings £8,828,812, then £7,094,675, then £6,480,524; average headcount 45, then 41, then 38; cash £5.73m, then £4.61m, then £4.52m. Set that against eight NHS Supply Chain frameworks, two of which started in 2026, and the question in the room writes itself: this is a business whose NHS category access has kept growing since that PPE year, while the last published income statement predates it — worth asking about directly, since FY2024 and FY2025 were filed abridged with no income statement.

prose: Two turnover figures are on the public record and no more. Timesco Healthcare Limited turned over £12,787,629 in the year to 28 February 2022 and £8,965,149 in the year to 28 February 2023, both read from the tagged accounts. The company's own strategic report describes FY2022 as "a bumper year mainly due to PPE related revenue" and reports gross margin easing from 44.12% to 39.42%, EBITDA of £778,662 against £2,484,769, debtor days lengthening from 48 to 60 and creditor days shortening from 38 to 35. Profit before tax was £552,608 against £2,394,982; profit after tax £529,128 against £2,053,039.

The class-of-business note is where the shape of the fall shows. On the company's own segment names, FY2023 against FY2022: PPE £2,366 against £3,929,193; GenMed £4,240,620 against £5,741,163; Anaesthetic £2,860,737 against £2,291,258; Services £891,328 against nil; Electro £583,515 against £458,703; Surgical £161,212 against £245,035; Chiropractic £152,140 against £122,277; Despatch £73,231 against nil. So the whole of the decline is PPE and GenMed, while anaesthesia, the range the company is best known for, grew by £569,479 that year — the only published year it can be measured against. By geography, United Kingdom sales were £7,600,997 of the FY2023 total and £11,431,811 of FY2022, with the rest of the world almost flat at £1,364,152 against £1,355,818.

After that the record goes quiet, and the reason is a filing choice rather than a gap in this pipeline. The FY2023 accounts were audited by Raffingers LLP. For FY2024 and FY2025 the company took audit exemption under section 477 of the Companies Act 2006 and filed abridged accounts under section 444(2A), which deliver a balance sheet and notes but no profit and loss account. What can be read from those balance sheets is that retained earnings fell from £8,828,812 at 28 February 2023 to £7,094,675 and then to £6,480,524; stocks fell to £1,670,787; debtors to £1,168,061; cash held broadly flat at £4,519,536. That movement in retained earnings is NOT reported here as a loss. Retained earnings move by profit or loss less distributions, the abridged filings disclose neither, and attributing the change to trading would be a guess dressed as a figure.

ownership: TIMESCO HEALTHCARE LIMITED, company number 03346938, was incorporated on 8 April 1997 and is active. It has carried three names: Timesco of London Limited and Timesco of London (2005) Limited before becoming TIMESCO HEALTHCARE LIMITED on 31 August 2012. Its registered SIC codes are 26600, manufacture of irradiation, electromedical and electrotherapeutic equipment, and 47749, retail sale of medical and orthopaedic goods in specialised stores. The registered office moved on 18 April 2023 from 19-20 Bourne Court, Southend Road, Woodford Green, Essex IG8 8HD to Timesco House, 3 Carnival Park, Carnival Close, Basildon, Essex SS14 3WN. The Woodford Green address is the office of its accountants, Raffingers.

There is no parent company on the register. The only active person with significant control is Mrs Nabila Naseem Fayyaz, notified on 2 February 2022, holding more than 25% but not more than 50% of the shares and of the voting rights. Three earlier PSC entries have ceased: Mr Sohail Fayyaz and Mrs Andeleeb Fayyaz, both notified 6 April 2016 and 11 April 2019 respectively and both ceased in April 2019, and Mr Shahjehan Fayyaz, notified 6 April 2016 and ceased 5 November 2021. Read that register carefully before repeating it: no one is recorded as holding a majority of this company, and the single active entry is a 25 to 50% holding. This is a British family business with decisions taken in Basildon, not a subsidiary of an overseas manufacturer.

Three charges are registered and all three are outstanding: a debenture in favour of HSBC Bank PLC created 6 February 2003, a fixed charge on purchased debts which fail to vest in favour of HSBC Invoice Finance (UK) Ltd created 23 January 2006, and a general pledge in favour of HSBC Bank PLC created 6 October 2015. The related party notes name a second structure a rep should know about: the company pays rent to Timesco Property Partnership, a partnership in which Mr Sohail Fayyaz and Mrs Nabila Fayyaz are members, £285,000 in FY2023, £299,400 in FY2024 and £306,600 in FY2025. Remuneration paid to close family members of the directors and key management personnel was £337,638 in FY2023, £224,157 in FY2024 and £163,689 in FY2025. A separate company, TIMESCO OF LONDON LIMITED, number 08182773, registered at the same Basildon address, was dissolved on 14 October 2025.

hiring: Timesco's own careers page carried no live vacancies on 19/08/2026: the Current Vacancies section reads only "Thank you for your interest in Timesco." The page is worth reading anyway, because it says something specific about how the company staffs itself: "we're proud to say that 8 out of the 9 managers within our Senior Team have been recruited from within", and "We do not recruit people to do a job, we actively recruit people to have a career with us; and our average length of service demonstrates that we do this very well." Taken with an average headcount that has fallen from 45 to 38 in three years, that is a small, long-tenured company that promotes internally, so an external commercial hire here is likely to be a specific gap rather than a growth requisition. There is no applicant tracking system on the site and no salary information; roles are advertised through recruiters this check did not cover.
marketPosition: The verifiable measure of this company's NHS position is its framework footprint: named supplier on 8 separate NHS Supply Chain frameworks, each confirmed against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch brief. They are Airway Management Products and Associated Equipment (2023/S 000-005729, 22 July 2024 to 21 July 2028), Central Venous Catheters and Associated Products (2025/S 000-001530, 23 March 2026 to 22 March 2028), Electrosurgical Consumables and Related Accessories (2024/S 000-001161, 20 October 2025 to 19 October 2028), Maternity, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Sexual Health Products (2019/S 214-525123, 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2027), Pulse Oximetry, Capnography and Related Monitoring Technologies (2023/S 000-011885, 4 March 2024 to 4 March 2028), Respiratory Solutions (1 August 2022 to 15 June 2027), Surgical Instruments (2020/S 170-412524, 6 August 2021 to 12 July 2027) and Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions (2025/S 000-032216, 4 August 2026 to 3 August 2028). The Airway Management, Surgical Instruments and Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions briefs were re-read on 19/08/2026 and name the company as "Timesco Healthcare Ltd" on each. Nothing expires within the next ten months; the earliest end date is Respiratory Solutions on 15 June 2027.

What it actually sells is best read from its own filings rather than its website, because the two are shaped differently. The class-of-business note in the FY2023 accounts puts GenMed at £4,240,620 and Anaesthetic at £2,860,737, which is 79% of turnover between them, with Electro £583,515, Surgical £161,212 and Chiropractic £152,140 much smaller. That last point is the one worth carrying into a conversation: Timesco is named on NHS Supply Chain's Surgical Instruments framework, and by its own segmentation surgical instruments were under 2% of the year's revenue. The framework award is category access, not a revenue line. The Hub's own crawl of timesco.com on 15/08/2026 read 224 products from the company's own catalogue, filed as General Medical 106, Anaesthesia 60 and Surgery 56, the largest single category being Airway Management with 54. Named ranges include the Callisto and Sirus XL laryngoscopes, Optima View video laryngoscopy, the Vide chest drainage system, the NeuroLight pupillometer, Wira-Flexi fixation, the Coral sphygmomanometer and Evac-S single use suction.

Two things sit outside that crawl and should not be mistaken for absences. Podiatry is a real Timesco division with its own site at timesco-podiatry.co.uk, selling foot dressers, nail probes, nail files and nail cutters plus a Social Nail Care single patient use range; it is not in the 224 products above because the Hub has only crawled timesco.com, and the accounts show that business, as Chiropractic, at £152,140 in FY2023. And the company's policies page states LSAS Level 3, the Labour Standards Assurance System, "for instrument and laryngoscope portfolios", alongside REACH and WEEE compliance, an ISO certificate referenced GBMD_010037, a Carbon Reduction Plan under PPN 06/21 updated August 2025 and steps toward ISO 14001. That matters commercially because labour standards assurance is exactly what NHS Supply Chain scrutinises in instrument categories: its Surgical Instruments brief states that "Sustainable procurement is embedded into our category management processes to ensure that our suppliers meet requirements for carbon reduction plans, evergreen assessment, modern slavery, social value and NHS England net zero supplier roadmap." The brief does not itself specify a required LSAS level, so the Level 3 claim is published here as the company's own statement about itself, read on its own site on 19/08/2026, and not as an NHS Supply Chain finding.

No market share is given here and none is calculable. The company's own scale claims are its own and are published as such: "3,000+ product lines available", "200+ distributors worldwide" and "8.5m+ medical devices supplied each year", all from timesco.com/about-us, read 19/08/2026. No Timesco product could be confirmed in this Hub's NHS Supply Chain catalogue cache by NPC, so no catalogue code is quoted; that is a gap in the cache rather than evidence the company has no catalogue lines.

deepDive.interview: Read the FY2023 accounts before you go in, because everything interesting is in them and almost nobody applying will have. Three questions come out of the filings and none of them is hostile. First, the PPE cliff: the directors wrote that 2022 was "a bumper year mainly due to PPE related revenue" and the segment note shows PPE going from £3.93m to £2,366 in twelve months, while anaesthesia grew. Asking what the company kept from that year, in customers or in listings, rather than what it lost, is a commercial question that shows you read the report. Second, the reporting gap: FY2024 and FY2025 were filed abridged with no income statement, so a candidate cannot know the current revenue, and asking straightforwardly where turnover sits now is fair and expected. Third, category access against category revenue: they are on the Surgical Instruments framework and surgical was £161,212 in the last published year, so ask which of the eight frameworks the team is actually being measured on. Two pieces of context to carry: the newest framework, Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions, started on 4 August 2026 and consolidates three older ones, which means live trust-level implementation work right now; and this is a family business with one active PSC holding 25 to 50%, no parent company and a landlord that is a partnership of two of its own directors, so the people you meet are the people who decide. Finally, know the two dates. The business says it has traded since 1964. The company you would be employed by was incorporated in 1997 and has been called Timesco Healthcare Limited since 2012.

deepDive.tagline: Family-run Stafford wholesaler of pharmacy packaging, disposables and dispensers, founded from a 1970s pharmacy sundries business, still fully owned and directed by the Pittock family.

links.label: NHS Supply Chain contract launch brief (Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions)

deepDive.lede: Valley Northern is on the incumbent-plus list for NHS Supply Chain's new Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions framework, which starts 4 August 2026 and merges the old Patient Assessment Devices, Blood Pressure Cuffs and Thermometer Device frameworks into one 40-supplier deal. It is a genuinely family business, not a marketing line: all five current directors and all four people with significant control on the Companies House register share the surname Pittock, and the company's own history page traces the name back to a Valley Road pharmacy sundries business their grandfather David Pittock started in 1972.

prose: No turnover figure can be read for this company. Its Companies House filing history shows only total exemption full accounts each year (most recently to 31 December 2024, filed 25 June 2025), which is the small company exemption that lets a business file a balance sheet without a profit and loss account or a turnover figure. There is no group or subsidiary structure disclosed that would let a parent level number stand in for it, and Valley Northern's own website does not publish a turnover or key figures page.

The company does publish some scale indicators on its own homepage as live counters rather than audited figures: 810,957,000 bags supplied, six countries supplied, 1,414 product lines available online and 26 years industry experience, counting from the 2000 founding of Valley Northern specifically, not the earlier family pharmacy business. These are self-reported marketing statistics, not filed financial data, and are labelled as such here rather than treated as a growth series.

ownership: Valley Northern Limited, company number 09188858, is a private limited company incorporated on 28 August 2014, with its registered office at Valley Northern, Carver Road, Astonfields, Stafford ST16 3BP. Its SIC code is 46460, wholesale of pharmaceutical goods. Status is active. Companies House, read 18/08/2026.

It is not part of any disclosed group structure and there is no parent company or PE or institutional shareholder on the register. The four active persons with significant control, notified 14 September 2020, are Adrian Pittock, Oliver John Pittock, Darren Pittock and Dale Pittock, each recorded with the generic nature of control has significant influence or control rather than a specific shareholding band. An earlier PSC statement, notified 19 August 2016 and ceased 16 December 2016, had recorded Adrian Pittock alone holding more than 25% but not more than 50% of shares and voting rights; that entry was superseded by the current four person notification in 2020, so the precise current shareholding split between the four is not stated on the public register and is marked Not verified here.

The company's own history page describes it as continuously family owned since its 1972 origins as a pharmacy sundries business, Valley Road, hence the name, through a 2000 split off into Valley Northern proper under Oliver Pittock, and incorporation as a limited company in 2014.

press.text: Valley Northern is named as one of 40 suppliers on NHS Supply Chain's new Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions framework, combining the former Patient Assessment Devices, Blood Pressure Cuffs and Thermometer Device frameworks, which starts on this date and runs to 3 August 2028.

Launched a Controlled Drug Destruction Kit specifically designed for liquid medication, described on its own site as an industry first, alongside a Kinder to our planet range of eco-friendly packaging alternatives.
Supplied PPE dispensers to NHS Nightingale during the COVID-19 pandemic, alongside its ongoing supply to pharmacies, chemists and hospitals.

hiring: Valley Northern runs a single generic careers page, with no individually listed live vacancies, inviting applications by department: Sales, Customer Service, Accounts, Marketing, Purchasing, IT, Assistants and Warehouse. It markets itself to candidates as a family business with a friendly working environment, career growth opportunities and employee benefits. No specific current open roles or headcount target could be verified from this page; treat as Not verified beyond the general hiring channel existing.
marketPosition: Valley Northern positions itself as a specialist pharmacy and healthcare packaging, disposables and dispensers wholesaler serving hospital pharmacies, GPs, community pharmacies, wholesalers, dentists, vets, ambulance trusts and care homes across the UK, with next working day delivery as a core differentiator since 2002. Its own customer logo carousel names the NHS, BUPA, HCA Healthcare, Spire Healthcare, Nuffield, Numark, the MOD and the RAF among users of its products, though these are supplier published customer references rather than independently confirmed contracts.

Its verified NHS Supply Chain presence, Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions, starting 4 August 2026, sits alongside larger, better known medical device names on the same 40 supplier framework, such as Philips, GE Medical Systems, Welch Allyn and Draeger; Valley Northern's own product range is weighted toward packaging, dispensers and disposables rather than the diagnostic devices most of that framework covers, so its specific lot or lots on it were not independently confirmed in this session and are Not verified.
It holds ISO 9001 and ISO 14001 accreditation and a Cyber Essentials certificate, evidenced by PDFs linked from its own site footer.
deepDive.interview: Worth knowing before a conversation with this company: it is a genuinely small, closely held family operation, not a group subsidiary, so questions about ownership structure or a head office in another country will not land; decision making authority likely sits with the five Pittock directors rather than a wider corporate hierarchy. Its news is product and framework led rather than financial, so ask about its position on the new Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions framework, live from 4 August 2026, and which of the five lots it actually supplies into, since that could not be confirmed independently here. Also worth probing gently: which Pittock currently holds the top operational role, since the website's own team page anonymises this behind department graphics.

Could not be verified and deliberately omitted or flagged: any turnover or profit figure, the company files small company total exemption accounts with no P&L disclosed; current employee headcount, a third party search summary suggested 44 employees as of 31 December 2024, but this could not be confirmed by directly reading a Companies House or company published page in this session, so it has been left out rather than guessed; named individual job titles beyond director, the company's own team page groups staff by department graphic, not by name; the precise current percentage shareholding split between the four Pittock family PSCs, the register records significant influence or control without a percentage band for the current 2020 notification; and the company's LinkedIn company page, which could not be loaded in this session and is therefore not included as a linkedinPeople link.

background.text: CORRECTION: the previous listing ('Bile bags, Ryles tubes, Levin tubes') could NOT be substantiated -- zero mentions anywhere on Valley Northern's own site (150+ blog posts, sitemap, product pages checked), and none of those items appear under their name on the NHS Supply Chain catalogue. deepDive.lede: Vernacare made two significant moves within weeks of each other in early 2026: on 2 March 2026 it sold its Harm Reduction business, eXchange, to Orion Medical Supplies while striking an exclusive deal for Orion to source all its sharps containers from Vernacare, then on 7 April 2026 it acquired Eakin Surgical Limited from Eakin Healthcare Group, continuing a buy-and-build run that also took in Frontier Medical's Infection Prevention business in 2020, Robinson Healthcare in 2021 and Splice Cast Limited in 2023. Worth knowing before a meeting: the company is reshaping its portfolio in real time, trimming harm reduction while building out surgical solutions.
