press.text: Vernacare announced the appointment of Alex Hodges as Chief Executive Officer, bringing prior experience from Owens and Minor, Halyard Health and Kimberly-Clark.

Orion Medical Supplies acquired Vernacare's Harm Reduction business, known as eXchange, with Vernacare and Orion entering an exclusive partnership under which Orion will source all its sharps containers from Vernacare.

H.I.G. Capital-backed Vernacare completed the acquisition of Eakin Surgical Limited from Eakin Healthcare Group, a manufacturer of single-use surgical instruments including suction products and sterile procedure solutions; press coverage frames this as continuing a buy-and-build strategy that previously took in Frontier Medical's Infection Prevention business in 2020, Robinson Healthcare in 2021 and Splice Cast Limited in 2023.

hiring: Vernacare's own careers page describes the company as making a difference in healthcare, with vacancies also mirrored on third-party job boards, Reed, Glassdoor, CV-Library, Indeed, at the time of this check. Specific current vacancy titles, numbers or locations were not read in detail in this session and are not reported here; a rep wanting live openings should check the careers page directly.
marketPosition: Vernacare positions itself around three segments: Infection Prevention, Clinical Waste Management and Surgical Solutions, per its own website navigation and about page. It describes itself as a pioneer of single-use infectious waste disposal systems, manufacturing from two sites in the North West of England plus a Toronto, Canada base, serving more than 65 countries. It is a confirmed NHS Supply Chain framework supplier; the specific frameworks and lots are already captured elsewhere in this supplier's frameworks array and were not re-verified here, per the standing instruction not to duplicate that work.

The March 2026 divestment of its Harm Reduction, eXchange, business to Orion Medical Supplies, alongside the April 2026 acquisition of Eakin Surgical, suggests active portfolio reshaping under H.I.G. Capital ownership: narrowing out of harm reduction, needle and syringe provision, while building depth in surgical instruments and infection prevention. This is a live strategic direction, not a stable long-run position, and should be treated as current state rather than settled.
deepDive.interview: Given the pace of change, a rep meeting Vernacare should ask directly what the Eakin Surgical acquisition of 7 April 2026 means for their surgical solutions range and sales structure, and confirm whether the harm reduction exit to Orion on 2 March 2026 has any bearing on categories relevant to your own conversation, since that product line has left the business. It is also worth probing who currently owns commercial and NHS account relationships following two changes in a matter of weeks, as the four Companies House directors, Hall, Hodges, Morris, Wadhams, may not map neatly onto day-to-day commercial contacts you would actually deal with.

frameworks.note: Contract award notice UK6, Procurement Act 2023, published 18/08/2026, tender status 'complete', single lot, one award listing 21 suppliers. GBUK Ltd is named among the 21. 24 tenders were received, 22 assessed at final stage, 1 (Sai Medical Solutions Ltd) named unsuccessful. Award decision 06/07/2026 (a preliminary notice had estimated 27/07/2026 — this is the confirmed date from the award notice itself); earliest contract signature 17/09/2026, so this is AWARDED, not yet signed. Both incumbent Becton Dickinson entries do not appear among the 21 named suppliers on this notice, nor do Applied Medical Technology, ICU UK Medical, Iskus Health UK, Praxis Medical, Reliance Medical, Rocialle Healthcare, TLB Medical Supplies or William Davies Care, all of whom held a place on the outgoing 2023-2027 framework. AMENDED 26/08/2026, re-read at source: that list needs one qualification, because the outgoing framework named the ICU Medical group TWICE, as 'ICU UK Medical Ltd' and as 'Smiths Medical International Ltd', and only the first of the two is absent from the new award. 'Smiths Medical International Ltd' IS among the 21, at 1500 Eureka Park, Ashford TN25 4BF with the contact address MWATUKContracts@icumed.com, and that is Companies House 00362847, registered under that name from 01/03/2004 until it was renamed ICU MEDICAL INTERNATIONAL LIMITED on 02/10/2024 — the only company that has ever held the name. So the ICU Medical group keeps a place on this framework and loses a second one; note 31 of that company's accounts for the year ended 31 December 2024 records the two UK trading entities being consolidated with effect from 1 February 2026, with ICU UK Medical Limited transferring its trade and assets to 00362847. Two dated facts side by side; the notice gives no reason and none is asserted here. Stated as what the notice itself shows, not as a claim that the list is final: NHS Supply Chain's own commercial launch brief for this framework had not been published as of 18/08/2026 (the live brief page still showed the 2023-2027 framework), so this record should be checked against that brief once it appears, and 'not on the award notice' is not the same statement as 'will not supply under this framework.'

deepDive.tagline: French, family-owned since 1962 and still independent: no private equity, no listing · UK subsidiary at Swindon since 1973, under a new general manager since 1 January 2026
deepDive.lede: The thing worth knowing before this interview: Vygon UK changed hands at the top on 1 January 2026, and the new general manager is the man who was its finance director. Dale Keegan joined in August 2016 and was chief financial officer until the end of 2025; the group's own announcement says he takes over from Les Davies, who had run the subsidiary for twenty years and moves to developing Vygon's principal markets. Companies House shows the same switch as register events six weeks later: Keegan appointed a director on 1 February 2026, Davies resigned the same day. Underneath that, the UK trading position is unusually legible. Vygon is a named supplier on 15 NHS Supply Chain frameworks confirmed against the briefs, four of which started during 2026, and one of which, Infusion Pumps and Administration Sets, expires on 30 September 2026, six weeks from this record being written. A new commercial leader with a retender landing in his first year is the shape of the conversation you are walking into.

prose: No UK turnover figure can be read for this company. Vygon (U.K.) Limited (Companies House 01131530) files full accounts, most recently for the year ended 31 December 2025, filed on 10 June 2026, but they are filed as a 29-page PDF with no tagged figures, so there is nothing to read. Third-party company-data sites do publish a UK turnover for Vygon, derived by picking a line off that PDF. This record does not use it: identifying the turnover line by position is a guess about which number is turnover, and a wrong turnover against a named company is exactly the error this Hub refuses to make. The figures below are the group's, as the group itself publishes them, and they are not a proxy for UK trading.

Vygon's own key-figures page gives group turnover of €423 million for 2025. Its press releases through the first half of 2026 give €417.9 million for 2024, with 81% of that earned outside France. That is growth of roughly 1.2% year on year in euros, which for a private, family-held manufacturer with 11 factories is a holding pattern rather than a story, and it is worth reading alongside where the company is actually spending: the February 2026 Stiletto acquisition was explicitly aimed at the United States, not Europe.

Vygon SA is private and French, so there is no annual report, no investor call and no tagged filing to read. Everything above comes from the company's own published statements, which is a weaker source class than a filing and is labelled as such. Earlier years are not plotted because no Vygon-published figure for them was read in this session.

ownership: Vygon is a family company, founded in 1962 by Pierre Simonet. The group's own history page tells the story: he was a hospital patient, saw what sterilisation was costing staff, and went away to make single-use kit instead. It is still headquartered at 8 rue de Paris, Ecouen, north of Paris. It describes itself in every 2026 press release as "a family company" and "a mid-sized business", and nothing found in this session contradicts that: there is no listing, no private-equity holder and no announced sale process. That independence is the company's own stated position, and "independence, optimism and humanism" is the group's headline about itself. For a rep it is the practical difference between a business that answers to a family board and one that answers to quarterly guidance.

The UK entity is Vygon (U.K.) Limited, company number 01131530, incorporated 28 August 1973 and confirmed active at Companies House on 18/08/2026, registered at The Pierre Simonet Building, V Park, Gateway North, Latham Road, Swindon, Wiltshire SN25 4DL. Its registered activity is SIC 46460, wholesale of pharmaceutical goods: a sales and distribution entity, not a manufacturing one; the group's 11 factories are in Europe, the US and Colombia. The building is named after the founder.

The UK company's sole person with significant control is Vygon SAS of Ecouen, notified on 1 June 2016, holding 75% or more of the shares, registered at the Pontoise register of trade and companies under B325241750. That is the whole ownership chain: French parent, UK subsidiary, no intermediate holding company and no third-party investor on the register.

deepDive.peopleNote: The Companies House entries above are statutory register facts. Where this record says one person took over from another it is quoting Vygon's own announcement of 7 January 2026, not inferring succession from the register. Beyond the general manager, the UK commercial leadership could not be verified: Vygon UK's own page titled "Meet the Senior Leadership Team" (read 18/08/2026) describes the business units and names no individuals at all. Treat sales-director and business-unit-head names as Not verified, and confirm them nearer the interview.

press.text: Vygon announces Dale Keegan as general manager of its UK subsidiary, effective 1 January 2026. Keegan, with the company since August 2016 and CFO until the end of 2025, takes over from Les Davies, who moves to developing Vygon's principal markets. The release sets his brief as "driving growth across the NHS and the private sector".
NHS Supply Chain's Needlefree Connection Systems and Associated Products framework starts, running to 25 January 2028, with Vygon among 16 named suppliers.

Vygon acquires Stiletto® and its patented SlipStream™ insertion system from Avia Vascular of Salt Lake City, its first entry into the extended-dwell catheter segment. Financial details were not disclosed. The stated aim is US growth: the group calls North America "the world's largest and most dynamic market for midline and extended-dwell catheters".

NHS Supply Chain's Central Venous Catheters and Associated Products framework starts, running to 22 March 2028, with Vygon among 18 named suppliers, one of the narrowest supplier fields Vygon sits on.
NHS Supply Chain's Single Use Theatre Protective Wear and Related Consumables framework starts, running to 25 May 2029, with Vygon among 29 named suppliers.

Vygon Corporation receives Health Canada approval to commercialise Stiletto™, and appoints NIPRO Canada as national distributor. Four months after the acquisition, the extended-dwell line is still being rolled out in North America rather than Europe.
NHS Supply Chain's Syringes, Needles and Associated Products framework starts, running to 30 June 2029, with Vygon among 53 named suppliers.

hiring: No open-vacancy count could be verified. Vygon UK's careers page at vygon.co.uk/value-life/careers/ carries a "View our current vacancies" panel that is loaded by script and returned nothing readable in this session, and group roles are advertised through a separate careers portal. So this is Not verified rather than zero. What the careers page does say, and it is worth reading before an interview: "many of our senior team members started their Vygon journey from entry-level roles, and in many cases have been with the company for more than 20 years". The new general manager, a decade in and promoted from CFO, is that claim in practice.
marketPosition: Vygon calls itself "a world leader in the neonatology and vascular management clinical specialties" in its own press releases. That is the company's own description and no independently verified market share exists for it in any source read here, so none is stated. The one thing the group does quantify about itself is volume: 210 million medical devices produced a year, sold in more than 120 countries through 26 subsidiaries and 400 distributors, with 183 patents filed.

The verifiable measure of UK position is the NHS Supply Chain footprint: named supplier on 15 frameworks, confirmed against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs, and the pattern in them is tight rather than broad. Vygon appears in intravenous cannula, central venous catheters, extension sets and lines, IV accessories and pressure monitoring, needle-free connection systems, infusion pumps and administration sets, syringes and needles, blood collection devices, enteral feeding and bile bags, airway management, procedure packs, single-use theatre protective wear, pulse oximetry and capnography, patient monitoring, and maternity/obstetrics. That is one clinical story, the line into the patient and what runs through it, sold across fifteen buying routes, not a general-consumables catalogue.

Two of those fields are narrow enough to matter in an interview. Central Venous Catheters names 18 suppliers and Needle-free Connection Systems names 16, against 53 on syringes and needles and 57 on maternity. Where the field is small, framework presence is closer to a competitive position; where it is large, it is closer to a licence to quote.

The UK business also runs Vygon Vet, a veterinary consumables division of Vygon (UK) Ltd with over 20 years' trading, at vygonvet.co.uk. It is a genuine second channel out of the same Swindon operation and is easy to miss.
deepDive.interview: Three things are fair game and all three are sourced. First, the framework that runs out: Infusion Pumps and Administration Sets and Associated Products expires on 30 September 2026, six weeks after this record was written, and asking how the team is preparing for the retender shows you have read the award record rather than the website. Second, the leadership change: a general manager who came from the CFO's chair on 1 January 2026, after twenty years of the same predecessor, will have a view on what he wants done differently, so ask it directly rather than dancing round it. Third, the geography of the growth: the Stiletto acquisition and its Health Canada approval both point at North America, so a question about what the UK gets from the group's investment plan is a serious one. And know how this company sells: clinical nurse advisors, in-service training, competency sign-off and the Campus Vygon education platform are the delivery model, so a candidate who talks only about price per unit is answering the wrong question.

deepDive.tagline: One Belfast-registered company trades as both Cardiac Services and Synapse Medical: Companies House NI018037 (Uniphar Medtech UK Limited), whose turnover fell 17.0% to £25.4 million in the year to 31 December 2024 (filed 7 October 2025), down from £30.6 million the year before.

deepDive.lede: Cardiac Services and Synapse Medical are the same legal entity: Uniphar Medtech UK Limited, Companies House number NI018037, registered in Belfast since 1984. If you meet either brand name, or the older names Sisk Healthcare (UK) Limited or Cardiac Services Limited, you are dealing with one company. It distributes and services medical equipment rather than manufacturing it, is wholly owned two levels up by the Irish group Uniphar plc, and sits on 15 NHS Supply Chain framework listings across 12 distinct framework references. Turnover fell 17.0% in the year to 31 December 2024, to £25.4 million, having already peaked at £34.9 million in FY2022 — the fall in profit was sharper than the fall in revenue, because a fixed cost base didn't shrink with sales. The board itself says it does not track company-specific KPIs, because Uniphar plc manages performance divisionally across the group, so anything you hear about performance locally will be anecdotal rather than reported. Ask which brand a role or contract actually sits under before you assume the other one's range is out of scope.

prose: Turnover rose through the pandemic years to a peak of £34.9 million in FY2022, held roughly flat in FY2021 (£32.4 million) after a strong FY2020 (£34.6 million, itself up from £28.1 million in FY2019), then fell for two consecutive years: to £30.6 million in FY2023 and £25.4 million in FY2024 — a 27% fall from the FY2022 peak, with more than half of that fall (17.0%) landing in FY2024 alone.

Gross margin has stayed in a narrow band throughout — 38.1% (FY2019), 35.1% (FY2020), 39.7% (FY2021), 40.9% (FY2022), 41.7% (FY2023) and 40.4% (FY2024) — so the FY2024 profit fall was not primarily a pricing or cost-of-goods problem. Operating margin tells a different story: 16.0%, 13.7%, 19.5%, 17.6% and 16.8% in FY2019-FY2023, then 9.3% in FY2024. The strategic report attributes this to a £0.3 million rise in administrative expenses landing on top of the lower gross profit — in plain terms, a largely fixed cost base did not shrink when revenue did.

The directors' own explanation, in the FY2024 strategic report, is that the company 'is satisfied with its underlying trading performance' despite the fall, and that the board does not track company-specific KPIs at all: 'the directors of Uniphar plc manage the group's operations on a divisional basis. For this reason, the company's directors believe that analysis using key performance indicators for the company is not necessary or appropriate.' That is a director-level statement about how the business is managed, not a comment on the trend itself — the trend is the filed numbers above.

Set against this, Uniphar plc's own 2024 results describe the whole pan-European Medtech division — of which this UK company is one part — as growing gross profit organically by 9.1% in the same year. The UK entity's turnover fall and the group division's growth are not contradictory (a multi-country division can grow while one national unit contracts), but a rep should not assume the UK business is riding the same trajectory as the group headline; ask what is driving the UK-specific fall.

ownership: Uniphar Medtech UK Limited, company number NI018037, is a private limited company incorporated in Northern Ireland on 14 December 1984, registered at 6 Wildflower Way, Boucher Road, Belfast BT12 6TA. Companies House's own previous-names record for this number shows three prior names held by the same legal person, in sequence: BUSINESS AND SCIENTIFIC SERVICES LIMITED (14 December 1984 to 5 January 1994), CARDIAC SERVICES LIMITED (5 January 1994 to 14 December 2010), and SISK HEALTHCARE (UK) LIMITED (14 December 2010 to 19 May 2023); the current name took effect on 19 May 2023 (filings CERTNM/NM01/RES15, filed that day, following a resolution dated 15 May 2023).

Identity was established on four independent grounds, not on the Hub's own stored (unverified) match. First, the register's previous-names history above. Second, the registered office printed on the face of the balance sheet — 6 Wildflower Way, Boucher Road, Belfast, BT12 6TA — matches the address held on the register. Third, the balance sheet itself is headed 'REGISTERED NUMBER: NI 018037'. Fourth, the directors named in the accounts, T Dolphin and S Taaffe, match the two currently active directors on the register — Timothy Dolphin (appointed 20 August 2018) and Siobhán Taaffe (appointed 20 May 2022) — with company secretary A McCarthy on the accounts matching Aisling McCarthy on the register (appointed 1 May 2019). Beyond the register itself, two of the three sets of accounts read in this session carry the former names on their own cover pages: the year-ended-31-December-2020 accounts are headed 'SISK HEALTHCARE (UK) LIMITED', and the year-ended-31-December-2022 accounts are headed 'UNIPHAR MEDTECH UK LIMITED (Formerly Sisk Healthcare (UK) Limited)' — both quoting registered number NI 018037 on their cover.

A second, unrelated company also called CARDIAC SERVICES LTD exists on the register (company number 13965840, incorporated 9 March 2022, registered at Chester House, Lloyd Drive, Ellesmere Port, Cheshire CH65 9HQ, SIC code 86210 'General medical practice activities'). This is a distinct legal person with no link on the register to NI018037 and is not covered by anything in this record.

The persons-with-significant-control register for NI018037 names one active PSC: Uniphar Medtech Holdings UK Limited (company number NI040976, also registered at 6 Wildflower Way, Boucher Road, Belfast), holding more than 75% of shares and more than 75% of voting rights, notified 6 April 2016. NI040976 carries its own previous-names history — CARDIAC SERVICES (HOLDINGS) LIMITED (12 June 2001 to 31 August 2011) and SISK HEALTHCARE HOLDINGS (UK) LIMITED (31 August 2011 to 19 May 2023) — mirroring the operating company's own name changes. NI040976's own PSC register in turn names Uniphar Plc (Irish Companies Registration Office number 224324, registered at 4045 Kingswood Road, Citywest Business Park, Dublin) as holding more than 75% of shares and voting rights, plus the right to appoint or remove directors, notified 20 August 2018 — succeeding a previous PSC named Scale Holdings (Irish company number 423532), which ceased to be PSC on the same date.

The accounts corroborate this chain directly: note 26 to the FY2024 accounts states that 'all related parties and related party transactions are disclosed in the consolidated financial statements of Uniphar plc', obtainable from the company secretary of Uniphar plc at the Kingswood Road, Dublin address; note 7 states that 'auditors' remuneration is borne by the ultimate parent company, Uniphar plc'. Uniphar plc is an Irish public company whose shares trade on Euronext Growth Dublin (ticker UPR).

This UK business was previously part of the Sisk Healthcare group, under Sicon Limited. Uniphar plc's proposed acquisition of Sisk Healthcare was notified to the Irish Competition and Consumer Protection Commission on 25 April 2018 (case M/18/031); binding commitments addressing information-sharing between Uniphar's own wholesale/logistics business and Sisk Healthcare's business units were accepted on 18 July 2018, and the CCPC issued its clearing determination on 17 August 2018. This lines up with the dated PSC change on the NI040976 register — Uniphar plc replacing Scale Holdings as PSC on 20 August 2018 — and with Timothy Dolphin's appointment to the NI018037 board on that same date, 20 August 2018.

The accounts are audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers, Chartered Accountants & Statutory Audit Firm, One Spencer Dock, North Wall Quay, Dublin 1 — an Irish audit firm, consistent with the Irish parent. The FY2024 financial statements were approved by the board and signed by T Dolphin, Director, on 29 September 2025, and filed at Companies House on 7 October 2025.

deepDive.peopleNote: Companies House records dated appointments and terminations only, never succession. Both current directors were appointed on dates that sit inside a wider reshuffle: Timothy Dolphin was appointed on 20 August 2018, the same day Uniphar plc was notified as the new PSC of the immediate parent NI040976 (see ownership); Siobhán Taaffe was appointed on 20 May 2022, the same day two other directors' appointments were terminated (Mark David Reid and Gerard Edward Rabbette, both terminated 20 May 2022, filed as separate TM01s). These are stated here as dated events only — this record does not assert that Taaffe replaced either departing director. No named commercial, sales or country-manager leadership below main-board director level could be verified: Companies House lists only the statutory directors and secretary above, and neither cardiac-services.com nor synapsemed.co.uk names any commercial leadership, only general enquiry numbers and clinical/technical service teams. LinkedIn was not consulted, per this system's sourcing rules.

press.text: Uniphar plc notified the Irish Competition and Consumer Protection Commission of its proposed acquisition of Sisk Healthcare from Sicon Limited (CCPC case M/18/031).

The CCPC issued its determination clearing Uniphar plc's acquisition of Sisk Healthcare, subject to binding commitments (accepted 18 July 2018) on information-sharing between Uniphar's own wholesale/logistics business and Sisk Healthcare's business units (CCPC case M/18/031). Companies House separately records Uniphar plc becoming PSC of the NI040976 holding company on 20 August 2018.

Uniphar plc's 2024 preliminary results reported Medtech divisional revenue of €267.968m (2023: €249.216m) and divisional gross profit of €108.915m (2023: €99.870m), described by the group as 9.1% organic gross-profit growth for the division.

deepDive.hiring: The company's own audited accounts (note 8) show an average of 61 employees across 2024 — 21 in management & administration and 40 in selling & distribution — down from 63 in 2023; no directors' remuneration was paid in either year. Both trading brands route recruitment through the parent's careers page, unipharmedtech.com/careers, which is JavaScript-rendered and returned no readable vacancy listing when checked on 05/09/2026, so current open-role counts cannot be given from that source today. Synapse Medical's own website separately states (checked 05/09/2026) that it operates with '14 employees' including '9 Clinical Sales Specialists' — this reads as a brand-level headcount rather than the whole-company figure, since Cardiac Services and Synapse Medical together make up the 61 employees reported in the audited accounts.
marketPosition: This is a distributor and service provider, not a manufacturer. The FY2024 strategic report describes 'the supply and distribution of medical devices to the healthcare sector', relying on 'strong manufacturer relationships and established supply chain infrastructure' rather than in-house manufacturing; the company confirms it undertakes no research and development.

One legal entity, two live trading brands, two separate websites. Cardiac Services (cardiac-services.com) is the larger, longer-established brand: it describes six service lines — digital health, clinical engineering (a '25+' strong team), managed equipment services, hospital-division supply of equipment, software and consumables, therapeutic and simulation products, and training — from offices in Belfast, Dublin and Manchester. Synapse Medical (synapsemed.co.uk) is the smaller, imaging-focused brand: a diagnostic-imaging specialist working with manufacturer partners GE, Ulrich, Febromed, Kubtec, Lemar Pax and Calmed, with offices in Dublin and the UK.

The Hub's supplier index records one domain per merged company record, and this one holds cardiac-services.com. That reflects how the index is built, not a smaller capability at Synapse Medical: an absent Synapse Medical product listing elsewhere in the Hub is not evidence of an absent range — check synapsemed.co.uk directly for imaging-specific enquiries.

The Hub holds 15 NHS Supply Chain framework listings for this company, counted as every framework-category entry captured under any of the company's trading or former names. Those 15 entries span 12 distinct framework references (counted by the distinct value of NHS Supply Chain's own 'reference' field): four of the fifteen listed categories — Bladder Scanners, Ultrasound Scanners, Contrast Injectors and Specimen Cabinets — share a single reference, 2021/S 000-007768, meaning they sit as separate categories or lots inside one framework agreement rather than four independent contracts. Eleven of the fifteen entries were captured under a Cardiac Services name (including the former SISK Healthcare (UK) Ltd trading style), and four under a Synapse Medical name, matching the split between the two brands' own stated specialisms — cardiac/pulmonary diagnostics, ECG and defibrillation consumables, patient monitoring, airway management, orthotics, obstetrics/gynaecology and chart paper/film for Cardiac Services; ultrasound, ophthalmology, contrast injectors and endoscopy/oncology-ablation consumables for Synapse Medical.

Three further NHS Supply Chain briefs name a bare 'Uniphar Medtech' or 'Uniphar Medtech Ltd' without a UK company suffix (Perfusion 2024/S 000-033613, Minimally Invasive Surgery 2026/S 000-061906, Total Patient Assessment 2025/S 000-032216). These have not been merged into this record — they may belong to the Irish parent trading directly, or to a different Uniphar Medtech entity — and are an honest gap rather than a claimed capability.

Financially, the board itself states that no company-specific KPIs are tracked, because Uniphar plc manages the group divisionally; anything about local UK performance beyond the filed accounts numbers above will not come from the company's own published reporting.

deepDive.interview: Turnover fell 17.0% in FY2024 to £25.4 million, after a run-up to £34.9 million in FY2022 — ask what's driving the two-year decline, and whether the accounts due at Companies House by 30 September 2026 (year to 30 December 2025) show it stabilising. Operating margin nearly halved, from 16.8% to 9.3%, while gross margin barely moved (41.7% to 40.4%) — the strategic report points to a £0.3 million rise in administrative expenses on top of lower gross profit; ask what's actually in that cost increase and whether it's one-off or structural. The company trades as two separate brands, Cardiac Services and Synapse Medical, from one legal entity — ask which brand a role, contract or enquiry actually sits under, since the two run separate websites, separate offices and (per Synapse Medical's own site) apparently separate headcount reporting. The board states plainly it does not track company-specific KPIs because Uniphar plc manages performance divisionally — ask what does get measured and reported locally, and to whom. Group-wide, Uniphar plc's Medtech division grew gross profit organically by 9.1% in 2024 even as this UK entity's turnover fell — ask how the UK business's plan fits against that group growth story, and whether investment decisions are made locally or centrally from Dublin.

deepDive.lede: The thing worth knowing before this interview: on 1 September 2024 the medical business stopped being a separate company. Essity UK Limited's own audited accounts for the year ended 31 December 2024 record that it "acquired the trade and certain assets of its sister company BSN Medical Limited" for £20,408,000, and that "All 82 employees of BSN Medical Limited at 31 August 2024 were transferred to Essity UK Limited". On the same day it took the net assets and trade of Essity Operations Manchester Limited for £42,766,000 and another 237 staff. The directors say why in their own words: the transactions "were executed to simplify the structure of Essity's business in the U.K., to integrate the medical business into the main trading company and processes of Essity in the U.K, and to reduce administrative costs." So the company a medical sales candidate would be employed by is a £899.1m turnover manufacturer of paper based hygiene products with a wound care, compression and continence business inside it, not a medtech firm. The second thing to know is the direction of travel. Revenue has now fallen two years running, from £957.0m (FY2022) to £918.5m (FY2023) to £899,141,000 (FY2024), and the directors are explicit that this is deliberate: "The profitability of the business has continued to improve as a result of the review of contracts, which has also led to a decrease in revenues." Gross margin went from 29.0% to 34.0% and operating profit from £42,480,000 to £67,956,000 across the same two years. The pressure is falling on the paper side, not the medical side: one paper machine shut at Oakenholt in January 2024, the Tawd paper mill closed in September 2024 and sold in September 2025, and two more paper converting lines announced for closure in October 2025 at a stated 2025 cost of £5,900,000. Nothing in the filings shows a Health & Medical revenue line, because note 3 states "All revenue is derived from one class of business", so the size of the medical business inside this £899m company is not on the public record and should be asked about directly.

The directors' own KPI table on page 3 puts gross margin at 34.0% (2023: 29.0%) and the pre-tax profit margin at 8.5% (2023: 5.4%).

The increase includes the 237 staff who transferred from Essity Operations Manchester Limited and the 82 from BSN Medical Limited on 1 September 2024, so it is not a like-for-like hiring figure.

This is a wholly owned subsidiary paying up to its parent, not a family business taking money out, and it says nothing about the health of any one product line.

prose: Eight years of revenue are on the public record for this company and they were read from four filings, not estimated. £729,692,000 (FY2017) and £757,662,000 (FY2018) from the accounts to 31 December 2018; £816,798,000 (FY2019) and £808,293,000 (FY2020) from the accounts to 31 December 2020, where the label on the line is Turnover; £813,986,000 (FY2021) and £956,997,000 (FY2022) from the accounts to 31 December 2022, where the label has changed to Revenue; and £918,535,000 (FY2023) and £899,141,000 (FY2024) from the accounts to 31 December 2024. The shape is a long flat run in the £730m to £820m band, one sharp 2022 spike to £957.0m on input cost inflation being passed through, and two years of managed decline since.

Profit does not track revenue here, and that is the point a candidate should carry into the room. Operating profit was £52,354,000 in FY2018, £82,922,000 in FY2020, then £14,626,000 in FY2022, the peak revenue year, and £67,956,000 in FY2024 on lower revenue than FY2022. The directors' own explanation for FY2024 is a contract review: "The profitability of the business has continued to improve as a result of the review of contracts, which has also led to a decrease in revenues, combined with decreases in raw material, energy and freight costs." Their KPI table separates out what the group charges the entity, disclosing operating profit adjusted for Essity group effects of £144,137,000 (2023: £132,477,000) after adding back £76,181,000 (2023: £89,997,000) of "Franchise fees and cost sharing charges from Essity group and internal mark ups excluded from Business unit performance". A rep should know that number exists: the business unit results the UK management team is measured on are not the statutory ones.

Two cautions on reading the series. First, the perimeter changed on 1 September 2024, when the trade of BSN Medical Limited and the whole of Essity Operations Manchester Limited came inside this entity, so FY2024 is not strictly comparable with what came before. The company supplies its own answer: the same KPI table gives FY2024 revenue "excluding business transfers" as £885,462,000, against the reported £899,141,000. Second, the geography has moved sharply. Note 3 splits FY2024 revenue as United Kingdom £897,000,000 and Rest of Europe £2,141,000, where FY2023 was £858,766,000 and £59,769,000. Rest of Europe revenue fell by roughly £57.6m in one year while UK revenue grew by roughly £38.2m. Nothing in the accounts explains that movement, and no explanation is invented here.

ownership: ESSITY UK LIMITED, company number 03226403, was incorporated on 12 July 1996 and is active. It has carried three names: SCA Hygiene UK Limited from incorporation to 10 July 1998, SCA Hygiene Products UK Limited to 2 January 2018, and ESSITY UK LIMITED since. Its registered SIC codes are 17120, manufacture of paper and paperboard, and 17220, manufacture of household and sanitary goods and of toilet requisites, which is why a search of Companies House by industry will not surface this company as a medical supplier. The registered office is Southfields Road, Dunstable, Bedfordshire LU6 3EJ. The directors' report describes the principal activity as "the manufacture, distribution and sale of paper based hygiene products", and the strategic report describes three business areas: Consumer Goods, Professional Hygiene and Health & Medical.

Note 24 of the FY2024 accounts sets out the chain in the company's own words: "The company is a subsidiary of Essity Group Holding BV, a company registered in the Netherlands. By virtue of their shareholding, the ultimate parent company and controlling party of the company is Essity Aktiebolag (publ), a company incorporated in Sweden. The immediate parent company is Essity Holding UK Limited, a company registered in England and Wales." Essity Aktiebolag (publ) prepares the only consolidated accounts. On the Companies House register, a PSC02 filed 18 July 2024 notified Essity Holding Uk Limited as a person with significant control, and a PSC07 the same day recorded the cessation of Kevin John Starr as a PSC. There is no UK-level consolidated turnover here: Essity UK Limited files as a single company under FRS 101.

The medical business arrived in this entity in stages and the dates matter. Essity acquired BSN medical in 2017, per Essity's own Our Journey page. BSN Medical Limited then continued as a separate UK company until 1 September 2024, when this company "acquired the trade and certain assets of its sister company BSN Medical Limited" for £20,408,000; because the parties are under common control, the £18,086,000 excess over book value (goodwill £2,117,000 and tangible fixed assets £205,000) went straight to equity rather than through the income statement. The same day it took the net assets and trade of Essity Operations Manchester Limited at book value, £42,766,000, and bought £1,735,000 of inventories from Essity Distribution B.V. The Essity Operations Manchester pension obligations had already transferred on 28 June 2024. The pension scheme is the SCA UK Pension Plan and a qualifying pension scheme indemnity is in force for its trustees. Auditors are Ernst & Young LLP, whose fee for auditing this company was £468,000 (2023: £302,000).

hiring: No vacancy list was read for this company in this session and none is claimed. What the accounts do give is the shape of the workforce, which is more useful than a job board snapshot: 425 of 1,451 average employees were in sales and marketing in FY2024, against 388 of 1,355 in FY2023, so the commercial population grew by 37 in a year when total headcount rose largely through two internal transfers. Recruitment for the UK business is run through Essity's group careers route on essity.com rather than a UK-specific site, and the UK and Republic of Ireland page carries "Working for Essity in the UK and ROI", "Our Teams and Locations" and "Careers" sections. Essity publishes UK gender pay gap reports for 2023, 2024 and 2025, a Modern Slavery Statement 2026, a UK tax strategy dated 26 February 2026 and a Carbon Reduction Plan for Essity UK Ltd, all linked from that page and all worth a look before an interview, because they are the documents an NHS procurement team reads.
marketPosition: The verifiable measure of this company's NHS position is its framework footprint: named supplier on 9 separate NHS Supply Chain frameworks, each confirmed against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch brief. They are Advanced Wound Care (2024/S 000-029271, 1 September 2025 to 31 August 2027, 56 suppliers), Disposable and Washable Continence Care and Associated Products (2026/S 000-031173, 24 August 2026 to 23 August 2028, 12 suppliers), General Wound Care (2025/S 000-028909, 24 June 2026 to 23 June 2028, 28 suppliers), Hand Hygiene and Associated Products and Services (2023/S 000-000335, 12 June 2023 to 11 June 2027, 21 suppliers), Orthotics, Podiatry and Immobilisation (2024/S 000-019205, 3 March 2025 to 2 March 2027, 63 suppliers), Paper Hygiene (ITT_766, 8 April 2024 to 7 April 2028, 17 suppliers), Vascular Therapy and Associated Products (2023/S 000-012286, 28 February 2024 to 27 February 2028, 23 suppliers), Wound Closure (2025/S 000-001071, 19 January 2026 to 18 January 2030, 39 suppliers) and Urology and Bowel Management (2023/S 000-011173, 21 February 2024 to 20 February 2027, 57 suppliers). Three were re-read directly on 27/08/2026 and the dates and supplier counts matched what this Hub already held. The earliest end date is Orthotics, Podiatry and Immobilisation on 2 March 2027, so nothing expires within the next six months.

One detail in those briefs is worth more than the count. NHS Supply Chain's Wound Closure brief, re-read on 27/08/2026, still names the supplier as "BSN Medical Ltd", while the General Wound Care and Continence Care briefs name "Essity UK Ltd". The trade of BSN Medical Limited transferred into Essity UK Limited on 1 September 2024, so both names on NHS Supply Chain point at the same trading entity today. A rep who has only read one brief will have half the company's framework list, and a customer looking up "BSN Medical" in the catalogue is looking at Essity.

The same split runs through the catalogue. This Hub's NHS Supply Chain catalogue cache holds 74 distinct National Product Codes for this company across Leukomed, Leukoplast, Cutimed, Cutimed Sorbact, Cutimed Alginate, Comprilan, Actimove, Delta-Cast and the TENA continence ranges, and the catalogue files them under two supplier labels, "ESSITY UK TENA HM" and "ESSITY UK LIMITED HDS". Neither matches the registered name and neither matches the other. Essity's own UK and Republic of Ireland page describes the medical offer in its own words: "Health & Medical Solutions offers the global TENA brand to care homes, hospitals and other healthcare professionals. We are a global leader in the worldwide healthcare market, specialising in Compression Therapy, Wound Care and Orthopaedics. Our brands include Actimove, Cutimed, Delta-Cast, JOBST, and Leukoplast." That is the company's claim about itself, read on 27/08/2026, and it is published here as such and not as a finding.

No market share is given here and none is calculable, and no revenue split by business area exists to give one: note 3 of the FY2024 accounts states "All revenue is derived from one class of business", so there is no Health & Medical line in the statutory numbers. What can be said is that the medical business sits inside a company whose statutory activity is paper based hygiene products, whose cost pressure and site closures are all on the paper side, and whose UK revenue grew £38.2m in FY2024 while Rest of Europe revenue fell £57.6m. Note also that Essity's global structure names four business areas (Health & Medical Solutions, Personal Care, Consumer Tissue and Professional Hygiene) while this UK entity's own strategic report names three (Consumer Goods, Professional Hygiene and Health & Medical). Do not treat the two lists as the same thing.

There is no own-site product crawl for this supplier and the reason is worth recording. The Hub's crawler refused medical.essity.co.uk on 26/08/2026 because "the sitemap carries 0 product URLs". Checked directly on 27/08/2026, that domain no longer serves a site at all: both medical.essity.co.uk and essity.co.uk now redirect to https://www.essity.com/company/essity-in-the-world/uk-roi/, a corporate page with no catalogue. The catalogue is alive, on separate brand hosts, each returning HTTP 200 on 27/08/2026: tena.co.uk (with a dedicated /professionals section), jobst.co.uk, leukoplast.com, cutimed.com, actimove.com and delta-cast.com. This is the known one-domain-per-supplier limit, not evidence the company has no products.

deepDive.interview: Read the FY2024 accounts before you go in, because the single most important fact about this employer is in them and is not on any website: the medical business became part of Essity UK Limited on 1 September 2024, taking 82 BSN Medical staff with it, and the directors say the purpose was "to integrate the medical business into the main trading company and processes of Essity in the U.K, and to reduce administrative costs." Three questions fall out of that and none is hostile. First, integration: two years on, is Health & Medical run as a distinct commercial unit inside a paper business, or has it been absorbed into shared processes? The answer shapes what a sales role actually looks like day to day. Second, the numbers you are measured on: the KPI table adds back £76,181,000 of "Franchise fees and cost sharing charges from Essity group and internal mark ups excluded from Business unit performance", so ask which set of numbers the UK Health & Medical business unit is judged on, because it plainly is not the statutory ones. Third, revenue direction: revenue has fallen two years running while profit has risen, and the directors call that a contract review; ask whether that review has touched NHS Supply Chain lines, or only the consumer and professional side. Two pieces of live context to carry in. The Disposable and Washable Continence Care and Associated Products framework started on 24 August 2026 with only 12 named suppliers, which means trust-level implementation work is happening right now on a very short supplier list. And the pressure in this company is on paper, not medical: two converting lines were announced for closure in October 2025 at a stated £5,900,000 cost, in the Consumer Goods unit. Finally, know the naming. The company is Essity UK Limited, 03226403, registered SIC codes for paper and sanitary goods. NHS Supply Chain still names it "BSN Medical Ltd" on the Wound Closure brief and the catalogue lists it as "ESSITY UK TENA HM" and "ESSITY UK LIMITED HDS". Knowing which name a given customer sees is a genuinely useful thing to walk in with.
